definition_zh: 挖掘机；挖掘者；考古发掘人员；牙科挖除器械
definition_en: a machine or person that digs out earth or buried material, or a dental instrument for hollowing a cavity
core_image: 一台履带机器把斗臂伸进土坑，铲斗落下，旁边一名工人举着标杆示意深度
scene: 雨后的工地上，一台履带机器把斗臂伸进坑里，铲斗每次落下都带起湿土，测量员在旁举着标杆。 The excavator, a machine with a steel bucket, cut a trench beside the road before the pipes arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 excavator 指「用于开挖土方的机械」（第 1 个义项：以铲斗挖掘的工程机械）；句意为这台挖掘机在管道运到之前就在路边挖好了一条沟。可辨识物件：履带、斗臂、铲斗、湿土、测量标杆。

pos.zh: 挖掘机；挖掘者；牙科挖器（可数，复数 excavators）

senses.title: A digging machine
senses.definition: a powered machine with a bucket or scoop used to move earth and rock
senses.definitionCN: 带铲斗或勺斗、用于移动土石的动力机械
senses.example: The excavator cut a trench beside the road before the pipes arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 这台挖掘机在管道运到之前就在路边挖好了一条沟。
senses.why: excavate plus -or names the agent; when the agent is a machine, the suffix covers it as naturally as a person.
senses.whyCN: excavate 加 -or 命名施动者；当施动者是机器时，这个后缀同样自然涵盖它。

senses.title: The operator of such a machine
senses.definition: a person trained to run an excavating machine
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、操作挖掘机械的人
senses.example: The excavator signalled the truck to move forward.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘机操作员示意卡车向前移动。
senses.why: English often uses the machine name for the person who runs it, by metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用机器名称指操作它的人，这是转喻。

senses.title: An archaeological digger
senses.definition: a person who excavates a site, especially in a professional team
senses.definitionCN: 发掘遗址的人，尤指专业团队中的成员
senses.example: The excavator kept a notebook beside the trench.
senses.exampleCN: 这位发掘者在探沟旁放着一本笔记。
senses.why: the older personal sense survives in archaeology, where the tool is often small and the hand is human.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的人物义在考古学中保留下来，因为那里的工具常很小，施动的是人手。

senses.title: A type of machine
senses.definition: a class such as tracked, wheeled, backhoe or bucket-wheel excavator
senses.definitionCN: 履带式、轮式、反铲式或斗轮式等类别
senses.example: A bucket-wheel excavator can move a trainload of earth in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一台斗轮式挖掘机一小时能搬走一列车那么重的土。
senses.why: machines are classified by undercarriage and bucket, and the noun takes those modifiers.
senses.whyCN: 机械按底盘与铲斗分类，这个名词可带这些修饰语。

senses.title: The plant or contractor in engineering
senses.titleCN: 工程中的机械或承包方
senses.definition: the machine fleet or contractor responsible for excavation on a project
senses.definitionCN: 项目中负责开挖的机械队或承包方
senses.example: The excavator was booked for the whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘机被订了整整一周。
senses.why: in project speech, the machine stands for the service it performs.
senses.whyCN: 在项目口语中，机器代指它提供的服务。

senses.title: A dental excavator
senses.definition: a small hand instrument used to remove decayed tissue from a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 用于挖除牙体腐坏组织的小型手用器械
senses.example: The dentist chose a small excavator for the edge of the cavity.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医选了一把小挖器处理龋洞边缘。
senses.why: dentistry keeps the literal sense at a tiny scale: a hand tool that hollows.
senses.whyCN: 牙科在极小尺度保留字面义：一把挖空的手用工具。

senses.title: Metaphor: a person who digs out truth
senses.definition: by extension, someone who searches persistently through records or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 引申指持续翻查记录或证据的人
senses.example: The archivist was the excavator of the vanished company.
senses.exampleCN: 这位档案员是那家消失公司的「挖掘者」。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the agent role: someone operates the tool that removes layers.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留施动角色：有人操作移除层层的工具。

senses.title: Abstraction: a tool that reveals what is buried
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：使埋藏之物显现的工具
senses.definition: any instrument or method by which covered material is brought into view
senses.definitionCN: 任何使被覆盖材料显现的工具或方法
senses.example: A good question is an excavator for a silent room.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好问题是对沉默房间的「挖掘机」。
senses.why: the deepest sense separates the tool from its material: whatever removes cover can be called an excavator.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层把工具与材料分开：任何移除覆盖之物都可称为挖掘器。

intro.en: Excavator is excavate plus the Latin agent suffix -or. The machine sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavator 是 excavate 加拉丁施动后缀 -or；机器义出现在十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Excavare meant 'to hollow out, dig out', from ex- 'out' and cavare 'to make hollow'.
items.cn: excavare 意为「挖空、挖出」，来自 ex-「出」与 cavare「使空」。

items.en: Latin -or named the person who performs an action; English keeps it in agent nouns such as actor and creator.
items.cn: 拉丁 -or 命名实施动作的人；英语在 actor、creator 等施动名词中保留它。

items.en: A Latin agent noun excavator exists mainly as a formed pattern rather than a common classical word, so English excavator is best treated as an English formation on Latin pieces.
items.cn: 拉丁施动名词 excavator 主要作为一种构词模式存在，并非古典时期的常用词，因此英语 excavator 宜视为用拉丁成分构成的英语词。

items.en: Steam shovels and dredgers in the nineteenth century gave the agent noun a mechanical referent, and the machine sense now dominates.
items.cn: 十九世纪的蒸汽铲与挖泥船使这个施动名词获得机械所指，机器义如今占主导。

items.en: The older personal sense survives for archaeologists, and dentistry uses the same word for a small hand tool.
items.cn: 较古老的人物义在考古学家身上保留，牙科则用同一个词指小型手用工具。

items.en: Source uncertain (first machine use and Latin status): the exact date of the machine sense is not fixed, and the classical standing of Latin excavator is doubtful.
items.cn: 来源不确定（机器义首见与拉丁语地位）：机器义的确切年代无定论，拉丁 excavator 在古典时期的地位可疑。

note.en: Group one holds digger words easily confused with excavator; group two holds neighbouring machines and roles.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavator 混淆的挖掘类词；第二组是邻近的机械与角色。

entries.definition: The process or hole of digging; excavator names the machine or person that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖掘过程或坑；excavator 指做这件事的机器或人。

entries.definition: To dig out; the agent noun adds the doer to the action.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖出；施动名词在动作之外加上施动者。

entries.definition: A person or machine that digs; it is less technical and does not specify a bucket arm.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖掘的人或机器；较少技术性，不特指斗臂机械。

entries.definition: A machine that removes mud from the seabed or a river; the medium differs from dry excavation.
entries.definitionCN: 指从海床或河底取泥的机械；介质不同于干地开挖。

entries.definition: An excavating arm mounted on a tractor, digging toward itself; it is a kind of excavator.
entries.definitionCN: 指装在拖拉机上的反铲臂，向自身方向挖；是挖掘机的一种。

entries.definition: A machine with a blade that pushes soil; it moves material forward rather than lifting it.
entries.definitionCN: 指用推土铲推土的机械；把材料向前推，而非铲起。

entries.definition: Any large machine for moving soil; excavator is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何搬运土方的大型机械；挖掘机是其中一员。

entries.definition: Anyone who runs a machine; it does not specify the machine as excavator does.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人，泛称；不像 excavator 那样标明机器种类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the verb plus -or, the machine family and the small dental tool.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：动词加 -or、机械词族，以及那把小型牙科器械。

normal.en: excavate + -or: the one that digs.
normal.cn: excavate + -or：挖掘的那一个。

normal.en: -or is the Latin agent ending also seen in actor, creator and inspector.
normal.cn: -or 是拉丁施动词尾，也见于 actor、creator 与 inspector。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: The machine sense is nineteenth-century, when steam shovels replaced hand gangs.
normal.cn: 机器义出现在十九世纪，当时蒸汽铲取代了人工队。

normal.en: Dentistry keeps a tiny excavator for a tiny hollow.
normal.cn: 牙科保留一把小挖器，用于小小的空腔。

abstract.en: Picture a steel arm that reaches into the ground like a hand into a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一条钢臂伸进地里，像手伸进抽屉。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket that brings up one layer at a time and never takes two at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个铲斗一次只带起一层，从不同时取两层。

abstract.en: Picture a tool that is judged by what it uncovers, not by what it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一件工具，评价它的是它揭开了什么，而不是它搬走了什么。

examples.en: The excavator was too heavy for the narrow street.
examples.cn: 这台挖掘机太重，进不了这条窄街。

examples.en: An excavator operator must watch for buried cables.
examples.cn: 挖掘机操作员必须留意地下电缆。

examples.en: The dental excavator removed the softened dentine.
examples.cn: 牙科挖器去除了软化的牙本质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excavate（挖）+ or（东西/人）」——负责挖的那台机器或那个人 → 挖掘机；发掘者

root: excavate 加拉丁施动后缀 -or；excavate 由 excavation 逆构，源自拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one agent: the thing or person that digs. The agent becomes a machine, its operator, an archaeological digger, a machine type, a hired plant, a dental tool, a metaphor for an investigator and finally any instrument that reveals what is buried.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个施动者展开：挖的那台东西或那个人。这个施动者先成为机器，再成为操作员、考古发掘者、机械类型、租用的机械、牙科工具、调查者的比喻，最后成为任何使埋藏物显现的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tracked machine reaching its boom into a pit, the bucket biting wet soil, a surveyor's rod beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：履带机器把斗臂伸进坑里，铲斗咬住湿土，旁边立着测量标杆。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND ITS KINDS: one agent, many undercarriages and buckets.
branches.cn: 机器及其种类：同一个施动者，多种底盘与铲斗。

branches.en: THE HUMAN HAND: the operator and the archaeological digger share the name.
branches.cn: 人手：操作员与考古发掘者共用这个名称。

branches.en: THE SERVICE AND THE SMALL TOOL: a hired plant and a dental instrument both act on material.
branches.cn: 服务与小工具：租用的机械与牙科器械都作用于材料。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: an investigator becomes the one who removes layers.
branches.cn: 比喻：调查者成为移除层层的人。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the deepest sense is any tool that brings buried things into view.
branches.cn: 工具：最深的一层是任何使埋藏物显现的器具。

intro.en: Excavator is a verb plus the Latin agent suffix -or, so it reads as 'the one that digs'.
intro.cn: excavator 是动词加拉丁施动后缀 -or，因此可读作「挖掘的那一个」。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavare and excavare give excavate and excavation; the agent ending -or also builds actor, creator and inspector.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavare 与 excavare 衍生 excavate 与 excavation；施动词尾 -or 也构成 actor、creator 与 inspector。

items.example: The crew excavate the site in summer.
items.exampleCN: 施工队在夏天开挖场地。

items.meaning: one who or that which acts
items.example: The suffix turns an action into an agent.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成施动者。

items.example: The excavator lifted the bucket.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机提起铲斗。

items.example: The excavation lasted all summer.
items.exampleCN: 发掘持续了整个夏天。

items.example: The root describes the space made.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描述造出的空间。

items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the agent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供施动背后的动作。

items.example: The cavity was small but deep.
items.exampleCN: 这个洞小而深。

items.meaning: an excavating arm on a tractor
items.example: The backhoe dug close to the wall.
items.exampleCN: 反铲贴着墙挖。

items.meaning: a machine that removes mud from water
items.example: The dredger cleared the channel.
items.exampleCN: 挖泥船清理了航道。

latinEntries.structure: cavus, cava, cavum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 学费（按学期或学年收取的教学费用）
definition_en: the sum of money charged by a school or college for teaching, usually billed by term or by year
core_image: 餐桌上摊开的缴费通知单：一行是课时，一行是金额，旁边放着一台计算器
scene: 缴费通知单摊在餐桌上，旁边放着计算器和分期付款的说明，家长一行行核对数字，孩子站在门口不敢出声。 The tuition fee for the program includes laboratory costs.
sceneCN: 这里指「学费」（第 1 个义项：学校按学期或学年收取的教学费用）；句意为该项目的学费包含实验室费用。图中可辨识物件：缴费通知单、计算器、分期说明、餐桌。

pos.zh: 学费（可数，指一笔按学期或学年计的费用）

senses.title: The annual charge for a degree
senses.titleCN: 按学年收取的学位学费
senses.definition: the yearly sum a college charges a student for instruction
senses.definitionCN: 学院每学年向学生收取的教学费用
senses.example: The tuition fee for the program includes laboratory costs.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目的学费包含实验室费用。
senses.why: the phrase makes explicit what the bare word leaves open: which charge, billed how often.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把单用词没说明的部分讲清：是哪一笔钱、按什么周期收。

senses.title: The charge for one course
senses.definition: the amount billed for a particular course or module
senses.definitionCN: 为某门课程或模块计收的金额
senses.example: The tuition fee for the summer module is billed separately.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季模块的学费单独计收。
senses.why: billing splits one module from the rest, so the phrase narrows to a single line on the statement.
senses.whyCN: 计费把一门模块从其余部分拆开，短语就收窄为账单上的一行。

senses.title: The higher charge for overseas students
senses.definition: the larger sum charged to students from outside the home country
senses.definitionCN: 向来自境外的学生收取的更高费用
senses.example: Overseas students pay a tuition fee nearly twice the local rate.
senses.exampleCN: 国际学生缴的学费接近本地标准的两倍。
senses.why: a different payer is charged a different rate, so the phrase carries the student's identity as well as the sum.
senses.whyCN: 不同的付费方适用不同费率，因此短语同时带上学生身份与金额。

senses.title: The charge at a private school
senses.definition: the sum charged by a fee-paying rather than a state-funded school
senses.definitionCN: 由自费学校而非公立学校收取的费用
senses.example: The boarding tuition fee covers meals and lodging.
senses.exampleCN: 寄宿学费包含餐食与住宿。
senses.why: the funding source changes the bill, so a fee-paying school needs its own label for the same charge.
senses.whyCN: 经费来源改变账单，因此自费学校对同一笔收费需要自己的说法。

senses.title: An add-on charge
senses.titleCN: 学费附加费（实验、材料等）
senses.definition: an extra charge added to the basic fee for materials or facilities
senses.definitionCN: 在基本学费之外为材料或设施加收的费用
senses.example: A small tuition fee covers the art supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔小额学费附加费覆盖美术耗材。
senses.why: materials and facilities generate charges beyond instruction, and the phrase extends to cover them.
senses.whyCN: 材料与设施产生教学之外的收费，短语随之扩展覆盖这些项目。

senses.title: The amount left after aid
senses.titleCN: 扣除补助后的应付学费
senses.definition: the net sum a student owes after scholarships or grants are applied
senses.definitionCN: 奖学金或补助抵扣之后学生实际应付的净额
senses.example: After the grant, the tuition fee fell to a few hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 补助之后，学费降到几百。
senses.why: scholarships reduce the amount owed, so the phrase can name the net figure rather than the list price.
senses.whyCN: 奖学金减少应付额，因此短语可以指名净额，而非价目表上的数。

senses.title: The four-year total
senses.definition: the whole sum billed across a full course of study
senses.definitionCN: 整段学业期间计收的总额
senses.example: They saved for the tuition fee years before he applied.
senses.exampleCN: 在他申请之前很多年，他们就为这笔学费存钱。
senses.why: the same annual charge multiplied across the years becomes a single figure families plan around.
senses.whyCN: 同一笔年度收费乘以年数，变成家庭据以规划的一个数字。

senses.title: The economic price of an education
senses.titleCN: 比喻：受教育的经济代价
senses.definition: the total economic cost of gaining an education, including what is given up
senses.definitionCN: 获得教育所付出的经济总代价，包括放弃的收入
senses.example: The tuition fee of that year abroad was paid in missed promotions.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年海外求学的学费，是用错过的晋升换来的。
senses.why: the money image is borrowed, so what is paid can be income given up rather than cash.
senses.whyCN: 货币意象被借用，因此付出的可以是放弃的收入，而不只是现金。

intro.en: Tuition fee pairs a Latin word for guardianship turned instruction with an Old English word for payment.
intro.cn: 这个短语把由「监护」转为「教导」的拉丁词，与一个表示付款的英语本族词配在一起。

items.en: Tueri 'to guard' gave tuitio, a watching over, which English took as tuition.
items.cn: tueri「守护」派生出 tuitio「看护」，英语把它借作 tuition。

items.en: English tuition first meant guardianship, then instruction, and in American usage the price of instruction.
items.cn: 英语 tuition 先指监护，再指教导，在美式用法里又指教导的价钱。

items.en: Feoh meant cattle, then money and property, since livestock was the earliest measure of wealth.
items.cn: feoh 原指牛群，后指钱财与财产，因为牲畜是最早的财富尺度。

items.en: Fee narrowed from property in general to a payment for a right, an office or a service.
items.cn: fee 从泛指财产收窄为为权利、职位或服务支付的款项。

items.en: Billing practice joined the two so that the service and the charge were named in one phrase.
items.cn: 计费实务把两者连起来，使服务与收费在一个短语里同时说清。

items.en: Dating note: the compound's first billing use is approximate, and the exact period when it replaced the bare word in American catalogues is not recorded.
items.cn: 年代说明：该短语最早用于计费的年代只是约数；它在美国院校收费表中取代单用词的确切时期没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds the two parts of the phrase and their close forms; group two holds other money words for study.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两个组成部分及其近形；第二组是其他表示求学花费的词。

entries.definition: Without the second word it can mean teaching or the charge; the phrase removes that ambiguity.
entries.definitionCN: 不带后一个词时，它可指教学也可指收费；短语消除了这层歧义。

entries.definition: A charge for a service; it is the countable payment, not the whole cost of study.
entries.definitionCN: 为服务收取的费用；是可数的一笔付款，不是求学总成本。

entries.definition: The plural usually covers several charges at once, of which tuition is only one.
entries.definitionCN: 复数常指同时收取的多项费用，学费只是其中一项。

entries.definition: An adjective for a school or pupil that pays rather than being state-funded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容自费而非公立的学校或学生。

entries.definition: The whole cost of instruction, often including housing and books in journalism.
entries.definitionCN: 教学的总开支，新闻写作中常含住宿与书本。

entries.definition: The sum a provider demands for a service; broader than a school fee.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供方要求的金额；比学校费用更宽。

entries.definition: A charge imposed by an authority; it suggests obligation rather than a price list.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威机构征收的费用；暗示义务而非价目表。

entries.definition: Awarded money that reduces what must be paid; it is the opposite direction of the same flow.
entries.definitionCN: 颁发的资助，用来减少应付金额；是同一资金流中的反向项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real billing words, real catalogue phrases and real kitchen tables.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实计费词汇、真实收费表说法与真实的餐桌场景。

normal.en: One part names the teaching, the other names the payment: the phrase is simply the two halves pushed together.
normal.cn: 一半指教学，一半指付款：短语就是把两半推到一起。

normal.en: Without the second half the first word can mean either teaching or its price.
normal.cn: 没有后一半时，前一个词既可指教学，也可指价钱。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: pay the tuition fee, tuition fee waiver, annual tuition fee.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：缴学费、学费减免、年度学费。

normal.en: The payment word came from cattle, the oldest form of wealth.
normal.cn: 表示付款的那个词来自牛群，即最古老的财富形式。

normal.en: Bills arrive by term or by year, which is why the phrase is countable.
normal.cn: 账单按学期或按年到来，因此这个短语可数。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded into a school brochure.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折进学校宣传册里。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a turnstile priced per term rather than per visit.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闸机按学期而非按次收费。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger line that names both the lesson and the loss.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上的一行，同时写着课程与损失。

examples.en: The tuition fee for the program includes laboratory costs.
examples.cn: 该项目的学费包含实验室费用。

examples.en: Overseas students pay a tuition fee nearly twice the local rate.
examples.cn: 国际学生缴的学费接近本地标准的两倍。

examples.en: After the grant, the tuition fee fell to a few hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 补助之后，学费降到了几百美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「教学」加「付款」：为教学付的那笔钱 → 学费

root: 短语由 tuition 与 fee 合成；tuition 出自拉丁 tuitio「看护」，后引申为教导及其价款；fee 源自古英语 feoh「牛群、钱财」，后收窄为为权利或服务支付的款项。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses take one bill and change its size and scope: a year, a course, an overseas rate, a private school, an add-on, a net figure, a four-year total, and finally the whole economic price of learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一张账单在改变大小与范围：一学年、一门课、海外费率、私立学校、附加费、净额、四年总额，最后是求学的整体经济代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bill on a kitchen table with a calculator beside it and a payment plan underneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：餐桌上的一张账单，旁边放着计算器，下面压着分期说明。

branches.en: THE CORE AND THE TOTAL: one year's charge, then the same charge summed across four years.
branches.cn: 核心与总额：先是一学年的收费，再把同学年的收费累成四年。

branches.en: UNIT AND EXTRAS: a single course billed apart, and charges added for materials.
branches.cn: 单元与附加：单门课单独计费，以及为材料加收的费用。

branches.en: DIFFERENT PAYERS: the overseas rate and the private-school rate.
branches.cn: 不同的付费方：海外费率与私立学校费率。

branches.en: AFTER AID: the net figure once scholarships are applied.
branches.cn: 补助之后：奖学金抵扣后的净额。

branches.en: BORROWED PRICE: the whole cost of learning, paid partly in opportunities missed.
branches.cn: 借用的价钱：求学的整体代价，部分以错失的机会支付。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived word for teaching to a native English word for payment; each half still builds its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「教学」词与英语本族的「付款」词连接起来，两半各自仍能构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tueri 'to guard' gives tuition, tutor and tutelage; Old English feoh 'cattle, money' gives fee and feudal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tueri「守护」衍生出 tuition、tutor 与 tutelage；古英语 feoh「牛群、钱财」衍生出 fee 与 feudal。

items.meaning: teaching, or the charge for it
items.meaningCN: 教学，或为教学支付的费用
items.example: Tuition rose with the new laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 随着新实验室建成，学费上涨。

items.structure: fee (noun, from Old English feoh 'cattle, money')
items.meaning: a payment for a right or service
items.meaningCN: 为权利或服务支付的款项
items.example: The fee covers the examination.
items.exampleCN: 这笔费用覆盖考试。

items.example: The tuition fee is due in two parts.
items.exampleCN: 学费分两期缴纳。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The ending makes a noun of the guarding verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把守护的动词变成名词。

items.meaning: one who teaches a small group
items.example: Her tutor corrected the essay.
items.exampleCN: 她的导师修改了这篇文章。

items.example: Tutorials are held on Fridays.
items.exampleCN: 辅导课在周五进行。

items.example: A fee-paying school charged more.
items.exampleCN: 一所自费学校收费更高。

items.example: Fees include tuition and lodging.
items.exampleCN: 费用包括学费与住宿。

latinEntries.structure: feudal (adjective, from feoh via Medieval Latin feodum)
latinEntries.meaning: holding land in return for service

definition_zh: n. 大洞穴，岩洞
definition_en: a very large cave, often with an opening in a hillside
core_image: 巨大的岩洞深处落下一滴水
scene: 洞口幽深，走进大洞穴后，只听见水滴落下的回声。 Deep inside the cavern they could hear only dripping water.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cavern 指大洞穴；句意是进入洞中只听到水滴回响。

pos.zh: 大洞穴，岩洞

senses.title: The large cave
senses.definition: a large cave, especially a hollow in rock
senses.definitionCN: 尤指岩石中的巨大空洞
senses.example: The cavern echoed with every step.
senses.exampleCN: 每走一步，洞穴都在回响。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin caverna, a hollow.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 caverna（空洞）。

senses.title: A hollow space
senses.definition: any deep enclosed hollow
senses.definitionCN: 任何深邃封闭的空腔
senses.example: The cellar felt like a cavern.
senses.exampleCN: 地窖像一个大洞穴。
senses.why: The sense widened to any echoing empty space.
senses.whyCN: 词义扩展到任何有回声的空旷处。

intro.en: Cavern comes from Latin caverna, a hollow, from cavus, empty.
intro.cn: cavern 源自拉丁语 caverna（空洞），来自 cavus（空的）。

items.en: Latin cavus means hollow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cavus 意为空心的。

items.en: Caverna names a hollow place.
items.cn: caverna 指空洞之处。

items.en: English cavern names a large cave.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语指大洞穴。

items.en: Geologists study cavern formation.
items.cn: 十七世纪地质学者研究洞穴形成。

items.en: Any echoing hollow can feel like a cavern.
items.cn: 现代任何有回声的空处都像洞穴。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cav- opening; the near-meaning group ranks hollows in rock.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cav- 开头；近义组排列岩石中的空腔。

entries.definition: A hollow space inside something.
entries.definitionCN: 空腔。

entries.definition: A natural hollow in rock.
entries.definitionCN: 洞穴。

entries.definition: An old word for an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 小酒馆。

entries.definition: A small picturesque cave.
entries.definitionCN: 岩洞。

entries.definition: A hole or empty space.
entries.definitionCN: 凹处。

entries.definition: A deep open crack in the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 深壑。

normalIntro.en: A cavern is a cave large enough to have its own weather.
normalIntro.cn: cavern 是大得能拥有自己气候的洞穴。

normal.en: Cavus means hollow.
normal.cn: cavus 意为空心的。

normal.en: A caverna is a hollow place.
normal.cn: caverna 是空洞之处。

normal.en: A cavern dwarfs a person.
normal.cn: 人站在大洞穴里显得很小。

normal.en: Every sound returns as an echo.
normal.cn: 每个声音都变成回声。

normal.en: The word can describe any vast hollow.
normal.cn: 这个词能形容任何巨大空腔。

abstract.en: A room built by water.
abstract.cn: 水建造的房间。

abstract.en: Darkness with a ceiling.
abstract.cn: 有天花板的一片黑暗。

abstract.en: A stone throat swallowing sound.
abstract.cn: 吞下声音的石头喉咙。

examples.en: The narrow path opened into a huge cavern.
examples.cn: 狭窄的小路通向一个巨大的洞穴。

examples.en: Caverns form slowly as water dissolves limestone.
examples.cn: 水溶解石灰岩，洞穴慢慢形成。

examples.en: His voice filled the cavern and came back doubled.
examples.cn: 他的声音充满洞穴，又叠着回声返回。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开汶」——岩石开出一个很大的空洞。

root: 拉丁语 cavus（空的）→ caverna（空洞）→ 英语 cavern

sensesIntro.en: A cave becomes a cavern when its emptiness has its own echo.
sensesIntro.cn: 当空洞有了自己的回声，岩洞就成了大洞穴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dropped stone falling far before it sounds
core.cn: 核心意象：落石很久之后才传来回响

branches.en: A mouth of stone above the trees.
branches.cn: 树顶上方的一张石头大口。

branches.en: Limestone slowly eaten hollow.
branches.cn: 被慢慢蚀空的石灰岩。

branches.en: A cellar that feels too large.
branches.cn: 显得过于空旷的地窖。

branches.en: An empty hall returning footsteps.
branches.cn: 把脚步送回的空大厅。

branches.en: Space measured by echo.
branches.cn: 用回声丈量的空间。

definition_zh: 海藻；海草（生长在海里的大型藻类，也指采作食物或原料的海藻）
definition_en: large algae that grow in the sea, especially when gathered as food or raw material
core_image: 退潮后的礁石上挂着一片片湿滑的褐绿色长带，随残余的水流来回摆动
scene: 退潮后，渔妇蹲在湿滑的礁石上，用镰刀割下一长条褐绿色的海藻，抖了抖水放进竹篮。 At low tide she cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock and shook it into her basket.
sceneCN: 这里 seaweed 指「长在海里的大型藻类，可采集的海藻」（第 2 个义项：作为采集物或食材的海藻）；句意为退潮时她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻，抖掉水放进篮子。

pos.zh: 海藻；海草（大型海生藻类）
可食用的海藻；海藻制品

derivatives.zh: 带海藻味的；长满海藻的
海藻床（成片生长的海藻区）

senses.title: Marine algae growing in the sea
senses.definition: large algae that grow attached to rocks or the seabed in salt water
senses.definitionCN: 附着在礁石或海底生长的大型海生藻类
senses.example: Seaweed covered the rocks below the tide line.
senses.exampleCN: 潮线以下的礁石上覆满了海藻。
senses.why: The compound simply says 'a weed of the sea': sea names the place, weed names a plant-like growth, and the pair covers whatever grows there in sheets.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词字面就是「海里的草」：sea 标地点，weed 标像植物的生长物，合起来泛指成片长在那里的东西。

senses.title: Seaweed gathered as food
senses.definition: seaweed harvested and prepared for eating, fresh or dried
senses.definitionCN: 采收后新鲜或干燥食用的大型海藻
senses.example: She cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻。
senses.why: Once people gather it deliberately, the word shifts from the plant in the sea to the crop in the basket.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们有意采集，这个词就从「海里的植物」转为「篮子里的收成」。

senses.title: Raw material for industry
senses.definition: seaweed processed to extract gums, minerals or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 经加工以提取胶质、矿物质或化学品的海藻
senses.example: Brown seaweed is processed for alginate used in food and medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 褐藻被加工成用于食品与医药的褐藻胶。
senses.why: The same harvest feeds factories, so the word also names a bulk material rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 同样的收成也供给工厂，因此这个词也指大宗原料，而不只是植物。

senses.title: Fertiliser spread on fields
senses.definition: seaweed used as mulch or soil improver on farmland
senses.definitionCN: 用作覆盖物或土壤改良剂的海藻
senses.example: Crofters spread seaweed on the potato beds each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 佃农每年春天把海藻铺在土豆地里。
senses.why: Coastal farming long used what the tide delivered, so seaweed became a word for free fertiliser.
senses.whyCN: 沿海农业长期利用潮水送来的东西，于是 seaweed 也成了「免费的肥料」。

senses.title: Weed cast up on the shore
senses.titleCN: 被浪冲上岸的腐烂海藻
senses.definition: seaweed washed ashore and left to rot along the high-water line
senses.definitionCN: 被冲上岸、在高潮线一带腐烂的海藻
senses.example: Flies rose from the seaweed at the high-water mark.
senses.exampleCN: 高潮线处的海藻上飞起一群苍蝇。
senses.why: Here the plant is dead and stranded; the word follows the material wherever the tide leaves it.
senses.whyCN: 此时植物已死并被搁浅，这个词跟着物质走，潮水把它留在哪里就指哪里。

senses.title: Underwater forest and habitat
senses.titleCN: 海藻林与其中的栖息地
senses.definition: a dense stand of large seaweed that shelters fish and invertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 为鱼类与无脊椎动物提供遮蔽的密集大型海藻群落
senses.example: Kelp, the tallest seaweed, forms forests along cold coasts.
senses.exampleCN: 海带是最高的海藻，在寒冷海岸形成森林。
senses.why: Ecology treats the mass as habitat, so seaweed names a place as well as a plant.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这一大片视为栖息地，因此 seaweed 既指植物也指地点。

senses.title: A sheet used to wrap food
senses.definition: a thin dried sheet of seaweed used to wrap rice or fillings
senses.definitionCN: 用来包米饭或馅料的干燥海藻薄片
senses.example: She wrapped the rice in a sheet of seaweed.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一片海藻把米饭卷起来。
senses.why: Cuisine turns the plant into a countable sheet, and the word follows the product's new shape.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪把植物变成可数的薄片，词义随之跟到成品的新形态上。

senses.title: A tangled mass, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：纠缠成团的一大堆
senses.definition: a dense, disordered tangle that resembles seaweed in a harbour
senses.definitionCN: 像港里海藻那样密集而杂乱的一团东西
senses.example: A seaweed of old rope and nets clogged the repair shed.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆旧绳索和渔网像海藻一样缠塞了修理棚。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps only the shape of the mass: something long, wet and hopelessly entangled.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义只保留「一团」的形态：长长的、湿的、缠得解不开。

intro.en: Seaweed is a native English compound of sea and weed, not a borrowing; its two halves are both Old English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seaweed 是英语本族复合词，由 sea 与 weed 组成，并非外来借词；两半都来自古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sǣ meant 'sea, lake, sheet of water' and survives in sea, as well as in compounds such as sea-bird and sea-wall.
items.cn: sǣ 意为「海、湖、大片水域」，留存为 sea，也见于 sea-bird、sea-wall 等复合词。

items.en: Wēod meant 'herb, grass, plant', with no hint of nuisance; the modern sense 'unwanted plant' developed later.
items.cn: wēod 意为「草、植物」，本无「有害」之意；现代「杂草」义是后来才发展出来的。

items.en: The compound sea + weed is recorded in the sixteenth century for plants of the sea; the exact first citation is not settled, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: sea + weed 的复合形式在 16 世纪有记录，指海中的植物；确切的最早书证尚无定论，因此年代为约数。

items.en: Modern botany limits seaweed to large algae; seagrasses are flowering plants and are therefore not seaweeds, a distinction everyday use often ignores.
items.cn: 现代植物学把 seaweed 限制为大型藻类；海草是开花植物，因此不算海藻，但日常用法常忽略这一区别。

items.en: From the nineteenth century seaweed was harvested for iodine and potash, and later for alginates, food and feed.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，海藻被采收用于制碘与钾碱，后来又用于褐藻胶、食品与饲料。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-English origin of weed is unsettled, and the earliest date of the compound is approximate rather than a fixed citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：weed 在英语之前的来源没有定论，复合词的最早年代也只是约数，而非确切书证。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for the same thing; group two holds words for edible sea plants that overlap without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同一种东西的形近词；第二组是可食海生植物的近义词，彼此重叠但并非同义。

entries.definition: Built from sea + -ward 'in the direction of', it means toward the sea and has nothing to do with weed.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea + -ward「朝……方向」构成，意为朝海的方向，与 weed 无关。

entries.definition: A marine flowering plant with roots and flowers, not an alga; the name looks parallel but the biology is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有根有花的海洋开花植物，不是藻类；名称结构相似，但生物类别不同。

entries.definition: Wrack is seaweed, especially when washed ashore; sea wrack overlaps with seaweed but usually names the stranded mass.
entries.definitionCN: wrack 指海藻，尤指冲上岸的；sea wrack 与 seaweed 重叠，但通常指搁浅的那一堆。

entries.definition: Seaweed is the large, visible member of the algae; the group also contains single-celled forms never called seaweed.
entries.definitionCN: 海藻是藻类中大型、可见的成员；藻类还包括从不被称为 seaweed 的单细胞种类。

entries.definition: A kind of very large brown seaweed forming underwater forests; it is a seaweed, but not every seaweed is kelp.
entries.definitionCN: 一种形成海底森林的超大型褐藻；kelp 属于海藻，但并非所有海藻都是 kelp。

entries.definition: Seaweed of the shore, especially brown kinds cast up by the tide; the word stresses the stranded state.
entries.definitionCN: 岸边的海藻，尤指被潮水冲上岸的褐藻；这个词强调被搁浅的状态。

entries.definition: A Japanese term for dried laver sheets; it names one prepared food, while seaweed is the general material.
entries.definitionCN: 日语词，指干燥的紫菜片；它指一种成品食物，而 seaweed 是泛称的原料。

entries.definition: A red seaweed eaten dried in northern Europe; again a member of the seaweed family rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 北欧常晒干食用的一种红藻；同样是海藻家族的一员，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sea + weed: a plant-like growth of the sea, read literally.
normal.cn: sea + weed：字面就是「海里的草状生长物」。

normal.en: Seaweed is uncountable as a mass but countable as kinds: seaweed on the rocks, seaweeds of the tropics.
normal.cn: 作物质时不可数，作种类时可数：礁石上的 seaweed，热带的多种 seaweeds。

normal.en: Seagrass is not seaweed: it flowers, has roots, and belongs with land plants.
normal.cn: seagrass 不是 seaweed：它有花有根，属于陆生植物的近亲。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seaweed extract, seaweed farming, seaweed soup, seaweed bed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：海藻提取物、海藻养殖、海藻汤、海藻床。

normal.en: The industrial product alginate comes from brown seaweed, which links the food word to chemistry.
normal.cn: 工业产品 alginate 来自褐藻，这把食物词与化学连了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a green ribbon that keeps waving even after the wave has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿色的带子，浪走了它还在摆。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of the sea carried home on a woman's back.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮「海」被背回家。

abstract.en: Picture a tangled heap of nets that looks like it grew on the quay.
abstract.cn: 想象码头上一堆缠结的渔网，像是从岸上长出来的海藻。

examples.en: Seaweed on the rocks keeps the shore cool and wet at low tide.
examples.cn: 礁石上的海藻在退潮时为岸边保冷保湿。

examples.en: The farm grows seaweed for food and for alginate.
examples.cn: 这个养殖场养殖海藻，用于食用和提取褐藻胶。

examples.en: A thick layer of seaweed marked where the storm tide had reached.
examples.cn: 厚厚一层海藻标出了风暴潮抵达的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: sea（海）+ weed（草）——海里的草就是海藻；看到礁石上的绿带子就想这个词

root: 英语本族复合词：sea（古英语 sǣ「海」）+ weed（古英语 wēod「草、植物」）；weed 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material through its uses: the plant in the sea, the crop in the basket, the raw material in the factory, the mulch on the field, the wrack on the strand, the forest under water, the sheet on the plate, and finally the tangle in the harbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种材料穿过各种用途：海里的植物、篮里的收成、厂里的原料、田里的肥料、滩上的搁浅物、水下的森林、盘上的薄片，最后是港口的缠结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet green ribbons hanging from rocks, water still dripping from them.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿漉漉的绿带子挂在礁石上，水还在往下滴。

branches.en: WHERE IT LIES: alive on the rock or dead on the strand, the word stays with the material.
branches.cn: 它在哪儿：活着长在石上，或死了搁在滩上，词都跟着这份材料走。

branches.en: FOOD: the harvest is eaten fresh, dried, or pressed into sheets.
branches.cn: 食物：收成可鲜食、晒干，或压成薄片。

branches.en: WORKING MATERIAL: factories extract gums, farms dig it into the soil.
branches.cn: 可用之材：工厂提炼胶质，农田把它翻进土里。

branches.en: HABITAT: a dense stand becomes a forest that shelters other life.
branches.cn: 栖息地：密集的一片成了庇护其他生命的森林。

branches.en: SHAPE ALONE: the figurative sense keeps only the long, wet, tangled look.
branches.cn: 只剩形态：比喻义只保留长、湿、缠结的样子。

intro.en: Seaweed is a compound, so its two free morphemes can be read separately and then recombined in other words.
intro.cn: seaweed 是复合词，两个自由语素可以分开读，再组合进别的词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: sea and weed are native English words. The Latin-based relatives are algae, algal and alginate, borrowed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：sea 与 weed 是英语本族词。以拉丁为源的亲属词 algae、algal、alginate 是另行借入的。

items.example: The compound names the place of growth.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半标出生长地点。

items.example: The second half names the plant-like growth.
items.exampleCN: 后半标出像植物的生长物。

items.example: Seaweed covered the rocks.
items.exampleCN: 海藻覆满了礁石。

items.example: The bay holds dozens of seaweeds.
items.exampleCN: 这个海湾有数十种海藻。

items.meaningCN: 带海藻味的；覆满海藻的
items.example: The cove was seaweedy at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时这个小湾到处是海藻。

items.meaning: a patch where seaweed grows thickly
items.example: Fish shelter in the seaweed bed.
items.exampleCN: 鱼在海藻床里躲避。

items.example: The lotion contains seaweed extract.
items.exampleCN: 这款乳液含海藻提取物。

items.example: Seaweed farming spread along the cold coast.
items.exampleCN: 海藻养殖在寒冷海岸推广开来。

definition_zh: 有先见之明的；能预知的
definition_en: knowing or acting as if one already knows what is going to happen
core_image: 一个人提前站在明天的位置上，回头看今天的人群
scene: 他在会上说这栋楼迟早会出问题，两年后果然塌了。 He said at the meeting that the building would fail, and two years later the remark proved prescient.
sceneCN: 这里 prescient 指有先见之明（第 1 个义项：预见未来）；句意为他在会上说这栋楼迟早会出问题，两年后这句话果然应验，显出先见。

pos.zh: 有先见之明的；能预知的

senses.title: Foreseeing events
senses.definition: of a person, knowing what will happen before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 形容人在事情发生之前就知道它会来
senses.example: The chairman was prescient about the collapse of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 主席对市场的崩盘早有预见。
senses.why: The word attributes knowledge of the future, which no one quite has.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把对未来的知识归给某个人，而没人真能拥有它。

senses.title: Prescient warning
senses.definition: of a warning that names the danger before anyone else does
senses.definitionCN: 在别人之前就点出危险的警告
senses.example: Her prescient warning was filed and forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句有先见的警告被归档，然后被遗忘。
senses.why: The word judges the timing of a sentence, not the person who said it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判一句话的时机，而非说话的人。

senses.title: Prescient analysis
senses.definition: of reasoning that reaches tomorrow's conclusion from today's facts
senses.definitionCN: 从今天的事实推出明天结论的推理
senses.example: The report's prescient analysis read the trade figures correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告有预见性的分析把贸易数字读对了。
senses.why: Analysis earns the word by being right early, not by being loud.
senses.whyCN: 分析靠早而正确赢得这个词，不靠声量。

senses.title: Prescient writer
senses.definition: of an author whose work describes a future that later arrives
senses.definitionCN: 作品描述了后来真的到来的未来的作者
senses.example: The novel was prescient about how people would talk to machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说预见了人们将如何与机器交谈。
senses.why: Art can be called prescient without having made a single forecast.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以被称作有先见，却一次预测也没做过。

senses.title: Market call
senses.definition: of a financial judgement that turns out right before the crowd agrees
senses.definitionCN: 在众人认同之前就被证明正确的金融判断
senses.example: His prescient call on the currency made him briefly famous.
senses.exampleCN: 他对货币的先见判断让他短暂成名。
senses.why: Money gives the word a scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 钱给这个词一块记分牌。

senses.title: Prescient policy
senses.definition: of a rule made for a problem that has not yet fully appeared
senses.definitionCN: 为尚未完全出现的难题制定的规则
senses.example: The ban looked fussy then and prescient now.
senses.exampleCN: 那项禁令当时显得多事，如今显得有先见。
senses.why: Institutions are praised for this sense only after the fact.
senses.whyCN: 机构只会在事后因这个义项受到称赞。

senses.title: Prescient dream
senses.definition: of a dream or a feeling that seems to have announced an event
senses.definitionCN: 似乎提前宣告了某件事的梦或感觉
senses.example: She had a prescient dream the night before the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故前一晚，她做了一个预知般的梦。
senses.why: The word admits the uncanny without quite believing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词容许诡异之事，却不完全相信它。

senses.title: Retrospective prescience
senses.definition: the label given afterwards to a remark that happened to be right
senses.definitionCN: 事后给一句碰巧说对的话贴上的标签
senses.example: Every lucky guess is called prescient once the results are in.
senses.exampleCN: 结果一出来，每个走运的猜测都被叫作先见。
senses.why: This sense exposes the trick: the word is often awarded backwards.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项揭穿了把戏：这个词常是倒着颁发的。

intro.en: Prescient is 'knowing before': prae- is before, and scire is to know.
intro.cn: prescient 就是「先知道」：prae- 为在前，scire 为知道。

items.en: Scire meant 'to know', the verb behind science and conscience.
items.cn: scire 意为「知道」，是 science 与 conscience 背后的动词。

items.en: Scientia meant 'knowledge', and English made it science.
items.cn: scientia 意为「知识」，英语把它变成 science。

items.en: Praescire meant 'to know beforehand', a plain compound of prae- and scire.
items.cn: praescire 意为「预先知道」，是 prae- 与 scire 的朴素复合。

items.en: English formed prescient from the Latin participle in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由拉丁语分词造出 prescient。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to warnings, analyses, novels and lucky guesses alike.
items.cn: 现代用法把它同时用于警告、分析、小说与走运的猜测。

note.en: The look-alike group is the scire family; the near-meaning group separates prophetic, foresighted, clairvoyant and far-sighted.
note.cn: 形近组是 scire 词族；近义组把「预言的」「有远见的」「千里眼的」与「目光长远的」分开。

entries.definition: knowledge of what is coming.
entries.definitionCN: 对将至之事的知识。

entries.definition: with knowledge of what is coming.
entries.definitionCN: 带着对将至之事的了解。

entries.definition: knowing everything.
entries.definitionCN: 无所不知的。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 内心的是非感。

entries.definition: announcing what will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告将发生之事的。

entries.definition: planning for what may come.
entries.definitionCN: 为可能到来之事作打算的。

entries.definition: seeing things beyond the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 看见感官之外之物的。

entries.definition: looking far ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 看得远的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a man standing in tomorrow and looking back at today.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一个人站在明天，回头看今天」的画面。

normal.en: Prescient is prae plus scire: to know before.
normal.cn: prescient 是 prae 加 scire：先知道。

normal.en: Think of a warning filed two years before the collapse.
normal.cn: 想象一条在崩塌前两年就被归档的警告。

normal.en: Pre-SCI-ent: the stress sits on sci, where the knowing lives.
normal.cn: pre-SCI-ent：重音落在 sci，正是「知道」所在。

normal.en: Say PRESH-uhnt in American speech; the s softens like a whisper.
normal.cn: 美式读成 PRESH-uhnt，那个 s 软得像耳语。

normal.en: Pair it with hindsight: prescient is hindsight awarded in advance.
normal.cn: 把它和 hindsight 配对：prescient 是提前颁发的后见之明。

abstract.en: The word is always awarded after the event, which is why it tells us more about winners than about vision.
abstract.cn: 这个词总在事件之后颁发，所以它更多地告诉我们谁赢了，而不是谁有远见。

abstract.en: A prescient remark needs only to be right early; it does not need to be wise.
abstract.cn: 一句有先见的话只需要早而正确，不需要有智慧。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a small shelf of prescient warnings that nobody read in time.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有一小架没人及时读的先见警告。

examples.en: The remark proved prescient two years later.
examples.cn: 两年后这句话被证明有先见。

examples.en: The chairman was prescient about the collapse of the market.
examples.cn: 主席对市场的崩盘早有预见。

examples.en: The novel was prescient about how people would talk to machines.
examples.cn: 这部小说预见了人们将如何与机器交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: pre（在前）+ scient（知道）：提前就知道，就是「有先见之明的」。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）与 scire（知道）构成的 praesciens

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all arrive early: a person, a warning, an analysis, a writer, a market call, a policy, a dream and a label given out after the fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都提前到达：一个人、一个警告、一份分析、一位作家、一次市场判断、一项政策、一个梦，以及事后颁发的标签。

core.en: STANDING IN TOMORROW, LOOKING BACK
core.cn: 站在明天，回头看

branches.en: A person and a dream, both credited with the future.
branches.cn: 被归功于未来的人与梦。

branches.en: A warning and an analysis, judged by timing.
branches.cn: 按时机被评判的警告与分析。

branches.en: A writer whose fiction arrives before the fact.
branches.cn: 小说先于事实到达的作家。

branches.en: A market call and a policy.
branches.cn: 一次市场判断与一项政策。

branches.en: The prize handed out afterwards.
branches.cn: 事后颁发的那份奖。

intro.en: The scire family is about knowing: science is organised knowledge, conscience is knowledge shared with oneself, prescient is knowledge that arrives early.
intro.cn: scire 词族关乎知道：science 是有组织的知识，conscience 是与自己共享的知识，prescient 是提前到达的知识。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- supplies the 'before' and scire supplies the 'know'; the participle praesciens simply joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 提供「在前」，scire 提供「知道」；分词 praesciens 只是把它们接起来。

items.exampleCN: 一个先见的警告。

items.example: A moment of prescience.
items.exampleCN: 一刻先见。

items.example: He spoke presciently.
items.exampleCN: 他带着先见说话。

items.example: Modern science.

items.example: A clear conscience.
items.exampleCN: 清白的良心。

items.example: A conscious choice.

items.example: An omniscient narrator.

definition_zh: 出口；输出；（货物的）外运；（历史上的）遣送出境外
definition_en: the act or process of sending goods, data or people out of a country
core_image: 海关档案室里一本厚厚的簿册，每一页都记着一批离境货物的名称、数量与去向
scene: 海关档案室里，关员把一批刚离境的货物逐项登记到簿册上，记录它们的数量与去向。 The clerk recorded the exportation of the machinery in a thick ledger.
sceneCN: 这里指「货物外运这一行为」，对应第 1 个义项：把货物从本国送出境的动作与过程；句意为关员把这批机械的出口登记进一本厚簿册。画面要点：档案室、厚簿册、离境货物清单、登记笔。

pos.zh: 出口；输出（不可数，指行为或过程）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次外运事件）

derivatives.zh: 出口（exportation 的基础动词，去掉行动名词后缀即得，指把货物搬出去）
出口商（export 加施动后缀，指执行外运的一方）
可出口的（export 加表示可能的形容词后缀，指允许外销）
多次外运（exportation 加复数后缀，语义由单次过程转为多次事件）
出口带动的（export 加 led 构成的复合形容词，指增长由出口驱动）

senses.title: The act of sending goods out of a country
senses.titleCN: 把货物送出国境的行为
senses.definition: the act or process of sending goods out of a country to another market
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从本国送出、运往另一市场的动作或过程
senses.example: The clerk recorded the exportation of the machinery in a thick ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 关员把这批机械的出口登记进一本厚簿册。
senses.why: Latin exportatio is a noun of action from exportare 'to carry out', so the word names the carrying itself rather than the cargo or the carrier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 exportatio 是由 exportare「搬出去」构成的行动名词，因此这个词指搬运本身，而不是货物或承运人。

senses.title: The customs procedure for goods leaving
senses.definition: the official procedure, declaration and permission required for goods to leave a country
senses.definitionCN: 货物离境所需的官方手续、申报与许可
senses.example: Exportation requires a declaration filed before loading.
senses.exampleCN: 出口须在装船前提交申报。
senses.why: Once a state watches goods leave, the act acquires paperwork, and the noun shifts from motion to procedure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家要看着货物离开，这个动作就有了文书，名词便从位移转向程序。

senses.title: The measured outflow in trade statistics
senses.titleCN: 贸易统计中计量的外流量
senses.definition: the total quantity or value of goods sent out, as recorded in trade accounts
senses.definitionCN: 贸易账目中记录的送出货物总量或总值
senses.example: Exportation rose by nine percent in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第二季度出口量上升了百分之九。
senses.why: Statistics turn a repeated action into an aggregate, so the noun comes to denote a figure rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: 统计把反复发生的动作汇成总量，于是这个名词指一个数字而不是一次事件。

senses.title: A consignment sent abroad
senses.definition: a particular shipment of goods sent out of the country
senses.definitionCN: 被送出本国的一批具体货物
senses.example: The exportation left the port on Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 这批出口货物周二离港。
senses.why: A process noun can also stand for its product, especially when the shipment is treated as one event.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词也能指它的产物，尤其当一批货物被视作一次事件时。

senses.title: Bulk sending of a single commodity
senses.definition: the large-scale sending of one commodity, such as grain or timber, to foreign buyers
senses.definitionCN: 把粮食、木材等单一商品大规模送往外国买方
senses.example: The exportation of grain was halted during the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 旱灾期间谷物外运被叫停。
senses.why: Commodity policy speaks of flows rather than shipments, so the abstract noun fits bans and quotas.
senses.whyCN: 商品政策谈的是流量而不是单票货物，因此抽象名词适合与禁令、配额搭配。

senses.title: The outward transfer of data
senses.definition: the transfer of data from one system to another, especially out of a controlled environment
senses.definitionCN: 数据从一个系统转移到另一个系统，尤指离开受控环境
senses.example: Cross-border data exportation is limited by the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 新规限制了数据跨境输出。
senses.why: Computing and law borrowed the trade term because data, like cargo, can be moved out of a jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 计算机与法律借用贸易术语，因为数据和货物一样可以被移出管辖范围。

senses.title: Historical sending of people out of a country
senses.titleCN: 历史上把人员遣送出境外
senses.definition: the former practice of sending convicted persons or unwanted groups out of a country
senses.definitionCN: 旧时把罪犯或被视为多余的人群送出本国的做法
senses.example: The old records list the exportation of convicts to the colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案记载了把罪犯遣送到殖民地的做法。
senses.why: The verb once applied to persons as well as goods, so the noun retains this historical, now archaic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词旧时也用于人，不只是货物，因此名词保留了这一历史义，如今已属古旧用法。

senses.title: The outward spread of ideas or culture
senses.definition: the carrying of ideas, styles or institutions from one country to others
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、风格或制度从一国传到别国
senses.example: The exportation of the city's design style changed neighbouring ports.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市设计风格的外传改变了邻近港口。
senses.why: The formal noun extends the trade image to influence, where nothing is bought and nothing is weighed.
senses.whyCN: 这一正式名词把贸易意象扩展到影响力，那里既无人购买，也无人称重。

intro.en: Exportation comes from Latin exportatio 'a carrying out', the action noun of exportare. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: exportation 出自拉丁 exportatio「搬出」，是 exportare 的行动名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Portare 'to carry' formed the stem of the family, with a pre-Latin origin that is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: portare「搬运」构成这个词族的词干，其拉丁语之前的来源属重构，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus portare gave exportare 'to carry out, send away'.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 portare 构成 exportare「搬出、送走」。

items.en: The suffix -atio made a noun of action, so exportatio meant the carrying out itself.
items.cn: 后缀 -atio 构成行动名词，因此 exportatio 指「搬出」这一动作本身。

items.en: English took both the verb and the action noun from Latin, using them first in a general sense of sending out.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语同时借入动词与行动名词，最初泛指「送出」。

items.en: Commercial and customs usage narrowed the noun to goods leaving a country, and later acts extended it to people and to data.
items.cn: 商业与海关用法把这个名词收窄为货物离境，后来的法令又把它扩展到人与数据。

note.en: The first group shares the outward carrying stem or looks close to it; the second group names related processes of sending things out.
note.cn: 第一组共享「向外搬运」词干或与之外形相近；第二组是其他表示「把东西送出去」的过程。

entries.definition: The act in verb form, or the goods themselves; exportation is the formal process noun with no plural cargo sense in ordinary use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式或指货物本身；exportation 是正式的过程名词，日常不指具体货物。

entries.definition: The party that exports; the two words differ in that one names a process and the other a person or firm.
entries.definitionCN: 执行出口的一方；两词的区别在于一个指过程，一个指人或公司。

entries.definition: The same action noun with the inward prefix: the process of bringing goods in.
entries.definitionCN: 同一行动名词配向内的前缀：把货物运入的过程。

entries.definition: Trans- 'across' plus portare: the process of carrying from place to place, with no border and no sale.
entries.definitionCN: trans-「穿过」加 portare：把货物从一处运到另一处的过程，不含国界与买卖。

entries.definition: A batch of goods sent by a carrier; it counts consignments, while exportation names the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 承运人运送的一批货物；它计批次，而 exportation 指整个过程。

entries.definition: The movement of goods or money out of a place; it is neutral about borders and law.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或资金从一个地方流出的移动；对边界与法律保持中性。

entries.definition: A sale made in a foreign market; the money changes hands, while exportation records the goods leaving.
entries.definitionCN: 在外国市场完成的销售；钱在那里易手，而 exportation 记录的是货物离境。

entries.definition: The sending off of goods or messages; it stresses promptness rather than customs status.
entries.definitionCN: 把货物或消息送出；它强调迅速，而不是海关身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin action suffix, the real carrying root and real administrative phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁行动后缀、真实的搬运词根与真实行政搭配。

normal.en: -atio makes an action noun, so exportation is the carrying-out itself, not the cargo.
normal.cn: -atio 构成行动名词，所以 exportation 是「搬出」这个动作，而不是货物。

normal.en: The base verb is export, and the doer is exporter; the three form a set.
normal.cn: 基础动词是 export，执行者是 exporter，三者构成一套。

normal.en: Fixed phrases are administrative: exportation licence, ban on exportation, exportation records.
normal.cn: 固定搭配属行政语域：出口许可、出口禁令、出口记录。

normal.en: The mirror noun is importation, the same suffix with the inward prefix.
normal.cn: 镜像名词是 importation，同一后缀配向内的前缀。

normal.en: This noun is formal and uncountable in ordinary use, so it suits laws and reports.
normal.cn: 这个名词在通常用法中正式且不可数，因此适合法律与报告。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where each line is an act, not a thing, and the act fills a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，每一行是一个动作而不是一件东西，而这个动作占满一页。

abstract.en: Picture a border official stamping the leaving itself rather than the box.
abstract.cn: 想象边境官员盖章的对象是「离开」这件事，而不是箱子。

abstract.en: Picture a signal leaving a sealed room, its path written down before it goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信号离开封闭的房间，在出发前就先把路径记录下来。

examples.en: Exportation of the antique furniture was forbidden.
examples.cn: 这件古董家具被禁止出口。

examples.en: The report traced the exportation of raw cotton over ten years.
examples.cn: 报告追溯了十年间原棉的外运情况。

examples.en: New rules govern the exportation of personal data.
examples.cn: 新规管束个人数据的输出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「往外搬这件事」——export 是搬出去，加上表示行为的尾巴，指搬出去的过程 → 出口、外运

root: 拉丁 exportare「搬出去」+ -atio（行动名词后缀）→ exportatio「搬出」；词根 portare 意为「搬运」，更深来源为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a process or its record: the act of sending out, the customs procedure, the statistical flow, one consignment, a bulk commodity flow, a data transfer, a historical removal of people and a cultural spread.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指一个过程或其记录：送出的动作、海关手续、统计流量、单批货物、大宗商品外运、数据转移、历史上的人员遣送，以及文化外传。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a customs ledger in which each leaving shipment occupies one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本海关簿册，每一批离境货物占一行。

branches.en: BASE PROCESS: the noun names the carrying out itself.
branches.cn: 基础过程：名词指搬运出去这一动作本身。

branches.en: ADMINISTERED FLOW: paperwork and commodity policy turn the act into a regulated procedure.
branches.cn: 被管理的外流：文书与商品政策把动作变成受规管的程序。

branches.en: COUNTED AND BATCHED: the process becomes a figure, or one shipment.
branches.cn: 计量与分批：过程变成一个数字，或一批货物。

branches.en: DATA OUT: the same process applied to records leaving a system.
branches.cn: 数据外出：同一过程用于离开系统的记录。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CULTURE: persons and ideas also travel under this name.
branches.cn: 人与文化：人与观念也以这个名义出行。

intro.en: Exportation is a Latin action noun: a prefix of direction, a verb of carrying and a suffix that turns the act into a noun.
intro.cn: exportation 是一个拉丁行动名词：方向前缀、搬运动词，以及把动作变为名词的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare 'to carry' gives export, import, transport and portable, while -atio forms nouns of action such as exportatio and importatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 portare「搬运」衍生 export、import、transport 与 portable，-atio 则构成 exportatio、importatio 这类行动名词。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀决定搬运的方向。

items.example: The root names the movement of a load.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指一担货物的移动。

items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: Exportation of the ore was recorded.

items.example: They export citrus each winter.

items.example: The exporter paid the levy.
items.exampleCN: 出口商缴纳了这笔税。

items.example: The hides are exportable.
items.exampleCN: 这些皮革可以出口。

items.example: Importation of the seed is banned.

items.example: Transportation costs doubled.
items.exampleCN: 运输成本翻了一番。

items.example: They carried a portable stove.
items.exampleCN: 他们带了一台便携炉。

definition_zh: 腹部的；与腹有关的
definition_en: relating to the abdomen, the part of the body between the chest and the legs
core_image: 躯干中段的一圈，被一条腰带圈出的区域

pos.zh: 腹部的；与腹有关的

senses.title: Of the belly region
senses.definition: belonging to or located in the part of the trunk between the chest and the pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 属于或位于躯干上胸下骨盆之间的那一部分
senses.example: An abdominal strain kept the player out of the match.
senses.exampleCN: 腹部拉伤让这名球员错过了比赛。
senses.why: The adjective is built directly on the Latin noun for the belly; it points at that one region of the trunk.

senses.title: Of structures on the underside
senses.titleCN: 位于腹侧或下方的（如鱼鳍）
senses.definition: of fins or other structures, positioned on the underside or belly side of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 指鱼鳍等结构位于动物的下腹一侧
senses.example: The characin has abdominal fins set far back on its body.
senses.exampleCN: 这种脂鲤的腹鳍长在身体很靠后的位置。
senses.why: In zoology the same region word labels whatever grows on the belly side, fins included.
senses.whyCN: 在动物学中，同一个部位词也用来标记长在腹侧的东西，鱼鳍也不例外。

intro.en: Abdominal is simply Latin abdomen plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: abdominal 就是拉丁语 abdomen 加形容词后缀 -al。

items.en: Abdomen named the belly; its earlier origin is uncertain, possibly from abdere, to hide.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdomen 指腹部；更早的来源不确定，一般认为可能与 abdere「藏」有关。

items.en: Abdominalis was formed in learned writing for things of the belly.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 abdominalis 在学术写作中构成，指与腹有关之物。

items.en: The adjective came into learned English through French medical texts.
items.cn: 该形容词经法语医学文献进入学术英语。

items.en: Abdominal settled in anatomy and medicine.
items.cn: 十七世纪起 abdominal 固定用于解剖学与医学。

items.en: It now appears in medicine, fitness, and zoology.
items.cn: 如今该词见于医学、健身与动物学。

note.en: The family is small: the noun abdomen and its Latin cousins.
note.cn: 这个词族很小：名词 abdomen 及其拉丁语近亲。

entries.definition: the noun for the belly

entries.definition: detestable; only the opening letters match

normal.cn: abdomen ＋ al：把「腹」变成形容词。

abstract.en: Feel a belt tightening around the middle.
abstract.cn: 感到一条腰带在腰腹收紧。

abstract.en: See a dotted line drawn on the torso.
abstract.cn: 看见躯干上画出的一条虚线。

abstract.en: Picture scales along a fish's underside.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼腹侧面排列的鳞片。

examples.en: He complained of sharp abdominal pain all night.
examples.cn: 他整夜诉说剧烈的腹痛。

examples.en: Strong abdominal muscles protect the lower back.
examples.cn: 强健的腹肌能保护下背部。

examples.en: The surgeon closed the abdominal incision with care.
examples.cn: 外科医生小心缝合了腹部切口。

root: 拉丁语 abdomen「腹部」＋ 形容词后缀 -al（源自拉丁 -alis）。abdomen 更早来源不确定，一般认为可能与 abdere「隐藏」相关，属存疑说法。学源形容词经中世纪拉丁语 abdominalis 与法语医学文本进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses map one region: the human belly, and whatever sits on an animal's underside.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项对应同一个区域：人的腹部，以及动物腹侧的构造。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the middle band of the trunk, ringed by a belt.
core.cn: 核心意象：躯干中段，被腰带圈出的那一圈。

branches.en: THE HUMAN BELLY: pain, muscles, surgery all live here.
branches.cn: 人的腹部：疼痛、肌肉、手术都在这里。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL UNDERSIDE: fins and parts on the belly side.
branches.cn: 动物腹侧：长在腹面的鳍等构造。

branches.en: ONE REGION: both senses point at the belly side.
branches.cn: 同一区域：两个义项都指向腹侧。

branches.en: LEARNED LANGUAGE: both are technical over everyday belly.
branches.cn: 书面语：两者都比白话 belly 更正式。

branches.en: ADJECTIVE JOB: the word never names the organ itself.

latinIntro.cn: abdomen 见于拉丁语记载；其更深层来源仍不确定。

definition_en: to speak or recite something loudly and dramatically, as if to an audience
core_image: 一个人站在空房间中央，抬手把句子一句句抛向看不见的听众
scene: 他在台上把台词念得铿锵有力。 He began to declaim the opening lines.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：declaim 指朗诵诗文；句意是他开始朗诵开场的那几行。

pos.zh: 慷慨陈词；高声演说；朗诵；猛烈抨击

senses.title: Speak dramatically

senses.why: Written lines given breath and volume.

senses.why: A voice thrown against a wall of policy.

intro.cn: declaim 源自拉丁语 declamare（高声喊出），由 de- 加 clamare 构成。

items.en: Clamare meant to cry out or shout.
items.cn: clamare 意为喊叫。

items.en: Declamare meant to practise public speaking aloud.
items.cn: declamare 意为练习高声公开演说。

items.en: Declame was an early spelling of the verb.
items.cn: declame 是该动词的早期拼法。

items.en: Declaim settled as the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 declaim 定为现代拼法。

items.en: Declaim was used for theatrical recitation.
items.cn: 十七世纪 declaim 用于戏剧式朗诵。

items.en: Declaim gained the sense of pompous speech.
items.cn: 十九世纪 declaim 带上夸夸其谈的意味。

definition_zh: 保存；保护；维护；留存状态
definition_en: the act of keeping something in its original condition and safe from damage, decay or loss
core_image: 一只玻璃罐封着一枚老照片和一片果肉，罐外贴着标着年份的标签
scene: 这里指「保存」。 The preservation of the manuscript required a climate-controlled room.
sceneCN: 这里 preservation 是「保护、保全」（第 1 个义项：使事物免受损坏）；句意：这份手稿的保存需要一个恒温恒湿的房间。图中可辨识物件：密封玻璃罐、老照片、标着年份的标签。

senses.title: Keeping from harm
senses.definition: the act of keeping something safe from damage, decay or destruction
senses.definitionCN: 使某物免受损坏、腐烂或毁坏的行为
senses.example: Preservation of the wreck began with a survey of the site.
senses.exampleCN: 沉船的保护工作从现场勘测开始。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep safe' gives praeservare, 'to keep safe beforehand'. The noun names that guarding.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 servare“看护”构成 praeservare“预先保全”，名词命名这份看护。

senses.title: Food preservation
senses.titleCN: 食品保存：让食物过季还在
senses.definition: the treatment of food so that it does not spoil, by drying, salting, canning or cooling
senses.definitionCN: 通过干燥、盐腌、罐装或冷藏使食物不腐败的处理
senses.example: Salt was the main means of preservation before refrigeration.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷藏出现之前，盐是主要的保存手段。
senses.why: Food spoils through organisms and moisture, so preservation is a war against decay carried out before decay starts.
senses.whyCN: 食物因微生物与水分而腐坏，所以保存是一场在腐坏开始之前发动的战争。

senses.title: Heritage conservation
senses.definition: the professional care of buildings, objects and documents so that they survive for the future
senses.definitionCN: 对建筑、器物与文献的专业养护，使其留存给未来
senses.example: The preservation of the old library took six years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆的保护工程耗时六年。
senses.why: Heritage work uses preservation because the goal is not repair but keeping the original fabric intact.
senses.whyCN: 遗产保护用 preservation，因为目标不是修缮，而是让原有材料完整留存。

senses.title: Nature protection
senses.titleCN: 自然保护：让物种和栖息地留着
senses.definition: the protection of wildlife, habitats or natural resources from destruction
senses.definitionCN: 使野生动物、栖息地或自然资源免遭破坏
senses.example: The trust works on the preservation of wetland birds.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构致力于湿地鸟类的保护。
senses.why: Here the thing preserved is a living system, so the word shifts from objects to processes that must keep running.
senses.whyCN: 这里被保存的是活的系统，词义从物件转向必须持续运转的过程。

senses.title: Legal and archival keeping
senses.definition: the duty or practice of keeping records and evidence unaltered for later use
senses.definitionCN: 为日后使用而保持记录与证据未被改动的义务或做法
senses.example: The court ordered the preservation of all emails.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令保全所有电子邮件。
senses.why: Law cares about alteration, not decay. Preservation here means the object stays exactly as it was when the dispute began.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心的是改动，不是腐坏。这里的保存意味着物件保持在争议开始时的原样。

senses.title: Self-preservation
senses.definition: the instinct or action of keeping oneself alive or unharmed
senses.definitionCN: 使自己存活或不受伤害的本能或行动
senses.example: Self-preservation made him lie about the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 出于自我保护，他在事故上撒了谎。
senses.why: The compound self-preservation turns the word inward: the thing guarded and the guard are the same person.
senses.whyCN: self-preservation 把词转向内部：被保护之物与保护者都是同一个人。

senses.title: Condition of an object
senses.titleCN: 保存状况：东西还挺完整
senses.definition: the degree to which an old object has survived intact, as in a good state of preservation
senses.definitionCN: 旧物完整留存的程度，如“保存状况良好”
senses.example: The coins were found in a remarkable state of preservation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些硬币被发现时保存状况极好。
senses.why: English uses the noun for the result as well as the act, so preservation can be a property of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语用这个名词兼指结果与动作，所以 preservation 也可以是事物自身的属性。

senses.title: Digital preservation
senses.titleCN: 数字保存：别让文件读不出来
senses.definition: the work of keeping digital files readable as formats and hardware change
senses.definitionCN: 在格式与硬件更替中保持数字文件可读的工作
senses.example: Digital preservation means migrating files before the software dies.
senses.exampleCN: 数字保存意味着在软件淘汰之前迁移文件。
senses.why: Digital objects do not rot, they become unreadable, so preservation adds format migration to its older meaning.
senses.whyCN: 数字对象不会腐烂，而会变得读不出来，因此数字保存给旧词义加上了格式迁移。

intro.en: Preservation comes from Latin praeservare 'to keep safe beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus servare 'to watch over, keep'. The noun is praeservatio.
intro.cn: preservation 来自拉丁 praeservare“预先保全”，由 prae-“在前”加 servare“看守、保存”构成，名词为 praeservatio。

items.en: servare meant 'to watch over, keep safe, preserve'. It is generally traced to a PIE root *ser- 'to watch over', but the reconstruction is debated and should be labelled uncertain.
items.cn: servare 意为“看守、保全、保存”。一般追溯到原始印欧语 *ser-“看护”，但该重构有争议，应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: servare 'keep safe' is not the same verb as servire 'to serve', which comes from servus 'slave'. Preserve and serve only look related in English.
items.cn: servare“保全”与 servire“服务”不是同一个动词，后者的来源是 servus“奴隶”。preserve 与 serve 只在英语中形近。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus servare gives praeservare, 'to guard in advance'. The prefix marks action taken before the danger arrives.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 servare 得 praeservare“提前看守”。前缀标记在危险到来之前采取的行动。

items.en: The action noun praeservatio named a keeping safe; medieval Latin used it in legal and medical senses.
items.cn: 动作名词 praeservatio 指保全；中世纪拉丁语把它用于法律与医学语境。

items.en: English borrows preservation through French, first for the keeping of food and of health.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 preservation，最初用于保存食物与维护健康。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries the word expands to buildings, wildlife and finally digital files, each with its own decay to fight.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，这个词扩展到建筑、野生动物，最终到数字文件，每一种都有自己的腐坏要对抗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serv- shape, but only some share the root 'keep safe'; the near-meaning group all involve protecting something, with different aims.
note.cn: 形近组共享 serv- 外形，但只有部分共享“保全”词根；近义组都涉及保护，目的不同。

entries.definition: to keep safe from decay; also a reserved area or a fruit conserve. The verb is the act; preservation is the process or result.
entries.definitionCN: 保存；保护区；果酱。动词是动作，preservation 是过程或结果。

entries.definition: a substance added to prevent decay. It is the tool of preservation, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 防腐剂。它是保存的工具，不是过程。

entries.definition: work done for others. It comes from servire 'to serve' and servus 'slave', not from servare 'keep safe'.
entries.definitionCN: 服务。来自 servire“服务”与 servus“奴隶”，并非 servare“保全”。

entries.definition: the protection of nature or heritage, often with careful management and repair. It allows change; preservation prefers no change.
entries.definitionCN: 保护；养护。它允许修复与变动，而 preservation 更倾向于不加改动。

entries.definition: defence against harm. It stresses blocking a threat, while preservation stresses keeping a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 保护。强调挡住威胁，而 preservation 强调维持状态。

entries.definition: the act of keeping or holding on to something. It stresses not losing it, not keeping it intact.
entries.definitionCN: 保留；保有。强调不失去，而非保持完好。

entries.definition: the work of keeping something in good working order. It is continuous repair, where preservation is guarding from decay.
entries.definitionCN: 维护；保养。是持续的修理，而 preservation 是防腐败坏。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: servare means 'keep safe', so preservation is the noun of keeping, not of serving.
normal.cn: servare 意为“保全”，所以 preservation 是“保存”的名词，不是“服务”的名词。

normal.en: The family preserve, preservative, preserver and preservation all keep the serv- stem.
normal.cn: preserve、preservative、preserver、preservation 全族保留 serv- 词干。

normal.en: Food preservation, historic preservation and digital preservation are three battlefields against three kinds of decay.
normal.cn: 食品保存、历史保护、数字保存是三个战场，对抗三种腐坏。

normal.en: The phrase in a good state of preservation shows the noun naming a condition, not an act.
normal.cn: 短语“保存状况良好”显示该名词也能命名一种状态，而非动作。

normal.en: Self-preservation turns the word on the person doing the guarding.
normal.cn: 自我保护把词转向正在看护的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a jar sealed with wax, the air kept outside and the fruit kept inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用蜡封住的罐子：空气挡在外面，果肉留在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case where the light is dimmed so that colour will not fade.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆的展柜把灯调暗，让颜色不褪。

abstract.en: Picture a copy of a file made before the old machine is switched off.
abstract.cn: 想象在老机器关机之前复制出的那份文件。

examples.en: Preservation of the wetland depends on keeping the water level stable.
examples.cn: 湿地的保护取决于保持水位稳定。

examples.en: The archive's preservation budget exceeds its acquisition budget.
examples.cn: 档案馆的保存预算超过了采购预算。

examples.en: Smoking meat is an old method of preservation.
examples.cn: 熏肉是一种古老的保存方法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep something from changing for the worse, whether the enemy is mould, time, law or a dead file format.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都让某物免于向坏的方向改变，无论敌人是霉菌、时间、法律还是失效的文件格式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed jar holding a year in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封住的罐子，把一个年份固定住。

branches.en: ACT AND CONDITION: the noun names the guarding and also the intact state that results.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：这个名词既命名看护，也命名由此得到的完好状态。

branches.en: BODY AND SELF: food kept from spoiling and a person kept alive both fight decay in the nearest frame.
branches.cn: 食物与自身：防止食物腐败与保住自己性命，都在最近的框里对抗腐坏。

branches.en: RECORDED PAST: a manuscript and a digital file both need active care or they vanish.
branches.cn: 被记录的过去：手稿与数字文件都需要主动养护，否则消失。

branches.en: LIVING SYSTEMS: wildlife preservation guards processes rather than objects.
branches.cn: 生命系统：野生动物保护守护的是过程，而非物件。

branches.en: LEGAL FIXITY: evidence preservation means keeping a record exactly as it was.
branches.cn: 法律上的固定：证据保全意味着让记录保持原样。

intro.en: Preservation is prae- plus servare plus -ion. The prefix marks action taken early, the verb marks keeping, and the suffix makes a noun of process or result.
intro.cn: preservation 由 prae- 加 servare 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记提前行动，动词标记看守，后缀构成过程或结果名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare 'keep safe' → praeservare 'guard beforehand'. The stem survives as preserv- in English, while servire 'serve' is a separate line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare“保全”→ praeservare“提前看守”。词干在英语中作 preserv-，而 servire“服务”是另一条线。

items.meaning: to keep from decay or loss
items.example: They preserved the timber with salt.
items.exampleCN: 他们用盐保存木材。

items.meaning: the act or state of being kept safe
items.example: Preservation work starts with documentation.
items.exampleCN: 保护工作从记录开始。

items.meaningCN: 防腐剂（-ive 构成表物或性质的名词）
items.example: The jam contains no preservatives.

items.meaningCN: 保存者；保护者（-er 施事名词）
items.example: He was a preserver of local songs.
items.exampleCN: 他是当地歌谣的保护者。

items.example: The preserved body was found in peat.
items.exampleCN: 这具保存下来的遗体发现于泥炭中。

items.example: Wet paper is barely preservable.
items.exampleCN: 湿纸几乎无法保存。

items.example: Self-preservation overrode his honesty.
items.exampleCN: 自我保护的念头压过了他的诚实。

items.example: Conservation allows sensitive repair.
items.exampleCN: 保护性养护允许适度修复。
