definition_zh: 按时间顺序的；年代学的；编年的
definition_en: arranged in the order in which events happened, or relating to the study of dates and time sequences
core_image: 一条从左向右延伸的时间轴，事件像珠子一样按发生的先后串在上面
scene: 档案馆员把一叠信件摊在长桌上，按邮戳日期从最早排到最晚。 The archivist spreads the letters on a long table and lays them out in chronological order by postmark date.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：chronological 指按时间顺序的；句意是馆员按邮戳日期把信件从最早排到最晚。

pos.zh: 按时间顺序的；年代学的；编年的

senses.title: Arranged by time of occurrence
senses.definition: ordered from earliest to latest according to when things happened
senses.definitionCN: 按照事情发生的先后，从最早到最晚排列
senses.example: The files are kept in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 这些档案按时间顺序保存。
senses.why: Chronological answers one question only: which came first? It ignores importance, size and logic, and keeps a single axis.
senses.whyCN: chronological 只回答一个问题：哪个先发生？它不管重要性、规模与逻辑，只保留一条轴。

senses.title: Belonging to chronology as a discipline
senses.definition: relating to the science of establishing and ordering dates
senses.definitionCN: 与确定日期并排列日期的学问有关
senses.example: Chronological research fixed the date of the eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 年代学研究确定了那次日食的日期。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes a method, not an arrangement. The scholar is not sorting papers but testing whether a date can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述一种方法，而不是一种排列。学者不是在整理纸堆，而是在检验一个日期是否可信。

senses.title: Of a sequence of records or events
senses.definition: describing a series whose items follow one another in time
senses.definitionCN: 描述按时间先后相接的一系列项目
senses.example: The report gives a chronological account of the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 报告按时间顺序叙述了谈判过程。
senses.why: A chronological account follows the clock rather than the argument. The reader learns what happened next, not what mattered most.
senses.whyCN: 编年式叙述跟着时钟走，而不是跟着论点走。读者知道接下来发生了什么，而不是什么最重要。

senses.title: Of age order
senses.definition: arranged by age, as of children in a class or siblings in a family
senses.definitionCN: 按年龄排列，如班级里的孩子或家庭中的兄弟姐妹
senses.example: The children were seated in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们按年龄顺序就座。
senses.why: Age is time made visible in a body. The adjective transfers the timeline from events to people, and the order becomes a seating plan.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是时间在身体上的可见化。这个形容词把时间轴从事件移到人身上，顺序就变成了一张座位表。

senses.title: Chronological narrative form
senses.definition: a style of telling a story from beginning to end without flashbacks
senses.definitionCN: 从头到尾讲述、不使用倒叙的叙事方式
senses.example: The film's chronological structure makes it feel like a documentary.
senses.exampleCN: 影片的编年结构让它像一部纪录片。
senses.why: Storytellers usually rearrange time for effect. Calling a narrative chronological marks the absence of that rearrangement, and that absence is itself a style.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事的人通常为了效果而重排时间。称一个叙述为 chronological，标示这种重排的缺席，而这种缺席本身就是一种风格。

senses.title: Geological time order
senses.definition: relating to the order of rock layers and past geological events
senses.definitionCN: 与岩层及过去地质事件的先后有关
senses.example: Geologists established a chronological framework for the strata.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家为这些地层建立了年代框架。
senses.why: In geology the timeline is read from the ground up: lower layers are older. The adjective describes an order that the earth itself recorded.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，时间轴要从下往上读：下层更古老。这个形容词描述的是大地自己记录下来的顺序。

senses.title: Chronological representation as a timeline
senses.definition: shown on a line or chart where distance stands for elapsed time
senses.definitionCN: 在一条线或图表上呈现，用距离表示流逝的时间
senses.example: The museum uses a chronological chart from 1800 to the present.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆使用一张从 1800 年至今的时间轴图。
senses.why: A timeline turns sequence into space. Once time is drawn as length, gaps and clusters become visible at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 时间轴把先后变成空间。一旦时间被画成长度，空白与密集就一眼可见。

senses.title: Chronological age in contrast to other measures
senses.titleCN: 与其它度量相对的实龄
senses.definition: in psychology and medicine, actual years lived, as opposed to mental or biological age
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学与医学中，实际活过的年数，相对于心理年龄或生理年龄
senses.example: Her chronological age is seventy, but her biological age is closer to fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的实际年龄是七十岁，但生理年龄接近五十。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a way of separating clocks from bodies. It marks the plain calendar count so that another, less visible count can be compared with it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了一种把日历与身体分开的方式。它标出朴素的日历计数，好让另一种不那么可见的计数与之比较。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase chronological order
senses.titleCN: 用于固定搭配 chronological order
senses.definition: in the phrase in chronological order, meaning following the actual sequence of events
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in chronological order，表示依照事件的实际先后
senses.example: Please list the incidents in chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 请按时间顺序列出这些事件。
senses.why: The phrase is the most common use of the word. It functions almost as a single instruction: do not group by theme, do not rank by importance, follow the clock.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是该词最常见的用法。它几乎等于一条单一指令：不要按主题分组，不要按重要性排序，跟着钟表走。

intro.en: Chronological is chronology plus -ical. Chronology was rebuilt in Renaissance Latin from two Greek elements: khronos, 'time', and -logia, 'account or study'. The compound is not classical Greek but a scholarly construction, and chronological came to English through French. Its core meaning has stayed remarkably stable: put events on one line and read them in order.
intro.cn: chronological 是 chronology 加 -ical。chronology 是文艺复兴拉丁语用两个希腊成分重建的：khronos“时间”与 -logia“论述、学问”。这个复合词不是古典希腊语，而是学术构造；chronological 经法语进入英语。其核心义一直相当稳定：把事件放在一条线上，按顺序读。

items.en: Khronos meant 'time' as a span or a period. Its deeper origin is uncertain; linguists have proposed connections with words for cutting or separating, but none is securely established.
items.cn: khronos 指作为一段跨度或时期的时间。它的更深来源不确定；语言学家提出过与“切割、分离”类词的关联，但没有一种被可靠确立。

items.en: Logia, from logos, meant 'speaking, account, reasoned study'. In compounds it named a field of inquiry, as in biology or theology.
items.cn: logia 来自 logos，意为“言说、记述、有理据的探讨”。在复合词中它命名一个研究领域，如 biology 或 theology。

items.en: The compound chronologia was formed by early modern scholars, not attested in classical Greek. It named the study of dates and the arrangement of events in time.
items.cn: 复合词 chronologia 由近代早期学者构造，不见于古典希腊语。它命名对日期的研究以及把事件按时间排列的工作。

items.en: French added -ique to form the adjective chronologique. English borrowed it as chronological in the 16th to 17th century, a date best given as approximate.
items.cn: 法语加 -ique 构成形容词 chronologique。英语在 16 至 17 世纪借入为 chronological，这个年代只能大致给出。

items.en: In English the adjective was used for both the discipline and the arrangement. Historians applied it to annals; scientists later applied it to strata and to measured sequences.
items.cn: 在英语中，这个形容词既用于学科，也用于排列。历史学家用它指编年史；科学家后来用它指地层与可量度的序列。

items.en: Modern usage extends to timelines, data logs, age measures and reverse-ordered feeds. The suffix -ical merely marks the adjectival form; the meaning still comes from the two Greek parts.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到时间轴、数据日志、年龄度量与倒序信息流。后缀 -ical 只标示形容词形式；意义仍来自两个希腊部分。

note.en: The first group separates chronological from two relatives from the same root and from one close adverb. The second group compares words that also deal with order in time.
note.cn: 第一组把 chronological 与两个同根亲属及一个形近副词分开。第二组比较同样处理时间顺序的词。

entries.definition: lasting a long time, said of illness or problems. It shares the Greek root for time but means 'long-drawn-out', not 'in time order'.
entries.definitionCN: 持续很久的，用于疾病或问题。它与“时间”共享希腊词根，但意为“长期的”，不是“按时间排列”。

entries.definition: the study of dates, or an ordered list of events. Chronological is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 年代学，或按顺序排列的事件表。chronological 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: in time order. The adverb modifies a verb; the adjective modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间顺序地。副词修饰动词；形容词修饰名词。

entries.definition: following in a series. It stresses succession and can apply to steps that have no time element at all.
entries.definitionCN: 依次相随的。它强调接续，也可用于完全没有时间要素的步骤。

entries.definition: relating to time in general, as opposed to space or eternity. It does not by itself imply an order.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间本身有关，相对于空间或永恒。它本身并不含“有序”。

entries.definition: coming one after the other without interruption. It can describe generations or attempts, not only dates.
entries.definitionCN: 接连不断相随的。它可描述世代或尝试，不只描述日期。

entries.definition: relating to past events as studied by history. A historical account may be thematic, while a chronological one must follow dates.
entries.definitionCN: 与历史研究的过去事件有关。历史叙述可以按主题，而编年叙述必须跟着日期。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Greek halves of the word and then tie it to the everyday places where the order matters.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用词的两个希腊半部，再把它系到日常需要讲究次序的地方。

normal.en: Split it: chrono (time) plus logical (ordered). Time plus order is the whole word.
normal.cn: 拆开：chrono（时间）加 logical（有逻辑的）。时间加秩序就是整个词。

normal.en: Picture beads on a string, each bead one event.
normal.cn: 想象一串珠子，每颗珠子是一个事件。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: chronological order versus reverse chronological order.
normal.cn: 对比这一对：正序时间与倒序时间。

normal.en: Keep the psychology pair: chronological age against biological age.
normal.cn: 记住心理学那一对：实际年龄与生理年龄。

normal.en: Watch the trap word chronic: same root, completely different meaning.
normal.cn: 提防陷阱词 chronic：同根，意义完全不同。

abstract.en: Hold one axis: a single line from left to right. Every sense either puts something on that line or studies the line itself.
abstract.cn: 抓住一条轴：从左到右的一条线。每个义项要么把某物放上这条线，要么研究这条线本身。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by what is ordered: events, dates, records, people, stories, rocks, charts, ages, and the fixed phrase.
abstract.cn: 按被排序的对象分组：事件、日期、记录、人、故事、岩石、图表、年龄，以及固定短语。

abstract.en: Notice what the word refuses to do: it does not rank importance or explain causes, it only says what came first.
abstract.cn: 留意这个词拒绝做的事：它不排重要性，也不解释原因，只说明什么先发生。

examples.en: Read the chapters in chronological order to follow the argument.
examples.cn: 按章节的时间顺序阅读，以跟上论证。

examples.en: Her chronological age is forty, though she looks younger.
examples.cn: 她的实际年龄是四十岁，虽然看起来更年轻。

examples.en: The archive is organised in reverse chronological order.
examples.cn: 该档案馆按倒序时间排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“克若诺逻辑可”：chrono 是时间，logical 是讲逻辑——按时间的逻辑排下去，就是 chronological，按时间顺序的。

root: 希腊语 khronos“时间”加 -logia“论述、学问”，文艺复兴拉丁语构造为 chronologia；法语加 -ique 成 chronologique，英语借入为 chronological（chronology + -ical）。

sensesIntro.en: Chronological is one of the most obedient adjectives in English: it follows the clock and nothing else. Its nine senses all place something on a single line — letters, negotiations, children, film scenes, rock layers, timelines, ages — or describe the discipline that builds that line. When a text is called chronological, the point is usually that it has refused to reorganise time for effect.
sensesIntro.cn: chronological 是英语中最守规矩的形容词之一：它只跟着钟表，别的都不管。它的九个义项都把某物放上同一条线——信件、谈判、孩子、电影场景、岩层、时间轴、年龄——或者描述建立这条线的学问。当一段文字被称为 chronological，重点通常是它拒绝为了效果而重排时间。

core.en: One axis only: what came first, what came next.
core.cn: 只有一条轴：什么先来，什么后到。

branches.en: ORDER: the plain arrangement and its fixed phrase.
branches.cn: 顺序：朴素的排列及其固定短语。

branches.en: RECORD: the discipline of dating and the sequence it produces.
branches.cn: 记录：断代的学问及其产生的序列。

branches.en: PEOPLE: age order, and actual age measured against other ages.
branches.cn: 人：年龄顺序，以及与他种年龄对照的实际年龄。

branches.en: STORY: narrative that refuses flashbacks.
branches.cn: 故事：拒绝倒叙的叙述。

branches.en: EARTH AND CHART: strata read upward, time drawn as length.
branches.cn: 大地与图表：自下而上读的地层，被画成长度的时间。

intro.en: Chronological carries two Greek pieces and one Latin suffix: khronos, -logia and -ical. The items below follow that build, then add the related forms that share the root for time, including two words that drifted far from 'order'.
intro.cn: chronological 带着两个希腊成分与一个拉丁后缀：khronos、-logia 与 -ical。下面的条目沿这个构造展开，再加上共享“时间”词根的关联形式，其中两个词已经远离“顺序”义。

latinIntro.en: The entries are Latinised Greek rather than native Latin: chronologia is a Renaissance coinage, chronicus is the Latin form of Greek khronikos, and chronographia names the writing of time. They are included as the Latin channel through which English received these forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这些条目是拉丁化的希腊词，而非本土拉丁语：chronologia 是文艺复兴造词，chronicus 是希腊 khronikos 的拉丁形式，chronographia 指对时间的记录。列入它们，是因为英语正是通过拉丁渠道接收这些形式。

items.example: Keep the receipts in chronological order.
items.exampleCN: 把收据按时间顺序保存。

items.meaning: the study of dates; an ordered list of events
items.example: The chronology of the war is still disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这场战争的年表仍有争议。

items.example: The events are listed chronologically.
items.exampleCN: 事件按时间顺序列出。

items.example: A chronologist dated the inscription to the third century.
items.exampleCN: 一位年代学家把铭文断为三世纪。

items.structure: Greek khronikos, 'of time', through Latin chronicus
items.example: He suffers from chronic back pain.
items.exampleCN: 他患有慢性背痛。

items.meaning: something placed in the wrong period
items.meaningCN: 时代错置；不合时宜的事物
items.example: A telephone in a medieval scene is an anachronism.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪场景里出现电话是时代错置。

items.meaning: to make things happen at the same time
items.example: Synchronize the two clocks before the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 实验前把两个钟对准。

items.meaning: actual years lived, as opposed to perceived or biological age
items.example: His chronological age is sixty-five.
items.exampleCN: 他的实际年龄是六十五岁。

items.example: Blog posts appear in reverse chronological order.
items.exampleCN: 博客文章按倒序时间显示。

items.meaning: the sequence in which events actually happened
items.example: The timeline presents the reigns in chronological order.
items.exampleCN: 时间轴按时间顺序呈现各朝统治。

latinEntries.meaning: the study and ordering of dates
the recording or writing of time

definition_zh: 依赖；依靠；依赖性；从属
definition_en: the state of needing or being supported by someone or something else, or of being decided by another factor
core_image: 一根细绳把吊灯吊在天花板的钩子上，灯的全部重量都落在那个钩子上
scene: 补给船延误了，岛上的空油罐排在码头边： The island's dependence on imported fuel became clear when the supply ship was delayed.
sceneCN: 这里 dependence 是「依赖」（第 1 个义项：需要外部供给才能维持）；句意：补给船延误时，这座岛对外来燃料的依赖就暴露无遗。图中可辨识物件：小岛码头、空油罐、延误的补给船、等待卸货的吊车。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠；依赖性；从属关系

forms.label: 不可数用法（表示状态时通常不可数）

senses.title: The state of relying on something
senses.titleCN: 依赖：重量挂在别人身上
senses.definition: the condition of needing another person or thing in order to function or survive
senses.definitionCN: 为了运作或生存而需要另一人或物的状态
senses.example: The village's dependence on the single well shaped its daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 全村对这口唯一水井的依赖塑造了它的日常生活。
senses.why: dependere means 'to hang down from'. A lamp hangs from a hook, and its weight rests on that hook; dependence is that hanging relationship turned into a state noun.
senses.whyCN: dependere 意为“悬挂于……之下”。吊灯挂在钩子上，全部重量压在钩子上；dependence 就是把这种悬挂关系变成状态名词。

senses.title: Economic reliance
senses.definition: a situation in which an economy needs another economy for trade, finance or supply
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体在贸易、金融或供给上需要另一经济体的状况
senses.example: The country's dependence on a single export made it fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家依赖单一出口商品，因此十分脆弱。
senses.why: An economy that leans on one buyer is like a lamp with one hook. The de- prefix points downward, the direction in which support must come.
senses.whyCN: 只靠一个买家的经济体就像只有一只钩子的吊灯。de- 前缀指向下方，也就是支撑必须来自的方向。

senses.title: Drug or alcohol dependence
senses.titleCN: 药物依赖：身体已经离不开
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person needs a substance and cannot stop without distress
senses.definitionCN: 一种医学状态，患者需要某种物质，停用即出现痛苦
senses.example: Long-term use can lead to physical dependence on the painkiller.
senses.exampleCN: 长期使用可能导致对止痛药的身体依赖。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the hanging image: the body has attached its normal function to a chemical hook. Removal of the hook produces withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了悬挂意象：身体把正常功能挂在某个化学钩子上。钩子一撤，就出现戒断反应。

senses.title: Mutual reliance
senses.titleCN: 相互依赖：两根柱子互相撑着
senses.definition: a relationship in which two parties each need the other
senses.definitionCN: 双方各自都需要对方的关系
senses.example: The two industries developed a mutual dependence that neither could easily break.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个行业发展出一种彼此都难以轻易切断的相互依赖。
senses.why: Two hanging objects can support each other, so the single hook becomes a pair of hooks. The noun still names a support relation, now symmetrical.
senses.whyCN: 两个悬挂物可以互相支撑，于是单钩变成一对钩子。这个名词仍命名支撑关系，只是现在是对称的。

senses.title: Statistical dependence
senses.titleCN: 统计依赖性：一个变量的变化牵着另一个
senses.definition: in statistics, the condition in which one variable's value is related to another's
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中一个变量的取值与另一个变量相关的状态
senses.example: The study tested the dependence of rainfall on ocean temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验了降雨对海洋温度的依赖性。
senses.why: A dependent variable hangs from an independent one: change the anchor and the hanging value moves. The statistical term borrows the same geometry.
senses.whyCN: 因变量悬挂在自变量上：锚点一动，悬挂的值就动。统计术语借用了同一套几何关系。

senses.title: Emotional reliance
senses.titleCN: 情感依赖：心里那根绳子
senses.definition: a psychological need for another person's approval, presence or support
senses.definitionCN: 在心理上需要他人的认可、陪伴或支持
senses.example: His emotional dependence made it hard for him to make decisions alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的情感依赖让他很难独自做决定。
senses.why: The support here is not physical weight but reassurance. The metaphor still works because the person's confidence is felt to hang from someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这里的支撑不是物理重量，而是安心感。隐喻仍然成立，因为这个人的信心被感觉成挂在别人身上。

senses.title: Technological reliance
senses.titleCN: 技术依赖：关键零件握在别人手里
senses.definition: the condition of needing foreign technology, components or expertise
senses.definitionCN: 需要外国技术、零部件或专业能力的状况
senses.example: Dependence on imported chips slowed the factory's expansion.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口芯片的依赖拖慢了工厂的扩张。
senses.why: Supply chains are chains of hooks: each stage holds the next. When a link is foreign, the whole structure leans outward.
senses.whyCN: 供应链是一串钩子：每一环吊着下一环。当某一环在海外，整个结构就向外倾斜。

senses.title: Subordinate status
senses.titleCN: 从属地位：名义上自主，实际受管
senses.definition: the status of a territory or institution that is controlled by another
senses.definitionCN: 领地或机构受另一者控制的地位
senses.example: The report described the region's long dependence on the colonial administration.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了该地区对殖民当局的长期从属。
senses.why: Political dependence is the institutional version of hanging: the smaller unit has no independent footing and takes its orders from above.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的从属是悬挂的制度版：较小单位没有独立立足点，命令来自上方。

intro.en: Dependence goes back to Latin dependere, built from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'. The literal 'hang down from' became 'rely on' in Late Latin and French, and English borrowed the state noun in the 16th century.
intro.cn: dependence 可追到拉丁 dependere，由 de-“向下”和 pendere“悬挂”构成。字面的“挂在……下面”在晚期拉丁语和法语中变成“依靠”，英语在 16 世纪借入了这个状态名词。

items.en: pendere meant 'to hang, be suspended'. It also gave pendulum and pendant, both visibly hanging objects, so the physical image is present across the family.
items.cn: pendere 意为“悬挂、被吊起”。它还派生了 pendulum 和 pendant，两者都是明显悬挂的物体，因此整个词族都带着这个物理画面。

items.en: dependere adds de- 'down from', giving 'to hang down from, be attached to'. Classical Latin used it of things physically suspended from a point.
items.cn: dependere 加 de-“从……向下”，意为“挂在……下面、附着于”。古典拉丁语用它描述实际悬挂在某个点上的东西。

items.en: The step from 'hang from' to 'rely on' is metaphorical: whatever hangs from a support cannot stand without it. Late Latin and French extend the verb to persons and conditions.
items.cn: 从“悬挂于”到“依靠”的转变是隐喻性的：挂在支撑物上的东西离开支撑就站不住。晚期拉丁语和法语把这个动词扩展到人和处境。

items.en: Dependence enters English in the 16th century as the state noun of depend. The exact first date is uncertain because dependence and dependency competed in spelling and meaning.
items.cn: dependence 在 16 世纪作为 depend 的状态名词进入英语。由于 dependence 与 dependency 在拼写和意义上长期竞争，确切的最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 20th century, medicine standardized drug dependence for the physiological need for a substance, separating it from addiction as a broader behavioural term.
items.cn: 20 世纪，医学界用 drug dependence 固定指对某物质的生理需要，以便与范围更广的行为术语 addiction 区分。

items.en: Statistical dependence was named in the same period: variables that are not independent are said to depend on one another, keeping the anchor image.
items.cn: 统计学的“依赖性”也在同一时期得名：不独立的变量被说成彼此依赖，保留了锚点意象。

note.en: The look-alike group contains the same pend- family with different endings; the near-meaning group shares the idea of needing support but names different kinds of need.
note.cn: 形近组是同一 pend- 词族的不同词尾；近义组都含“需要支撑”的意思，但指的需要类型不同。

entries.definition: a state of reliance, a dependent territory, or a required software component. It overlaps with dependence but is more countable and more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖状态、属地，或软件依赖项。它与 dependence 重叠，但更可数、更技术化。

entries.definition: relying on another; also a person who is supported by someone else. It describes the one who hangs, not the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的；亦指受抚养人。它描述“悬挂者”，而不是关系本身。

entries.definition: reliable and trustworthy. The -able suffix shifts the meaning from 'needing support' to 'able to be relied on'.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的；可信赖的。-able 后缀把意义从“需要支撑”转成“可以被依靠”。

entries.definition: the state of depending on someone or something, often with trust; it stresses confidence more than structural necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的依赖，常带信任意味；它比结构性必需更强调信心。

entries.definition: a strong compulsive need for a substance or activity; broader and more behavioural than drug dependence.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物质或活动的强烈强迫性需要；比 drug dependence 范围更广，更偏行为层面。

entries.definition: mutual dependence between parties; it names the two-way version of the same hanging relation.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的相互依赖；它命名的是同一悬挂关系的双向版本。

entries.definition: the state of being lower in rank or under another's authority; it concerns power, while dependence concerns need.
entries.definitionCN: 地位较低或受他人管辖的状态；它关乎权力，而 dependence 关乎需要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + pendere 'hang': dependence is the state of hanging from a support.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”：dependence 就是挂在支撑物下面的状态。

normal.en: pendulum and pendant are visible cousins: they hang, and dependence names what hanging means for people.
normal.cn: pendulum 和 pendant 是看得见的同族词：它们都悬挂，而 dependence 命名“悬挂”对人意味着什么。

normal.en: The usual preposition is on, which matches the image: the lamp hangs on the hook.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 on，正好对应画面：灯挂在钩子上（hangs on the hook）。

normal.en: dependent is the adjective, dependence the state noun, dependency the countable or territorial noun; keep the endings apart.
normal.cn: dependent 是形容词，dependence 是状态名词，dependency 是可数或属地名词；词尾要分清。

normal.en: independence is the same image with the negative prefix: no hook, standing on its own.
normal.cn: independence 是同一画面加否定前缀：没有钩子，自己站住。

abstract.en: Think of a single nail holding a heavy picture frame: remove the nail and the frame falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子挂着沉重的画框：钉子一拔，画框就掉。

abstract.en: Think of a climber clipped to one rope: every move is safe only while the rope holds.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者只扣在一根绳上：只要绳子还牢，每个动作才安全。

abstract.en: Think of two drunks holding each other up: neither can walk alone, which is mutual dependence.
abstract.cn: 想象两个醉汉互相扶着走：谁也不能独自走，这就是相互依赖。

examples.en: Reducing dependence on imported oil became the government's main energy goal.
examples.cn: 减少对进口石油的依赖成了政府的主要能源目标。

examples.en: The doctor warned that dependence on sleeping pills can develop quickly.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，对安眠药的依赖可能很快形成。

examples.en: Their friendship rested on a healthy dependence rather than on control.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊建立在健康的依赖之上，而不是控制之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地喷den斯”——地上（de）喷出的喷泉（pen）全靠水泵撑着 → dependence 依赖、依靠

root: 拉丁 dependere“挂在……下面、依附”（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）；depend- 词干 + -ence 状态名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one geometry: something hangs from a support, and its ability to stay in place belongs to that support.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一套几何关系：某物挂在支撑上，它能否留在原位取决于那个支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight hanging from a single hook.
core.cn: 核心意象：重量挂在唯一一只钩子上。

branches.en: TWO HOOKS: mutual reliance is the same hanging relation drawn with two supports.
branches.cn: 两只钩子：相互依赖是同一悬挂关系画成双支撑。

branches.en: ECONOMIC AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT: an economy leaning on one export and a factory leaning on imported chips both hang outward.
branches.cn: 经济与技术支撑：依赖单一出口的经济体和依赖进口芯片的工厂，都向外悬挂。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: chemical dependence and emotional dependence attach normal functioning to a hook outside the self.
branches.cn: 身体与心理：药物依赖与情感依赖都把正常运转挂到自我之外的钩子上。

branches.en: STATISTICS AND POLITICS: a dependent variable and a dependent territory both take their position from a stronger anchor.
branches.cn: 统计与政治：因变量与属地都从更强的锚点那里取得自己的位置。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every extension keeps the original 'hanging' meaning and adds only the kind of support involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：每个引申都保留最初的“悬挂”含义，只增加所涉及的支撑类型。

intro.en: Dependence is depend plus -ence, a Latin-derived state suffix. Both de- and pendere are fossilized inside the base; English adds only -ence, and -ent or -ency for related forms.
intro.cn: dependence 是 depend 加 -ence（源自拉丁的状态后缀）。de- 与 pendere 都已凝固在词基内；英语只加 -ence，相关形式则用 -ent 或 -ency。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere 'to hang' yields pendulus 'hanging', dependere 'hang from', and the noun dependens. The stem pend- also appears in pendulum, pendant and suspend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pendere“悬挂”派生 pendulus“悬挂的”、dependere“挂在……下”以及名词 dependens。词干 pend- 也出现在 pendulum、pendant、suspend 中。

items.meaning: to hang from; to rely on
items.meaningCN: 悬挂于；依赖；取决于（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）
items.example: The harvest depends on how much rain falls in spring.
items.exampleCN: 收成取决于春季降雨量。

items.meaning: relying on another; supported by another
items.meaningCN: 依赖的；受抚养的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: A dependent child must be listed on the form.
items.exampleCN: 受抚养子女必须填在表格上。

items.meaning: the state of relying on something
items.meaningCN: 依赖；依靠（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Dependence on a single supplier is a business risk.
items.exampleCN: 依赖单一供应商是一种商业风险。

items.meaning: reliance; a dependent territory; a required component
items.meaningCN: 依赖；属地；依赖项（-ency 构成状态或事物名词）
items.example: The software update broke an old dependency.
items.exampleCN: 这次软件更新破坏了一个旧的依赖项。

items.example: The old generator is noisy but dependable.
items.exampleCN: 那台旧发电机很吵，但很可靠。

items.meaningCN: 可靠地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The bus arrives dependably at seven each morning.
items.exampleCN: 这趟公交每天早上七点准点到。

items.meaningCN: 独立的；不受支配的（in-“不”+ dependent）
items.example: The laboratory is independent of the manufacturer.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室独立于制造商。

items.example: Global trade rests on a web of interdependence.
items.exampleCN: 全球贸易建立在一张相互依赖的网上。

latinEntries.meaning: to hang down from; to be attached to

definition_zh: 经济扩张；产出与就业上升的阶段
definition_en: a period in which an economy's output, employment and spending are growing
core_image: 港口的吊机昼夜不停，新厂房沿公路一排排立起，招工的人守在车站出口
scene: 港口的吊机昼夜不停，新厂房沿公路一排排立起来，招工的人守在车站出口，连旧仓库也被租空。 Shipping records show a year of economic expansion along the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 economic expansion 指「产出、就业与支出都在增长的阶段」（第 1 个义项：经济体规模整体扩大的时期）；句意为航运记录显示沿海经历了一年的经济扩张。图中可辨识物件：昼夜运转的吊机、新建厂房、车站招工牌、租空的旧仓库。

pos.zh: 经济扩张；经济上行阶段

derivatives.zh: 扩张主义的 / 扩张主义者

senses.title: A period of growing output
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which an economy produces, employs and spends more than before
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体比此前生产更多、雇用更多、支出更多的时期
senses.example: Shipping records show a year of economic expansion along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 航运记录显示沿海经历了一年的经济扩张。
senses.why: Expansion is the noun of a Latin verb meaning 'to spread out', so the phrase pictures the economy opening outward in every direction at once.
senses.whyCN: expansion 是一个意为「展开」的拉丁动词的名词，因此这个短语把经济想象成同时向四面八方铺开。

senses.title: The upswing of the cycle
senses.definition: the rising phase of the business cycle, between one trough and the next peak
senses.definitionCN: 商业周期中上升的那一段，位于一个谷底与下一个峰顶之间
senses.example: The last economic expansion lasted almost a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 上一轮经济扩张持续了近十年。
senses.why: Once cycles are drawn as waves, the rising half needs a name, and expansion is the natural opposite of contraction.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把周期画成波浪，上升的一半就需要名字，而 expansion 正是 contraction 的自然对立面。

senses.title: A firm widening its scale
senses.definition: the growth of a company through new plants, markets or staff
senses.definitionCN: 企业通过新工厂、新市场或新员工实现的增长
senses.example: The mill's economic expansion added two shifts and a rail siding.
senses.exampleCN: 这家磨坊的规模扩张增加了两个班次和一条铁路侧线。
senses.why: The same verb describes anything spreading wider, so a single business can expand exactly as an economy does.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词可描述任何变宽的事物，因此单个企业的扩张与整个经济的扩张用的是同一个词。

senses.title: Territorial expansion
senses.definition: the extension of a state's territory or a people's settled area
senses.definitionCN: 国家领土或族群定居区域的向外延伸
senses.example: Railways drove the economic expansion of the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路推动了边疆地区的版图扩张。
senses.why: Physical spreading is the oldest sense of the root, and land is the most literal thing an economy can spread across.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的铺展是这个词根最古老的义项，而土地正是经济最字面地可以铺展开的对象。

senses.title: Expansion of demand
senses.definition: a rise in total spending by households, firms and government
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、企业与政府总支出上升
senses.example: Demand-led economic expansion pushed up imports.
senses.exampleCN: 需求带动的经济扩张推高了进口。
senses.why: Economists split the economy into sides, so expansion can be located on the demand side as well as in total output.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把经济分成几侧，因此扩张既可以说在总产出上，也可以说在需求一侧。

senses.title: Expansion of credit
senses.definition: a growth in lending and borrowing that lets spending outrun current income
senses.definitionCN: 借贷规模增长，使支出得以超过当期收入
senses.example: Cheap credit financed the economic expansion of those years.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷为那些年的经济扩张提供了资金。
senses.why: Credit is one of the channels through which an economy widens, and the phrase takes the channel as its qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 信贷是经济变宽的渠道之一，这个短语便把渠道拿来作限定语。

senses.title: Expansion of capacity
senses.definition: the building of more plant, equipment and infrastructure so that more can be produced later
senses.definitionCN: 兴建更多厂房、设备与基础设施，以便日后生产更多
senses.example: Capacity-led economic expansion takes years to show in output.
senses.exampleCN: 产能带动的经济扩张要多年才体现在产出上。
senses.why: Because widening the ability to produce precedes the increase itself, the phrase can point at investment rather than at results.
senses.whyCN: 由于生产能力的扩大先于增加本身，这个短语可以指向投资而非结果。

senses.title: Expansion of the money supply
senses.definition: an increase in the quantity of money circulating in an economy
senses.definitionCN: 经济体中流通的货币数量增加
senses.example: Monetary economic expansion showed up first in asset prices.
senses.exampleCN: 货币层面的经济扩张最先体现在资产价格上。
senses.why: The central bank can widen the money stock directly, and the phrase borrows the same image for that measure.
senses.whyCN: 央行可以直接把货币存量放宽，这个短语便为那项度量借用了同一个意象。

intro.en: Economic expansion joins economic, from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia, with expansion, from Latin expansio, built on expandere 'to spread out', from ex- 'out' and pandere 'to spread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic expansion 由 economic（出自希腊 oikonomia，经拉丁 oeconomia）与 expansion 组合而成；expansion 来自拉丁 expansio，由 expandere「展开」构成，即 ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pandere meant 'to spread out, to unfold', and stands behind expand, expanse and expansion.
items.cn: pandere 意为「铺展开、展开」，是 expand、expanse 与 expansion 的来源。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere gave expandere 'to spread out, to open wide'.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere 构成 expandere「铺展开、张开」。

items.en: The noun expansio named the act of spreading out and the space so opened.
items.cn: 名词 expansio 指铺展的动作，也指由此张开的空间。

items.en: English expansion is recorded from the seventeenth century, first for physical spreading and then for wider extension of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 expansion 自 17 世纪有记录，先指物理上的铺展，后指任何意义上的向外延伸。

items.en: The economic sense developed with the language of business cycles in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 经济义随 19 至 20 世纪的商业周期话语发展出来。

items.en: Expansion is not related to expend or expenditure, which come from expendere, built on pendere 'to weigh'; the two roots only sound alike.
items.cn: expansion 与 expend、expenditure 并无亲缘，后者来自 expendere，词根是 pendere「称重」；两个词根只是听起来相近。

note.en: The first group holds terms often swapped for this phrase, including one that merely looks related; the second holds words for things getting wider or busier.
note.cn: 第一组是常与本短语互换的说法，其中含一个只是看起来相关的词；第二组是「变宽、变热闹」的词。

entries.definition: The sustained rise in output over years; expansion is one phase within that trend, and can be shorter.
entries.definitionCN: 多年间产出的持续上升；expansion 是这一趋势中的一个阶段，可能更短。

entries.definition: Widening of any kind; the phrase economic expansion narrows it to the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 任何意义上的变宽；短语 economic expansion 把它收窄到经济。

entries.definition: From expendere, built on pendere 'to weigh': money spent, not space opened, and no relative of expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expendere，词根是 pendere「称重」：指花出去的钱，而非张开的空间，与 expansion 并非同族。

entries.definition: Means wide in extent or open in manner; it can describe a mood as easily as a territory.
entries.definitionCN: 指范围广阔或态度开朗；既能形容领土，也能形容心情。

entries.definition: The upward movement of a cycle; it is nearly the same as expansion in cycle talk.
entries.definitionCN: 周期的向上运动；在周期话语中与 expansion 几乎相同。

entries.definition: A rapid upturn, often with speculation; it implies more heat and a sharper end than expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速的上行，常带投机；比 expansion 更热，也更暗示陡然的结束。

entries.definition: A climb back toward an earlier level; expansion need not be recovering anything lost.
entries.definitionCN: 朝此前水平回升；expansion 并不一定是在收回失去的东西。

entries.definition: A literal word for something becoming broader, with no economic measurement attached.
entries.definitionCN: 字面表示某物变宽的词，不带经济度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus pandere 'spread': the economy spreads outward.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」：经济向外铺开。

normal.en: The family runs expand, expansion, expansive, expansionary, expansionist.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：expand、expansion、expansive、expansionary、expansionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rapid economic expansion, export-led expansion, expansionary policy.
normal.cn: 固定说法：快速经济扩张、出口带动的扩张、扩张性政策。

normal.en: Expansion is the mirror of contraction in cycle talk.
normal.cn: 在周期话语中，expansion 是 contraction 的镜像。

normal.en: Do not link it to expenditure: that root is pendere 'to weigh'.
normal.cn: 别把它和 expenditure 联系起来：那个词根是 pendere「称重」。

abstract.en: Picture cranes that never sleep and a road lined with new roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象吊机昼夜不停，公路两旁全是新屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose settled edge keeps moving outward.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有人定居的边缘不断向外移动。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon widening in every direction at once, not just upward.
abstract.cn: 想象气球同时向四面八方变宽，而不只是向上。

examples.en: Export-led economic expansion brought foreign earnings into the valley.
examples.cn: 出口带动的经济扩张把外汇收入带进谷地。

examples.en: The bank warned that credit-driven economic expansion rarely ends quietly.
examples.cn: 银行警告说，信贷驱动的经济扩张很少平静收场。

examples.en: Capacity-led economic expansion may take years to appear in the figures.
examples.cn: 产能带动的经济扩张可能要多年才体现在数字上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ expansion（向外铺开）」——整块经济往外摊开 → 经济扩张

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」（oikos 家 + nomos 管理），经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语；expansion 出自拉丁 expandere「展开」= ex-「向外」+ pandere「铺展」→ expansio；与 expendere（pendere 称重）无亲缘。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one widening: the economy spreads outward, and that spreading is read as a cycle phase, as a firm's growth, as new territory, as more demand, as more credit, as more capacity and finally as more money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「变宽」展开：经济向外铺开，这个铺开再依次被读作周期阶段、企业成长、新领土、更多需求、更多信贷、更多产能，最后是更多货币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes that never stop, a road lined with new roofs, and an old warehouse rented out.
core.cn: 核心意象：不停歇的吊机、两旁全是新屋顶的公路，以及被租空的旧仓库。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND CYCLE: the widening of the whole economy, and its place as the rising half of a wave.
branches.cn: 产出与周期：整个经济的变宽，以及它作为波浪上升的一半所处的位置。

branches.en: FIRM AND LAND: one business spreads wider, and a people pushes its settled edge outward.
branches.cn: 企业与土地：单个企业变宽，一个族群把定居边缘向外推。

branches.en: DEMAND AND CREDIT: spending and lending are two channels through which the widening runs.
branches.cn: 需求与信贷：支出与借贷是这种变宽流经的两条渠道。

branches.en: CAPACITY: the ability to produce is widened before the output arrives.
branches.cn: 产能：生产能力先在扩大，产出随后才到。

branches.en: MONEY: the central bank widens the stock of money itself.
branches.cn: 货币：央行直接把货币存量放宽。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective and a Latin noun; the noun can be read as a prefix, a verb root and a process suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个希腊来源的形容词与一个拉丁名词组合而成；名词部分可拆成前缀、动词词根与过程后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pandere 'to spread' gives expand, expanse, expansion and expansive; ex- adds the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pandere「铺展」衍生出 expand、expanse、expansion 与 expansive；ex- 增添「向外」的方向。

items.example: The prefix sends the spreading outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把铺展送向外面。

items.example: The root supplies the image of opening wide.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「张开」的意象。

items.example: The compound supplied the English verb expand.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式提供了英语动词 expand。

items.example: The Latin noun gave English expansion.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词给出英语 expansion。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The firm expanded into two new markets.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司扩张进入两个新市场。

items.example: The adjective marks policy that deliberately expands.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记有意扩张的政策。

items.example: The adjective describes extent or temperament.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述范围或性情。

definition_zh: n. 倾盆大雨；暴雨；（比喻）一阵倾泻
definition_en: a sudden heavy fall of rain, or a large amount of something arriving at once
core_image: 一片乌云把整桶水倒在街上，行人举着包挡头，屋檐挂下水帘；一个信箱被四面飞来的纸片塞满
scene: 乌云像被捅破的水桶，整条街瞬间挂起水帘，行人举着包挡在头顶。 A sudden downpour sent everyone running for the bus shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 downpour 是「倾盆大雨」（第 1 个义项：骤然降下的大雨）；句意是一场骤来的倾盆大雨让所有人跑向公交候车亭。图中可辨识物件：乌云、水帘、举起的包、候车亭。

pos.zh: 倾盆大雨；暴雨；（比喻）一阵倾泻

senses.title: Sudden heavy rain
senses.definition: a sudden heavy fall of rain
senses.definitionCN: （名词）骤然降下的大雨
senses.example: A sudden downpour sent everyone running for shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 一场骤来的倾盆大雨让所有人跑向避雨处。
senses.why: A cloud tipping a whole bucket of water onto a street.
senses.whyCN: 一片乌云把整桶水倒在街上。

senses.title: A soaking burst
senses.definition: a short burst of rain so heavy that it soaks everything at once
senses.definitionCN: （名词）短促却大到瞬间把一切浇透的一阵雨
senses.example: We were caught in a downpour and arrived soaked.
senses.exampleCN: 我们遇上暴雨，到时全身湿透。
senses.why: A curtain of water hanging from a roof edge while people hold bags over their heads.
senses.whyCN: 屋檐挂下一道水帘，人们把包举在头顶。

senses.title: A flood of things
senses.definition: a large amount of something arriving all at once
senses.definitionCN: （名词）大量事物同时涌来
senses.example: The speech brought a downpour of criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 那场演讲招来一阵铺天盖地的批评。
senses.why: A letterbox stuffed with papers flying in from every side.
senses.whyCN: 一个信箱被从四面飞来的纸片塞满。

intro.en: Downpour is down plus pour, rain poured down; the compound is first recorded in the 19th century and replaced older phrases such as a downfall of rain.
intro.cn: downpour 由 down 加 pour 组成，雨被倒下来；这个复合词最早见于 19 世纪，取代了 a downfall of rain 一类旧说法。

items.en: Old English dune means down or downward.
items.cn: 古英语 dune 意为向下。

items.en: Middle English pouren means to pour, of unknown origin.
items.cn: 中古英语 pouren 意为倒，来源不明。

items.en: English pour is used for liquid flowing out in a stream.
items.cn: 英语 pour 用于液体成股流出。

items.en: The compound downpour is recorded for a heavy fall of rain.
items.cn: 复合词 downpour 被记录下来，指大雨。

items.en: Downpour becomes the standard word in forecasts.
items.cn: downpour 成为天气预报中的标准用词。

items.en: The word is also used figuratively for a flood of things.
items.cn: 这个词也比喻大量事物涌来。

note.en: Downpour is rain poured down; its look-alikes share down or pour, and its neighbours name other kinds of wet weather.
note.cn: downpour 是被倒下来的雨；形近词共用 down 或 pour，近义词则是别的潮湿天气。

entries.definition: a loss of power, or in older use a heavy fall of rain
entries.definitionCN: 垮台；旧时也指大雨

entries.definition: to pour out, or a thing poured out
entries.definitionCN: 倒出；倒出之物

entries.definition: a flow moving downward
entries.definitionCN: 向下移动的水流

entries.definition: a very heavy fall of rain or a flood
entries.definitionCN: 暴雨；洪水

entries.definition: a sudden very heavy fall of rain
entries.definitionCN: 骤然降下的暴雨

entries.definition: a short period of rain
entries.definitionCN: 一阵短时的雨

normalIntro.en: Five pictures of water emptied all at once.
normalIntro.cn: 五个「水一次倒空」的画面。

normal.en: A cloud tipping a whole bucket of water onto a street.
normal.cn: 一片乌云把整桶水倒在街上。

normal.en: A curtain of water hanging from a roof edge while people hold bags over their heads.
normal.cn: 屋檐挂下一道水帘，人们把包举在头顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: downpour ＝ down（向下）＋ pour（倒、灌）＝「往下倒」。雨不是落下来而是被倒下来，所以是倾盆大雨。同族的 outpouring 是「倾泻、流露」；旧时英语说 a downfall of rain，19 世纪后 downpour 成了标准词。比喻用法 a downpour of criticism 是「铺天盖地的批评」。
