definition_zh: 风化（作用）；岩石在原地被雨、霜、风分解的过程；因长期暴露而造成的损耗
definition_en: the slow breakdown of rock or other material where it lies, caused by rain, frost, wind, sun and living things
core_image: 岩壁上一条细缝，夜里的雨水冻成冰楔，白天把碎石一点点撬下来
scene: 峡谷步道上，向导指着岩壁上一道被冰楔撑开的细缝，说这些碎石不是被洪水搬来的。 Salt and frost drive the slow weathering that opens these cracks.
sceneCN: 这里 weathering 指「岩石在原位被风化分解的过程」（第 1 个义项：岩石在原地被雨、冻、风分解而不被搬走）；句意为盐分与霜冻驱动缓慢的风化，把岩壁上的裂缝一点点撑开。图中可辨识物件：岩壁裂缝、冰楔、脚下碎屑堆、向导抬起的手。

pos.zh: 风化（作用）；暴露于风雨造成的损耗（不可数）
weather 的现在分词：经受住风雨或难关；使受日晒雨淋而变质

derivatives.zh: 被风雨磨蚀的；饱经风霜的

senses.title: Breakdown of rock in place
senses.definition: the process by which solid rock is broken into fragments where it lies, without being carried away
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬的岩石在原地碎成小块，碎屑没有被搬走
senses.example: Frost and rain begin the weathering that turns granite into loose grains.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻与雨水启动了把花岗岩变成松散颗粒的风化。
senses.why: the -ing noun names a process, and geology reserves it for decay in place, as opposed to erosion, which removes the debris.
senses.whyCN: 加 -ing 的名词表示一种过程，地质学专指原位分解，与把碎屑搬走的侵蚀相对。

senses.title: Chemical weathering
senses.definition: the breakdown of minerals by dissolution, oxidation or hydrolysis when water and air react with them
senses.definitionCN: 水与空气和矿物发生反应，通过溶解、氧化或水解使矿物分解
senses.example: Feldspar is lost first during chemical weathering, leaving clay behind.
senses.exampleCN: 化学风化中最先失去的是长石，剩下黏土。
senses.why: chemical agents do not split the rock mechanically; they change the minerals themselves, so the residue is a new material.
senses.whyCN: 化学营力不靠机械力劈开岩石，而是改变矿物本身，因此残余物已是新材料。

senses.title: Frost wedging
senses.definition: the splitting of rock when water in its cracks freezes, expands and forces the walls apart
senses.definitionCN: 裂缝中的水结冰膨胀，把两侧岩壁推开的撑裂过程
senses.example: Water in the joint expands at night, and frost weathering pries the block loose.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里裂缝中的水膨胀，冻融风化把这块岩石撬松。
senses.why: water expands as it freezes, so a crack that holds water is worked open year after year; this is the most familiar mechanical agent.
senses.whyCN: 水结冰时体积膨胀，因此蓄水的裂缝年复一年被撑开，这是最常见的机械风化方式。

senses.title: Biological weathering
senses.definition: the loosening and alteration of rock by roots, burrowing animals, lichens and their acids
senses.definitionCN: 根系、穴居动物、地衣及其酸性分泌物造成的岩石松动与改变
senses.example: Lichen crusts and wedging roots add biological weathering to the cliff face.
senses.exampleCN: 地衣结壳与楔入的根系在崖面上叠加生物风化。
senses.why: living things act both mechanically, by pushing rock apart, and chemically, by releasing acids that dissolve minerals.
senses.whyCN: 生物既靠机械力把岩石顶开，也靠分泌酸类溶解矿物，两种方式同时起作用。

senses.title: Accelerated weathering from pollution
senses.definition: the unusually fast decay of stone caused by acids and salts released by industry or traffic
senses.definitionCN: 工业或交通释放的酸与盐使石材异常迅速地损坏
senses.example: Sulfur in the air speeds up the weathering of limestone statues.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的硫使石灰岩雕像加速风化。
senses.why: the natural process is the same, but the rate changes: acid deposition supplies reactants far faster than clean rain does.
senses.whyCN: 过程本身没变，变的是速度：酸性沉降提供的反应物远多于洁净雨水。

senses.title: Weathering of building stone
senses.definition: the surface damage that stone, brick or mortar suffers through long exposure to the elements
senses.definitionCN: 石材、砖或灰浆因长期暴露于天气而受到的表面损伤
senses.example: The survey mapped weathering on the cathedral's south wall.
senses.exampleCN: 测绘记录了主教座堂南墙上的风化损伤。
senses.why: conservation uses the same technical noun for damage that has to be measured, mapped and slowed.
senses.whyCN: 文物保护沿用同一术语，指需要测量、绘图并加以减缓的损伤。

senses.title: Slow wearing down of anything
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何事物被时间慢慢磨薄
senses.definition: the gradual weakening of an institution, idea or relationship under prolonged pressure
senses.definitionCN: 制度、观念或关系在长期压力下逐渐被削弱
senses.example: Decades of compromise produced a slow weathering of the party's founding promises.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的妥协使该党最初的承诺被慢慢磨蚀。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the cliff: nothing strikes it, yet repeated small exposures change its outline.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借自崖壁：并无重击，只是反复的小小暴露改变了它的轮廓。

senses.title: A bone's weathering stage
senses.titleCN: 考古埋藏学中的骨骼风化等级
senses.definition: a graded measure of how long a bone has been exposed on the surface before burial, scored from the damage visible on it
senses.definitionCN: 依骨骼表面损伤评定其在埋藏前于地表暴露了多久的分级指标
senses.example: The bones were scored for weathering before the site was dated.
senses.exampleCN: 在给遗址定年之前，先对骨骼的风化等级做了评分。
senses.why: burial science turned the process noun into a countable diagnostic scale, so a skeleton can be read like a clock.
senses.whyCN: 埋藏学把这个过程名词变成可计数的诊断尺度，于是骨架可以像钟表一样被读取。

intro.en: Weathering is the gerund of the verb weather, which comes from Old English weder 'air, sky, storm'. The geological noun is a nineteenth-century extension of the older verb 'to expose to the weather'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: weathering 是动词 weather 的动名词，源自古英语 weder「空气、天空、风暴」。这个地质学名词是十九世纪从旧动词义「暴露于天气之中」扩展而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Weder meant 'air, sky, storm', and its deeper origin is not established; the Germanic form usually cited, *wedra-, is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: weder 意为「空气、天空、风暴」，其更深来源未得到证明；通常引用的日耳曼语形式 *wedra- 属重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: From the fifteenth century the verb weather meant to expose something to sun, rain and wind, and also to come through such exposure safely.
items.cn: 自十五世纪起，动词 weather 指让某物暴露于日晒、雨淋与风中，也指安全地经受住这种暴露。

items.en: In the nineteenth century geologists made the gerund a technical noun for the decay of rock in place, and set it against erosion.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学家把这个动名词变为专门名词，指岩石在原地的分解，并与侵蚀概念对举。

items.en: Twentieth-century work divided the process into mechanical, chemical and biological weathering, each with its own agents.
items.cn: 二十世纪的研究把这一过程分为机械风化、化学风化与生物风化，各有自己的营力。

items.en: Late twentieth-century taphonomy borrowed the word for graded bone damage, giving archaeologists a way to estimate surface exposure.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的埋藏学借这个词指分级的骨骼损伤，使考古学家可以估算地表暴露时间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no agreed pre-Germanic source for weder exists, and every older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：weder 在日耳曼语之前没有公认的来源，凡为其提供更早形式者均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look close to weathering but do not share its history; group two gathers processes that also break material down but by different means.
note.cn: 第一组列的是与 weathering 形近却不同源的词；第二组列的是同样使材料分解、但营力不同的过程词。

entries.definition: The base verb and noun of the same word stock: it names the exposure itself, while weathering names the resulting process.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词族的动词与名词：它指暴露本身，weathering 则指由此形成的过程。

entries.definition: From Old English wiþerian 'to become dry, shrivel'; the resemblance to weather is accidental, since it has no sense of sky or storm.
entries.definitionCN: 源自古英语 wiþerian「变干、枯萎」；与 weather 的相似只是偶然，它并无天空或风暴之义。

entries.definition: Also ends in -ing, but it means shrivelling or a crushing remark, never rock decay.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以 -ing 结尾，但指枯萎或令人难堪的言辞，与岩石分解无关。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: it describes the result, while weathering names the process that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词：它描写结果，weathering 指造成该结果的过程。

entries.definition: Weathering breaks rock where it lies; erosion then carries the loosened material away with water, wind or ice.
entries.definitionCN: 风化在原地把岩石打碎；侵蚀随后用水、风或冰把松动的物质搬走。

entries.definition: The chemical attack of metal or stone by acids and salts; it is one path within chemical weathering, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 酸与盐对金属或石材的化学侵蚀，是化学风化中的一条途径，不等于整个风化过程。

entries.definition: Wear caused by moving particles grinding a surface, a mechanical agent that works only where sediment is in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 运动颗粒磨擦表面造成的磨损，只在有沉积物移动处起作用，属机械营力。

entries.definition: A broad word for going bad, used of wood, food or stone; it adds no information about the agents involved.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指变坏的通用词，可用于木材、食物或石材，但不说明具体营力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English weder 'sky, storm' plus -ing: what the sky keeps doing to stone.
normal.cn: 古英语 weder「天空、风暴」加 -ing：天空对石头反复做的事。

normal.en: The family runs weather, weathered, weather-beaten, weatherproof, weatherability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 weather、weathered、weather-beaten、weatherproof、weatherability。

normal.en: Textbooks pair the word: weathering breaks rock, erosion carries it away.
normal.cn: 教材常成对使用：风化打碎岩石，侵蚀将其搬走。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: chemical, mechanical, frost weathering.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：化学风化、机械风化、冻融风化。

normal.en: The word is uncountable in its geological sense, so one says the weathering of the cliff, not a weathering.
normal.cn: 地质义不可数，应说崖壁的风化，而不说一个风化。

abstract.en: Picture a stone face losing a grain of dust each year until the features go soft.
abstract.cn: 想象一张石脸每年掉一粒尘，直到五官变圆钝。

abstract.en: Picture a letter left on a windowsill until the ink fades to grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信留在窗台上，字迹被晒褪成灰色。

abstract.en: Picture an old rule that nobody repeals but nobody obeys any more.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没人废除、却也无人再遵守的旧规矩。

examples.en: Weathering has smoothed the carved letters until they can barely be read.
examples.cn: 风化把刻字磨平，几乎读不出来了。

examples.en: In dry valleys, salt crystallization is the main agent of weathering.
examples.cn: 在干旱谷地，盐结晶是风化的主要营力。

examples.en: The report separates weathering damage from the cracks caused by traffic.
examples.cn: 报告把风化损伤与交通造成的裂缝分开处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「weather（天气）+ ing（过程）」——天气天天磨，石头慢慢散 → 风化

root: 古英语 weder「天空、风暴」+ 动名词后缀 -ing；weder 的更深来源不确定，常见日耳曼语 *wedra- 属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one physical story: exposure opens the rock, agents split it, and then the same image is measured, blamed on industry, applied to buildings and finally to institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条物理线索展开：暴露使岩石开口，营力把它分开；随后同一意象被用于计量、归咎于工业、用于建筑，最后用于制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff losing one grain at a time while the weather works on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖壁在天气反复作用下，一次掉下一粒碎屑。

branches.en: MECHANICAL SPLIT: water and ice open the joints before anything is carried off.
branches.cn: 机械撑裂：水与冰先把节理撑开，尚未搬走任何东西。

branches.en: LIVING AND CHEMICAL AGENTS: acids from air, water and lichens alter the minerals themselves.
branches.cn: 化学与生物营力：来自空气、水和地衣的酸改变矿物本身。

branches.en: HUMAN-ADDED WEAR: the same process, but faster and mapped on standing buildings.
branches.cn: 人为叠加的损耗：过程相同，只是更快，并被测绘在现存建筑上。

branches.en: MEASURED EXPOSURE: burial science turns the process into a countable grade.
branches.cn: 可计量的暴露：埋藏学把过程变成可计数的等级。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL METAPHOR: pressure that never strikes still changes the outline.
branches.cn: 制度的隐喻：从未重击的压力仍会改变轮廓。

intro.en: Weathering is a Germanic base plus a native suffix, so its parts are read as English morphemes rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: weathering 是日耳曼语词基加本族后缀构成，其成分应按英语语素而非拉丁语素来读。

latinIntro.en: The base weder has no reliable Latin cognate, so latinEntries is left empty rather than filled with a guessed form.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 weder 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此 latinEntries 留空，而不填入猜测形式。

items.example: The weather turned before we reached the col.
items.exampleCN: 我们还没到垭口，天气就变了。

items.example: The breaking of the rock took centuries.
items.exampleCN: 岩石的破碎历经数百年。

items.meaning: the process of being worn by exposure
items.meaningCN: 暴露于天气而被磨蚀的过程
items.example: Weathering widened the joint year by year.
items.exampleCN: 风化年复一年地把节理撑宽。

items.example: The weathered stone crumbled under the trowel.
items.exampleCN: 风化的石头在铲下碎成粉末。

items.example: A weather-beaten sign hung over the door.
items.exampleCN: 门上方挂着一块饱经风雨的旧招牌。

items.example: The case is weatherproof and floats.
items.exampleCN: 这箱子防风雨，还能浮起来。

items.example: Tests rank the stone by weatherability.
items.exampleCN: 试验按抗风化能力给石料排序。

items.example: They weatherized the windows before winter.
items.exampleCN: 入冬前他们给窗户做了耐候处理。

items.meaning: steel that forms a protective rust layer
items.example: The bridge uses weathering steel instead of paint.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥用耐候钢，不刷漆。

definition_zh: 神经的；神经系统的；神经元的；神经网络的
definition_en: relating to nerves or to the nervous system, especially to nerve cells and the signals they carry
core_image: 一张由细线与节点连成的网，信号沿线路一跳一跳地传过去
scene: 实验室里，研究员把电极贴上皮肤，屏幕上出现一串随动作起伏的波形： The neural signal rose sharply when the hand moved.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经的、与神经信号有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及神经或神经系统）；句意为手一动，神经信号便急剧上升。

pos.zh: 神经的；与神经或神经系统有关的
神经元的；神经网络式的

senses.title: Relating to nerves
senses.definition: concerning nerves or the signals that travel along them
senses.definitionCN: 关于神经或沿神经传导的信号的
senses.example: The neural signal rose sharply when the hand moved.
senses.exampleCN: 手一动，神经信号便急剧上升。
senses.why: The adjective points to the wiring itself, so anything it describes belongs to the pathway that carries sensation and command.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指向线路本身，因此它所描述的一切都属于传导感觉与指令的通路。

senses.title: Of the nervous system
senses.definition: belonging to the whole system of brain, spinal cord and nerves
senses.definitionCN: 属于由脑、脊髓与神经构成的整个系统
senses.example: Neural tissue is found from the brain down to the fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 从脑一直到指尖都能找到神经组织。
senses.why: Once the parts are seen as one network, the adjective can describe the network as a whole rather than a single cord.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把这些部分看作一个网络，这个形容词就能描述整个网络，而不只是单根索。

senses.title: Of nerve cells
senses.definition: relating to nerve cells and their connections with one another
senses.definitionCN: 与神经细胞及其相互连接有关的
senses.example: Neural connections form fastest in the first years of life.
senses.exampleCN: 神经连接在生命最初几年形成得最快。
senses.why: At the cellular scale the network is made of individual cells, so the same adjective drops to the level of the node.
senses.whyCN: 在细胞尺度上，网络由一个个细胞组成，因此同一个形容词落到节点的层面。

senses.title: Neural network in computing
senses.titleCN: 神经网络的（计算机领域）
senses.definition: describing a computing model built from layers of simple units loosely modelled on neurons
senses.definitionCN: 描述由多层简单单元构成、粗略模仿神经元的计算模型
senses.example: A neural network learned to recognise faces from thousands of images.
senses.exampleCN: 一个神经网络从数千张图像中学会了识别人脸。
senses.why: The machine borrows the name because its units pass signals to one another in layers, like cells in a living network.
senses.whyCN: 机器借用这个名称，是因为其单元像活体网络中的细胞一样分层传递信号。

senses.title: Neural signal and activity
senses.definition: the electrical and chemical events by which nerves carry information
senses.definitionCN: 神经携带信息所依靠的电事件与化学事件
senses.example: The recording showed neural activity rising before the word was spoken.
senses.exampleCN: 记录显示，在说岀这个词之前神经活动已经增强。
senses.why: The adjective names the medium rather than the message: what is recorded is the traffic, not its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名媒介而非消息：被记录的是流量，而不是它的意义。

senses.title: Neural development
senses.definition: relating to the growth and wiring of the nervous system before and after birth
senses.definitionCN: 与出生前后神经系统的生长与布线有关的
senses.example: Neural development depends on both genes and early experience.
senses.exampleCN: 神经发育既依赖基因，也依赖早期经历。
senses.why: Development is the process that builds the network, so the adjective marks the period when the wiring is laid down.
senses.whyCN: 发育是搭建网络的过程，因此这个形容词标记线路被铺下的那段时期。

senses.title: Embryological structures
senses.titleCN: 胚胎与解剖结构中的神经（如神经管、神经嵴）
senses.definition: naming embryonic or anatomical structures such as the neural tube and neural crest
senses.definitionCN: 命名神经管、神经嵴等胚胎或解剖结构
senses.example: The neural tube becomes the brain and spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 神经管发育成脑与脊髓。
senses.why: In anatomy the adjective is attached to structures that will become, or belong to, the nervous system.
senses.whyCN: 在解剖学中，这个形容词附着于将要成为神经系统或属于神经系统的结构。

senses.title: Neural basis of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 行为或功能的神经基础
senses.definition: the nerve-level mechanism offered as the explanation for a behaviour or ability
senses.definitionCN: 被用来解释某种行为或能力的神经层面机制
senses.example: Researchers look for the neural basis of memory in the hippocampus.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者在海马体中寻找记忆的神经基础。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks an explanatory level: the question is not what happens but which wiring makes it happen.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词标记一个解释层面：问题不是发生了什么，而是哪套线路使之发生。

intro.en: Neural is Greek neuron sinew or nerve plus the Latin-derived adjective ending -al. It became a standard term in nineteenth-century physiology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neural 由希腊 neuron「筋、神经」加拉丁系形容词词尾 -al 构成，在 19 世纪生理学中成为标准术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and Greek medical writers used it for the cords they believed carried feeling and movement.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋、索或神经，希腊医学作者用它指他们认为传导感觉与运动的索状结构。

items.en: Latin nervus meant sinew or cord and is the cognate of Greek neuron; Latin supplied nervous and nerve, while Greek supplied neural and neuron.
items.cn: 拉丁 nervus 意为筋或索，与希腊 neuron 同源；拉丁语提供 nervous 与 nerve，希腊语提供 neural 与 neuron。

items.en: The shared ancestor is reconstructed as a form based on sneu-, meaning sinew; the exact shape is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 共同祖词被重构为以 sneu- 为基础、意为「筋」的形式；确切形态属重构，并非有书证的词。

items.en: The ending -al came to English through Latin -alis and French -al, forming adjectives of relation such as neural and cranial.
items.cn: 词尾 -al 经拉丁 -alis 与法语 -al 进入英语，构成 neural、cranial 这类关系形容词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology needed a word for everything belonging to nerves, and neural filled the gap beside the older nervous.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学需要一个词来指一切属于神经的东西，neural 填补了旧词 nervous 旁边的空位。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of neural is not firmly dated, and the choice between neural and nervous in early texts was not systematic.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：neural 最早的英语书证没有确定年代，早期文献中 neural 与 nervous 的取舍并不系统。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close; the second holds adjectives from neighbouring levels of description.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词；第二组是来自邻近描述层面的形容词。

entries.definition: Taking no side in a dispute, or having no charge; it shares the ending but comes from Latin neuter, neither one nor the other.
entries.definitionCN: 在争端中不站边，或电中性；结尾相同，但来自拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」。

entries.definition: A single nerve cell; neural is the adjective of the whole network or of such cells.
entries.definitionCN: 单个神经细胞；neural 是整个网络或这类细胞的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves, and also meaning anxious; it comes from Latin nervus rather than Greek neuron.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的，也表示紧张不安；它来自拉丁 nervus 而非希腊 neuron。

entries.definition: The medical study of the nervous system; neural describes, neurology names the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究神经系统的医学学科；neural 作描述，neurology 命名学科。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to neurons as cells; neural is broader and can cover the whole network.
entries.definitionCN: 专门与作为细胞的神经元有关；neural 范围更广，可涵盖整个网络。

entries.definition: Relating to the junction where one neuron passes a signal to the next; it is narrower than neural.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经元传递信号的接头有关的；比 neural 更窄。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses and the incoming side of the nerves; neural can describe either direction.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官及神经传入侧有关的；neural 可描述任一方向。

entries.definition: Relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum; neural covers the whole system including the cord and nerves.
entries.definitionCN: 与脑、尤指大脑有关的；neural 涵盖包括脊髓与神经的整个系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real cord roots, the real suffix and the real computing metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的索状词根、真实的后缀与真实的计算比喻。

normal.en: Greek neuron and Latin nervus both meant cord or sinew, so neural and nervous are cousins from two languages.
normal.cn: 希腊 neuron 与拉丁 nervus 都意为索或筋，因此 neural 与 nervous 是来自两种语言的表亲。

normal.en: Neural is the adjective, neuron is the cell, neurology is the discipline.
normal.cn: neural 是形容词，neuron 是细胞，neurology 是学科。

normal.en: Neural network is both a biological web and a computing model that borrows its name.
normal.cn: neural network 既指生物网络，也指借用其名的计算模型。

normal.en: Neural tube and neural crest are fixed embryology terms for structures that become the nervous system.
normal.cn: neural tube 与 neural crest 是固定的胚胎学术语，指发育成神经系统的结构。

normal.en: The phrase neural basis marks the level of explanation, not the thing explained.
normal.cn: neural basis 这一说法标记解释层面，而非被解释的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a net laid over the whole body, every knot connected to every neighbour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满全身的网，每个结都与相邻的结相连。

abstract.en: Picture a signal that is only traffic: it has a route but no meaning until something reads it.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只是流量的信号：它有路线，但在被读取之前没有意义。

abstract.en: Picture a machine built of layers of switches, named after the body it imitates.
abstract.cn: 想象一台由层层开关构成的机器，以它所模仿的身体部位命名。

examples.en: Neural signals travel along the spinal cord within milliseconds.
examples.cn: 神经信号在几毫秒内沿脊髓传导。

examples.en: The team trained a neural network on ten years of weather data.
examples.cn: 团队用十年的天气数据训练了一个神经网络。

examples.en: Neural plasticity allows the brain to adjust after injury.
examples.cn: 神经可塑性使大脑在受伤后得以调整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛柔」（neural）——牛一样韧的细索在全身连成网 → 神经的

root: 希腊 neuron「筋、索、神经」+ 拉丁系形容词词尾 -alis/-al；希腊 neuron 与拉丁 nervus 同源，祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one reference point, the nerve pathway, and shift the scale: the wiring, the whole system, the cell, the computing model, the signal, development, embryology, and the level of explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一个参照点——神经通路，只改变尺度：线路、整个系统、细胞、计算模型、信号、发育、胚胎结构，以及解释层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net of threads and knots, each signal hopping from one knot to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由线与结组成的网，信号从一个结跳到下一个结。

branches.en: THE PATH AND THE WHOLE: one nerve thread, and the system it belongs to.
branches.cn: 通路与整体：一根神经线，以及它所隶属的系统。

branches.en: NODE AND TRAFFIC: the cell that fires, and the signal it sends.
branches.cn: 节点与流量：放电的细胞，以及它发出的信号。

branches.en: THE BORROWED NAME: a computing model made of layered units.
branches.cn: 借来的名称：由分层单元构成的计算模型。

branches.en: BUILDING THE NET: development before birth, and the embryonic structures that start it.
branches.cn: 搭建网络：出生前的发育，以及启动它的胚胎结构。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION LAYER: the wiring offered as the reason for a behaviour.
branches.cn: 解释层：用线路作为某种行为的原因。

intro.en: Neural is a Greek stem with a Latin adjective ending, which is why its relatives split between neuron and nerve.
intro.cn: neural 是希腊词干加拉丁形容词词尾，因此其同族词分成 neuron 与 nerve 两条线。

latinIntro.en: Greek neuron passed into Latin medical writing, and Latin nervus supplies the rival family nerve and nervous; New Latin added neuralis.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 neuron 进入拉丁医学写作，拉丁 nervus 提供另一支 nerve 与 nervous；新拉丁语又添 neuralis。

items.example: The word names both the cord and the cell.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指索，也指细胞。

items.example: The suffix builds adjectives of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Neural tissue runs through the spinal cord.
items.exampleCN: 神经组织贯穿脊髓。

items.example: Anatomical Latin used neuralis for nerve structures.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学拉丁语用 neuralis 指神经结构。

items.example: Each neuron has a body, an axon and dendrites.
items.exampleCN: 每个神经元都有胞体、轴突与树突。

items.example: Neurology became a clinical specialty in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 神经病学在 19 世纪成为临床专科。

items.example: Neuralgia can follow a viral infection.
items.exampleCN: 神经痛可能继发于病毒感染。

items.meaning: the embryonic structure that becomes brain and cord
items.meaningCN: 发育成脑与脊髓的胚胎结构
items.example: The neural tube closes in the first month.
items.exampleCN: 神经管在第一个月内闭合。

items.meaning: a connected set of neurons or of computing units
items.meaningCN: 相互连接的神经元或计算单元集合
items.example: The neural network was trained on labelled images.
items.exampleCN: 这个神经网络用带标签的图像训练。

latinEntries.structure: Greek neuron, used in Latin medical texts

definition_zh: 锻造：把金属加热后用锤击或压制使其成形；也指锻件、锻造行业，以及伪造、缔造等动名词用法
definition_en: the shaping of metal by hammering or pressing it while hot, together with forged parts, the trade, and the gerund uses of counterfeiting and building
core_image: 锻锤落下，烧红的钢坯被压扁拉长，表面的氧化皮像碎屑一样脱落
scene: 锻锤一下下落下，烧红的钢坯被压扁拉长，表面的氧化皮碎屑四处飞溅。 Forging aligns the grains of the steel and makes the shaft much stronger.
sceneCN: 这里指锻造工艺本身（第 1 个义项：加热后靠锤打或压制使金属成形）；句意为锻造使钢的晶粒排列一致，让这根轴强得多。

pos.zh: 锻造；锻造工艺（不可数）
一次锻打作业；一个火次（可数）
锻件（可数，复数形式指成批锻件）
锻造；伪造；缔造（原动词的现在分词与动名词）

derivatives.zh: forge（铁匠铺；锻造）+ -ing → 锻造活动的基础词，指整间作坊或单次动作
forge + -ed（分词形容词）→ 锻造的；伪造的，语义偏移为「经锤打成形或假冒制成」
forge + -er（施事）→ 伪造者；锻工，语义偏移为「做假文件的人」
forge + -ery（行为或产物）→ 伪造；伪作，语义偏移为「假冒的文件或艺术品」
die（模具）+ forging → 模锻，语义偏移为「金属在闭合模腔中成形」
forging + press（压机）→ 锻造压力机，语义偏移为「以巨大压力使热坯成形」

senses.title: The process
senses.titleCN: 锻造工艺：加热后锤打或压制成形
senses.definition: the process of shaping metal by hammering, pressing or stamping it while hot
senses.definitionCN: 在热态下靠锤击、压制或冲压使金属成形的过程
senses.example: Forging aligns the grains of the steel and makes the shaft much stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 锻造使钢的晶粒排列一致，让这根轴强得多。
senses.why: Hot metal deforms instead of cracking, and the deformation lines up the grain structure; that is why forging is valued for strength rather than only for shape.
senses.whyCN: 热金属变形而不开裂，变形又使晶粒结构排列一致；因此锻造的价值在强度，而不只在形状。

senses.title: One heat, one operation
senses.titleCN: 一个火次：一次锻打作业
senses.definition: a single heating of a workpiece and the hammering that follows before it cools
senses.definitionCN: 对工件的一次加热，以及随后在其冷却前完成的锤打
senses.example: The first forging brought the bar down to a square section.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个火次把铁条锻成了方截面。
senses.why: Metal can only be worked while it is above a certain temperature, so the craft is counted in heats rather than in hours.
senses.whyCN: 金属只有在高于某温度时才能加工，因此这门手艺按火次计数，而不是按小时计数。

senses.title: The forged part
senses.definition: a part that has been produced by forging, especially in the plural forgings
senses.definitionCN: 靠锻造制成的零件，复数形式尤指成批的锻件
senses.example: The order covers castings and forgings for the same engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这批订单包括同一台发动机的铸件与锻件。
senses.why: A count noun appears when the output is handled as stock: foundries ship castings, forges ship forgings.
senses.whyCN: 当产出被当作库存来处理时，就会出现可数名词：铸造厂发铸件，锻造厂发锻件。

senses.title: The shop and the trade
senses.definition: the workshop where forging is done, and the trade that carries it on
senses.definitionCN: 进行锻造的车间，以及从事这项工作的行当
senses.example: Forging moved to a new bay with two presses.
senses.exampleCN: 锻造搬进了一个有两台压机的新车间。
senses.why: The activity's name transfers to the place and to the occupation, because both are defined by the operation.
senses.whyCN: 活动的名称转移到场所与职业，因为两者都由这项操作来定义。

senses.title: Ways of forging
senses.titleCN: 锻造方法：自由锻、模锻与锻焊
senses.definition: the recognised methods of forging, such as open-die, closed-die and forge welding
senses.definitionCN: 被公认的锻造方法，如自由锻、闭式模锻与锻焊
senses.example: Die forging gives a near-final shape with little waste.
senses.exampleCN: 模锻能得到接近最终的形状，废料很少。
senses.why: Once forging becomes an industry, its variants need names: an open die lets the metal spread, a closed die forces it into a cavity.
senses.whyCN: 锻造一旦成为产业，各种变体就需要名称：自由锻让金属自由展宽，闭式模锻则把金属逼进模腔。

senses.title: Counterfeiting
senses.titleCN: 伪造：由锻造动词引申的动名词用法
senses.definition: the act of making a false copy of a document, signature or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 假冒文件、签名或有价物的行为
senses.example: The forging of the will was proved by the ink.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱是伪造的，这一点由墨迹得到证明。
senses.why: The gerund inherits the 'make a false thing' sense of the verb, so it names the act rather than the person or the object.
senses.whyCN: 动名词继承动词「制作假东西」的义项，因此它命名行为，而不是人或物件。

senses.title: Building something lasting
senses.definition: the act of creating or establishing a lasting link, alliance or career
senses.definitionCN: 创造或建立持久联系、联盟或事业的行为
senses.example: The forging of ties between the two ports took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两座港口之间联系的建立用了十年。
senses.why: Shaping metal into a durable object supplies the image for making anything meant to hold, so the gerund can name the building of bonds.
senses.whyCN: 把金属锻成耐久器物，为任何意在牢固的创造提供意象，因此动名词可以命名纽带的建立。

senses.title: A stage in production
senses.titleCN: 生产链中的一环：锻造、机加工、热处理
senses.definition: the forging stage considered as one link in a manufacturing sequence
senses.definitionCN: 作为制造序列中一环来看的锻造阶段
senses.example: The part goes from forging straight to heat treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个零件从锻造直接进入热处理。
senses.why: In a factory a craft becomes a step with an input and an output, so forging is scheduled between the billet and the finished part.
senses.whyCN: 在工厂里，手艺变成有输入与输出的一个步骤，因此锻造被排在钢坯与成品之间。

intro.en: Forging is the verbal noun of forge, a word that came from a Latin workshop term through French; its form is ordinary English, but it carries several centuries of sense development.
intro.cn: forging 是 forge 的动名词；forge 这个词语经法语来自拉丁语的作坊词。它的形态是普通英语，却承载了几个世纪的语义发展。

items.en: Fabrica meant a workshop or craft, and fabricare meant to make or build; the pair stands behind both forge and fabricate, which entered English by different routes.
items.cn: fabrica 指作坊或手艺，fabricare 指制作或建造；这一对词是 forge 与 fabricate 的共同背景，而两者经不同路线进入英语。

items.en: Old French forgier meant to hammer metal and also to make or invent; the second sense is the seed of both the 'create' and the 'counterfeit' meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 forgier 指锤打金属，也指制作或编造；第二个义项正是「缔造」与「伪造」两义的种子。

items.en: Middle English took forge as noun and verb. The smithy sense is earliest, and the -ing form appears as the ordinary verbal noun of the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语把 forge 既作名词也作动词。铁匠铺义最早，而带动名词词尾的形式作为该动词的常规动名词出现。

items.en: From 'make' come the senses of establishing an alliance and of making a false document; from 'hammer' comes the industrial sense of a shaping stage.
items.cn: 从「制作」生出缔结联盟与制作假文件两义；从「锤打」生出作为成形阶段的工业义。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century industry fixed the countable forgings for finished parts and the method names die forging, open-die forging and forge welding.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的工业固定了可数用法（成品锻件），以及模锻、自由锻、锻焊等方法名。

items.en: Dating and reconstruction: the dates of each sense are approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of faber is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 年代与重构：各义项的年代只是大致，faber 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the forms of the forge family; group two separates forging from the competing shaping processes.
note.cn: 第一组把 forge 词族的各种形式分开；第二组把锻造与竞争性的成形工艺分开。

entries.definition: The workshop, the hearth or the single act; forging names the activity or its output, not the place.
entries.definitionCN: 作坊、炉火或单次动作；forging 命名活动或产出，而不是场所。

entries.definition: Hammered into shape, or faked; it describes the object that resulted.
entries.definitionCN: 锤打成形的，或假冒的；它描述所得的物件。

entries.definition: The false document or artwork itself, or the crime of making it; forging is the act, forgery is the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 假冒的文件或艺术品本身，或制作它的罪行；forging 是行为，forgery 是物件。

entries.definition: The press that delivers the blows; it is equipment, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 施加压力的机器；它是设备，而不是过程。

entries.definition: Shaping metal by pouring it molten into a mould; forging works on solid metal and therefore gives different grain flow.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔融金属浇入铸型来成形；锻造加工固态金属，因此晶粒流向不同。

entries.definition: Pressing sheet metal into a shape with a die; it is a cold-forming cousin of forging, used on thin stock.
entries.definitionCN: 用模具把薄板压成形状；它是锻造的冷成形亲属，用于薄料。

entries.definition: Cutting metal to size with powered tools; forging moves material into shape instead of removing it.
entries.definitionCN: 用动力工具把金属切到尺寸；锻造是把材料移到所需形状，而不是去掉材料。

entries.definition: Hammering metal by hand at an anvil; forging also covers press work on an industrial scale.
entries.definitionCN: 在铁砧上手工锤打金属；forging 还涵盖工业规模的压制成形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin workshop pair, the countable output, and the real method names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的作坊词对、可数的产出，以及真实的方法名。

normal.en: forge + -ing: the process and its product, the same ending that turns casting into castings and smelting into a trade.
normal.cn: forge + -ing：过程与产物共用这一词尾，正如 casting 变 castings、smelting 变行业名。

normal.en: The countable output is forgings, just as the countable output of a foundry is castings.
normal.cn: 可数产出是 forgings，正如铸造厂的可数产出是 castings。

normal.en: The method names are real: open-die, closed-die, and forge welding.
normal.cn: 方法名都是真的：自由锻、闭式模锻、锻焊。

normal.en: The three figurative senses are all still alive: forging a link, forging a document, forging ahead.
normal.cn: 三个引申义至今都活着：建立联系、伪造文件、稳步推进。

normal.en: The strength comes from grain flow: hammering bends the grain lines to follow the shape instead of cutting them.
normal.cn: 强度来自晶粒流向：锤打让晶粒线顺着形状弯，而不是把它们切断。

abstract.en: Picture a bar being squeezed rather than carved, so nothing is lost and the grain is rearranged.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁条被挤压而不是被雕刻，因此没有材料损失，晶粒则被重新排列。

abstract.en: Picture a document and a blade made by the same motion of the hand, one honest and one not.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件与一把刀由同一手势做出，一个诚实，一个不诚实。

abstract.en: Picture a factory schedule where a craft becomes a slot between billet and finished part.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工厂排程，其中一门手艺变成钢坯与成品之间的一个格子。

examples.en: Forging produces a stronger shaft than cutting it from a solid block.
examples.cn: 锻造做出的轴，比从整块材料上切出来的更强。

examples.en: The plant orders forgings from three different suppliers.
examples.cn: 这家工厂从三家不同供应商订购锻件。

examples.en: The forging of the certificate was detected by the serial number.
examples.cn: 证书的伪造被序列号识破。

dict_mnemonic.text: forge（锻造）+ ing（过程/产物）＝ 锻造、锻件；记「热坯受压、晶粒顺形、废料极少」。

root: forge 来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」与 fabricare「制作」，经古法语 forge／forgier 进入英语；加 -ing 构成动名词，指锻造工艺及其产物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the hammer: the process, one heat, the forged part, the shop and trade, the method names, counterfeiting, building a bond, and a stage in production.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着锤子走：工艺本身、一个火次、锻件、车间与行业、方法名、伪造、建立纽带，以及生产链中的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a power hammer falls, the hot billet flattens and lengthens, and scale flies off the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：锻锤落下，热坯被压扁拉长，氧化皮从表面飞散。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: deformation under heat lines up the grain and raises strength.
branches.cn: 工艺本身：热态变形使晶粒排列一致，从而提高强度。

branches.en: THE UNIT AND THE SLOT: one heat counted as a working unit, and the stage scheduled in a factory.
branches.cn: 火次与工序格：一个火次作为作业单位，以及工厂排程中的一个阶段。

branches.en: THE OUTPUT AND THE PLACE: countable forgings shipped as stock, and the bay or trade that makes them.
branches.cn: 产出与场所：作为库存发运的可数锻件，以及制造它们的车间或行当。

branches.en: THE METHODS: open dies, closed dies and forge welding split the craft into named routes.
branches.cn: 方法层：自由锻、闭式模锻与锻焊把手艺分成有名目的路线。

branches.en: THE TWO GERUNDS: making a false document, and making a bond that is meant to last.
branches.cn: 两个动名词：制作假文件，以及建立意在持久的纽带。

intro.en: Forging is forge plus the ordinary -ing noun ending; the technical vocabulary adds method and equipment words rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: forging 是 forge 加普通的 -ing 名词词尾；技术词汇靠方法与设备词扩展，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin fabrica and fabricare stand behind the base word, and faber 'craftsman' behind them; the verbal noun itself is purely English in formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fabrica 与 fabricare 是基础词的来源，更早还有 faber「工匠」；动名词本身在构词上完全是英语的。

items.structure: forge (n., v.; from Old French, from Latin fabrica)
items.meaning: to hammer hot metal; the shop
items.example: They forge the ring in one heat.
items.exampleCN: 他们一个火次就把圆环锻好。

items.meaning: the process, or its countable product
items.example: The forgings are stacked by size.
items.exampleCN: 锻件按尺寸堆放。

items.meaningCN: 锤打成形的；也指假冒的
items.example: A forged shaft resists fatigue better.
items.exampleCN: 锻制的轴更耐疲劳。

items.example: The forger used an old typewriter.
items.exampleCN: 伪造者用了一台旧打字机。

items.meaning: the false object or the crime
items.example: The forgery passed as an original for years.
items.exampleCN: 这件伪作多年被当作原作。

items.example: Die forging holds tight tolerances.
items.exampleCN: 模锻能保持很紧的公差。

items.meaning: forging between flat or simple dies
items.meaningCN: 在平砧或简单砧面之间锻造
items.example: Open-die forging shapes the ingot first.
items.exampleCN: 自由锻先把钢锭锻出粗形。

items.meaning: the machine that delivers the pressure
items.example: The forging press is rated in tonnes.
items.exampleCN: 这台锻造压力机以吨位标定。

items.meaning: joining by hammering hot metal together
items.example: Forge welding leaves no filler metal.
items.exampleCN: 锻焊不留填充金属。

definition_zh: 数据处理；资料处理
definition_en: the systematic conversion of raw data into usable information by a defined procedure
core_image: 一筐杂乱的单据倒进机器，出来时变成整齐的汇总表
scene: 一筐杂乱的单据被倒进机器入口，出来时已变成整齐的汇总表，边角还盖着日期戳。 The office moved its data processing to a shared service so that bills were checked overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 data processing 指把原始数据按固定流程转换成可用信息的工作（第 1 个义项：把原始数据转成可用信息）；句意：办公室把数据处理移交给共享服务，账单因而能在一夜之间核对完毕。图中可辨识物件：单据筐、机器入口、汇总表、日期戳。

pos.zh: 数据处理；资料处理

senses.title: Turning raw data into information
senses.definition: the work of sorting, calculating and summarizing raw records so that they become useful
senses.definitionCN: 对原始记录进行排序、计算与汇总，使它们变得有用的工作
senses.example: Data processing turns a pile of receipts into a monthly total.
senses.exampleCN: 数据处理把一堆收据变成月度总额。
senses.why: the phrase names a transformation rather than a tool: raw records go in, usable information comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是一次转换而非一件工具：原料记录进去，可用信息出来。

senses.title: Processing done by computer
senses.definition: the same work carried out automatically by electronic machines
senses.definitionCN: 由电子机器自动完成的同一类工作
senses.example: Electronic data processing replaced rooms full of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 电子数据处理取代了成屋子的办事员。
senses.why: when machines took over the work, the phrase kept its meaning and gained an adjective rather than a new noun.
senses.whyCN: 机器接管这项工作后，短语保留原义，只加了一个形容词，而没有另造名词。

senses.title: Batch processing of transactions
senses.definition: collecting transactions and running them through the system in one scheduled pass
senses.definitionCN: 收集事务并在一次排定的运行中统一处理
senses.example: Payroll data processing runs as a batch every second Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 工资数据处理每隔一个周五成批运行一次。
senses.why: early machines were fastest when fed work in large blocks, and that style became a named sense of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 早期机器在大批喂入任务时最快，这种做法就成了短语的一个具名义项。

senses.title: Routine business processing
senses.definition: the regular handling of invoices, payroll, stock and accounts in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 组织中发票、工资、库存与账目的常规处理
senses.example: The accounts data processing team closes the books each month.
senses.exampleCN: 账务数据处理团队每月结账。
senses.why: business administration adopted the phrase for its recurring paperwork long before computers, and kept it afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 商务管理远在计算机之前就用这个短语指重复性的单据工作，此后一直沿用。

senses.title: Entry, validation and cleaning
senses.definition: the front-end work of keying data in, checking formats and removing errors
senses.definitionCN: 录入数据、检查格式并剔除错误的前端工作
senses.example: Most data processing errors come from the entry step, not the report.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数数据处理错误来自录入环节，而不是报表。
senses.why: before any calculation can be trusted, records must be made consistent, and that preparation belongs under the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在计算结果可信之前，记录必须先一致，这份准备工作也算在同一个短语之下。

senses.title: Scientific and statistical processing
senses.definition: the preparation and analysis of measurements from experiments or surveys
senses.definitionCN: 对实验或调查所得测量的整理与分析
senses.example: Satellite data processing removes noise before the images are studied.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星数据处理在图像被研究之前先去掉噪声。
senses.why: research produces raw measurements that must be corrected and summarized, which is the same transformation under another domain.
senses.whyCN: 研究产出的原始测量必须被校正与汇总，这是同一转换在另一个领域里的表现。

senses.title: Processing personal data under law
senses.definition: any operation performed on personal information, as defined by privacy law
senses.definitionCN: 隐私法所定义的、对个人信息进行的任何操作
senses.example: The contract sets out what data processing the supplier may perform.
senses.exampleCN: 合同列明供应商可进行哪些数据处理。
senses.why: privacy law needed a broad term covering collection, storage and deletion, and chose this everyday phrase.
senses.whyCN: 隐私法需要一个涵盖收集、存储与删除的宽泛术语，于是选用了这个日常短语。

senses.title: Manual and clerical processing
senses.definition: the same work done by hand, with files, ledgers and written rules
senses.definitionCN: 用档案、账簿与书面规则手工完成的同类工作
senses.example: Before the machines, data processing meant clerks and filing cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 在有机器之前，数据处理意味着办事员与档案柜。
senses.why: the phrase never required a computer, so it still describes paper-based work in small offices and archives.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从来不要求计算机，因此仍可描述小办公室与档案馆里的纸面工作。

intro.en: Data processing joins data, the plural of Latin datum, to processing, from Latin procedere by way of process. The phrase is twentieth-century, though the work is older. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: data processing 把拉丁语 datum 的复数 data 与出自拉丁语 procedere 的 processing 接在一起。短语是二十世纪的，但这项工作更老。年代均为约数。

items.en: Datum means something given, from dare, to give; the plural data entered English as a mass of facts to be handled.
items.cn: datum 意为「被给予的东西」，出自 dare「给予」；复数 data 以「待处理的大量事实」之意进入英语。

items.en: Procedere is pro-, forward, plus cedere, to go: to go forward, hence to advance a matter through stages.
items.cn: procedere 是 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」：向前走，引申为把事情分阶段推进。

items.en: Latin processus, a going forward, gave English process, which as a verb means to put material through a series of operations.
items.cn: 拉丁语 processus「前进」给出英语 process，作动词时指把材料送过一连串操作。

items.en: Data processing became common in the mid-twentieth century for the clerical and then electronic handling of records in offices.
items.cn: data processing 在二十世纪中期通行起来，先指办公室里的文书记录处理，后指电子处理。

items.en: Electronic data processing named a whole industry and a job title, and the phrase survived the move from punched cards to networks.
items.cn: 电子数据处理曾是一个行业与一个职位的名称，短语也从穿孔卡时代活到了网络时代。

items.en: The first half from Latin datum and the second from Latin procedere are both documented. The phrase's first use is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for cedere or dare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 datum，后半出自拉丁语 procedere，两段都有文献依据；短语最早使用的年代只有约数，cedere 与 dare 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the phrase's own parts and near forms; the second group names neighbouring activities that handle data.
note.cn: 第一组是短语自身的构件与近形；第二组是同样与数据打交道的相邻活动。

entries.definition: Putting material through a series of operations; alone it could refer to food or applications, not only data.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料送过一连串操作；单独用时也可指食品或申请，不只数据。

entries.definition: The one that performs the processing, whether a clerk, a service or a chip; the phrase names the work, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 执行处理的一方，可以是办事员、服务或芯片；短语指工作，不指执行者。

entries.definition: The raw records before any operation; processing is what makes them useful.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未经过任何操作的原始记录；处理才使它们有用。

entries.definition: The part of a computer that executes instructions; it is hardware, whereas data processing is the work done with it.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机中执行指令的部件；它是硬件，而数据处理是用它完成的工作。

entries.definition: Looking for patterns and meaning; processing prepares and transforms records, analysis asks what they show.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找模式与含义；processing 负责准备与转换记录，analysis 追问它们说明什么。

entries.definition: The single step of typing records into a system; it is one part of data processing, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把记录敲入系统的单一步骤；它是数据处理的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: A broader phrase covering any transformation of information, including by minds; data processing usually implies records and machines or clerks.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的短语，涵盖任何信息转换，包括由头脑完成；data processing 通常暗示记录与机器或办事员。

entries.definition: Working out results by arithmetic or logic; data processing includes sorting and formatting, which are not computation.
entries.definitionCN: 用算术或逻辑算出结果；数据处理还包括排序与排版，那些不算计算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real office history and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的办公史与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Data are the raw facts; processing is putting them through steps until they are useful.
normal.cn: data 是原始事实；processing 是让它们过一遍步骤直到有用。

normal.en: Procedere is pro- forward plus cedere go, so a process is a going forward through stages.
normal.cn: procedere 是 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」，所以 process 就是分阶段向前推进。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the office world: data processing system, data processing department, batch processing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出办公世界：数据处理系统、数据处理部门、批处理。

normal.en: The family runs data, process, processing, processor and data processor.
normal.cn: 同族词有 data、process、processing、processor 与 data processor。

normal.en: Privacy law uses the phrase for any operation on personal information, including deletion.
normal.cn: 隐私法用这个短语指对个人信息的任何操作，包括删除。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of receipts entering a machine and leaving as one clean total.
abstract.cn: 想象一筐收据进入机器，出来时成了一个干净的总数。

abstract.en: Picture a river of paper narrowing into a single tap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条纸的河流收窄成一个水龙头。

abstract.en: Picture clerks handing their ledgers to a humming box that never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象办事员把账簿交给一只嗡嗡作响、从不睡觉的盒子。

examples.en: The department handles data processing for every regional office.
examples.cn: 这个部门为所有地区办公室做数据处理。

examples.en: Good data processing catches a wrong date before it reaches the report.
examples.cn: 好的数据处理能在错误日期进入报表之前把它抓住。

examples.en: The contract limits how much personal data processing the vendor may do.
examples.cn: 合同限制了供应商可进行多少个人数据处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得（da）他（ta）＋剥（pro）塞（cess）ing」——把得到的数据一层层剥开塞进流程，就是数据处理

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ datum → 复数 data「数据」；拉丁 pro-「向前」+ cedere「走」→ procedere → processus → process「处理」；processing 为 process 的动名词，二者合为 data processing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one transformation from raw records to usable information, then branch into machine work, batch runs, office routine, entry work, research, legal definition and plain clerical handling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次转换展开：从原始记录到可用信息，再分叉到机器处理、成批运行、办公例行、录入工作、科研、法律定义与纯文书处理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of messy slips tipped into a machine and coming out as a clean summary sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一筐杂乱单据倒进机器，出来时是一张干净的汇总表。

branches.en: TRANSFORMATION: sorting, calculating and summarizing until records become information.
branches.cn: 转换：排序、计算与汇总，直到记录变成信息。

branches.en: MACHINE STYLE: the same work done by electronics, often in scheduled blocks.
branches.cn: 机器方式：同一工作由电子设备完成，常按排定的批次进行。

branches.en: OFFICE ROUTINE: invoices, payroll and accounts processed on a repeating cycle.
branches.cn: 办公例行：发票、工资与账目按循环周期处理。

branches.en: PREPARATION: entry, validation and cleaning come before any trusted result.
branches.cn: 准备：录入、校验与清洗先于任何可信结果。

branches.en: DOMAINS: science, privacy law and paper-based clerks all use the same phrase for their own handling of records.
branches.cn: 领域：科研、隐私法与纸面办事员都用同一个短语指各自对记录的处理。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-derived elements: data from dare through datum, and processing from procedere through process plus the English ending -ing.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源成分构成：data 出自 dare 经 datum，processing 出自 procedere 经 process 再加英语词尾 -ing。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives datum and procedere; the ending -ing that makes the second half a noun is English, added after process had already entered the language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出 datum 与 procedere；把后半变成名词的 -ing 是英语词尾，是在 process 已进入英语之后才加上去的。

items.example: Data are literally the given.
items.exampleCN: 数据字面上就是被给予的东西。

items.example: A datum is one recorded fact.
items.exampleCN: 一个数据点就是一条记录事实。

items.example: The plural now works as a mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数如今作不可数名词用。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement inside process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 process 里的「行进」意味。

items.example: A matter is advanced through stages.
items.exampleCN: 事情被分阶段向前推进。

items.example: The noun became English process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词成了英语 process。

items.example: The verb is the working core of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是短语的工作核心。

items.example: Processing names the activity rather than one run.
items.exampleCN: processing 指这项活动，而不是某一次运行。

items.example: The gerund can be uncountable.
items.exampleCN: 这个动名词可以不可数。

items.example: Processor names the machine or the person.
items.exampleCN: processor 指机器或人。

definition_zh: 沟；壕沟；战壕；海沟；挖沟
definition_en: a long, narrow, deep cut in the ground, a military ditch, or a deep depression on the ocean floor; also to dig such a cut
core_image: 地面被直直切出一条窄而深的槽，两侧的土堆成整齐的脊
scene: 工人在路面上开出一条窄槽，准备埋电缆。 Workers dug a narrow trench along the curb for the new cable.
sceneCN: 这里 trench 指「人工挖出的狭长沟槽」（第 1 个义项：为工程开挖的沟）；句意为工人们沿路缘挖出一条窄沟，用来埋新电缆。图中可辨识物件：路缘、窄沟、铁锹、电缆盘。

pos.zh: 沟；壕沟；战壕；海沟；沟状凹陷
在……挖沟；开槽；挖沟埋设

derivatives.zh: 尖锐的；有力的（同源但词义分化）

senses.title: A dug ditch
senses.definition: a long, narrow cut dug in the ground for drainage, cables or foundations
senses.definitionCN: 为排水、电缆或基础而在地面挖出的狭长深沟
senses.example: Workers dug a narrow trench along the curb for the new cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们沿路缘挖出一条窄沟，用来埋新电缆。
senses.why: trench goes back to Old French trenchier 'to cut', so the noun starts as the line left by a cutting action.
senses.whyCN: trench 上溯到古法语 trenchier「切」，因此这个名词最初就是切割动作留下的那条线。

senses.title: A military trench
senses.definition: a long defensive ditch from which soldiers fight and shelter
senses.definitionCN: 士兵据以作战与隐蔽的狭长防御沟
senses.example: The regiment held the trench through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团在战壕里守了一整个冬天。
senses.why: the military sense narrows the engineering sense to a ditch that protects bodies from fire.
senses.whyCN: 军事义把工程义收窄为一条保护身体免受火力的沟。

senses.title: A deep ocean trench
senses.definition: a long, narrow, very deep depression on the ocean floor
senses.definitionCN: 洋底上狭长而极深的凹陷
senses.example: The earthquake epicentre lay near a deep ocean trench.
senses.exampleCN: 震中位于一条深海沟附近。
senses.why: the ocean floor has cuts of the same narrow shape, so geology reused the word for them.
senses.whyCN: 洋底也有同样狭长形状的切口，因此地质学沿用了这个词。

senses.title: A geological trough
senses.definition: a long, narrow depression in rock or sediment formed by faulting or erosion
senses.definitionCN: 由断裂或侵蚀在岩石、沉积物中形成的狭长凹陷
senses.example: A fault trench runs across the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一条断层沟横穿谷底。
senses.why: the shape, not the digging, is what matters here: a natural cut in the ground is still a trench.
senses.whyCN: 这里重要的是形状而非挖掘：地面上的天然切口仍叫 trench。

senses.title: To dig a ditch
senses.definition: to dig a long, narrow cut in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在地面挖出狭长的沟
senses.example: They trenched the field to drain the low corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田里挖沟，为低洼的一角排水。
senses.why: the verb is simply the action that produces the noun, and English often pairs such nouns with a zero-derived verb.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是产生这个名词的动作，英语常让这类名词与零派生动词配对。

senses.title: To cut a trench through land
senses.titleCN: 动词：在土地上开槽穿过
senses.definition: to cut a trench across or through an area, as for a pipeline
senses.definitionCN: 为铺设管道等而在某区域横切出一条沟
senses.example: Crews trenched the hillside for the water main.
senses.exampleCN: 施工队在坡上开沟，铺设供水主管。
senses.why: with an object like field or hillside, the verb stresses the area crossed rather than the ditch itself.
senses.whyCN: 接 field 或 hillside 这类宾语时，动词强调的是被穿越的区域，而非沟本身。

senses.title: To open an excavation trench
senses.definition: to open a controlled excavation cut at an archaeological site
senses.definitionCN: 在考古遗址上开挖有控制的探沟
senses.example: The team trenched the mound in a grid pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 团队按网格在土丘上开挖探沟。
senses.why: archaeology adopted the engineering word for its own orderly cuts through layered ground.
senses.whyCN: 考古学借用了工程词，指它在层状地面上开出的有序切口。

senses.title: Archaic: to encroach
senses.definition: to encroach or infringe upon something, as in the old phrase trench upon
senses.definitionCN: 侵占或侵犯某物，见于旧短语 trench upon
senses.example: The old statute forbade anyone to trench upon the commons.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法令禁止任何人侵占公地。
senses.why: the image of cutting into another's ground produced an older legal sense of encroachment that survives only in archaic prose.
senses.whyCN: 切入他人土地的意象产生了较早的法律义「侵占」，今仅存于古旧文字。

intro.en: Trench comes from Old French trenche 'a cut, ditch', from trenchier 'to cut', a verb of uncertain deeper origin, sometimes linked to Latin truncare 'to cut off'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trench 来自古法语 trenche「切口、沟」，出自 trenchier「切」；这个动词更深的来源不确定，有人把它与拉丁 truncare「切掉」联系起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trenchier meant 'to cut, slice, carve'. Its relation to Latin truncare 'to cut off' is often proposed but not established beyond doubt.
items.cn: trenchier 意为「切、割、刻」。人们常提出它与拉丁 truncare「切掉」有关，但并未确凿证实。

items.en: The noun trenche named a cut or a ditch, and English borrowed it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 trenche 指切口或沟，英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: From the seventeenth century trench was used for siege and field fortifications, and the sense dominated after the trench warfare of 1914 to 1918.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，trench 用于攻城与野战工事；一九一四至一九一八年的堑壕战之后，这一义项占据主导。

items.en: Oceanography applied the word to deep linear depressions of the sea floor in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 海洋学在十九世纪末把这个词用于洋底狭长的深凹陷。

items.en: The verb meaning 'to dig a trench' developed alongside the noun; the archaic sense 'to encroach' is older and now rare.
items.cn: 意为「挖沟」的动词与名词并行发展；古旧的「侵占」义更早，今已罕见。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether trenchier descends from Latin truncare is disputed, and the exact first English date is not fixed, so any intermediate form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：trenchier 是否源自拉丁 truncare 尚有争议，英语最早书证的确切年代也未固定，凡给出的中间形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates trench from its own compounds and its sharp-edged relative trenchant; group two holds near synonyms for a long cut or channel.
note.cn: 第一组把 trench 与其复合词、以及同源但词义分化的 trenchant 分开；第二组是表示狭长切口或通道的近义词。

entries.definition: En- 'in' plus trench: to fix firmly, or to protect with a trench; it is a verb, not the ditch itself.
entries.definitionCN: en-「进入」加 trench：使牢固扎根，或用壕沟防护；它是动词，不指沟本身。

entries.definition: From the same Old French 'cutting' stock: sharp and forceful in speech or writing, not a physical ditch.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古法语「切」的词源：指言辞犀利有力，并非实体沟渠。

entries.definition: A belted raincoat named after the trenches of the First World War; it contains trench but names clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 得名于第一次世界大战战壕的束带雨衣；它虽含 trench，却指衣物。

entries.definition: War fought from opposing systems of trenches; it uses trench but names a kind of conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 从相互对峙的壕沟体系进行的战争；它虽含 trench，却指一种冲突形式。

entries.definition: A long narrow channel dug for drainage or irrigation; it is usually shallower and less military than a trench.
entries.definitionCN: 为排水或灌溉挖出的狭长渠道；通常比 trench 浅，也没有军事含义。

entries.definition: A passage for water, natural or built; it stresses flow rather than the cut itself.
entries.definitionCN: 天然或人工的水道；强调水流，而非切口本身。

entries.definition: A long narrow depression cut into a surface, often shallow and machined; a trench is deeper and in ground.
entries.definitionCN: 切在表面上的狭长凹槽，常较浅且为机加工；trench 更深且开在地面。

entries.definition: A narrow cut made by a plough in soil; it is agricultural and shallow, not a fortification.
entries.definitionCN: 犁在土里开出的狭沟；属农业用途且较浅，不是工事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trench- 'cut' + the noun ending: the cut itself.
normal.cn: trench-「切」+ 名词词尾：切出来的那道口子。

normal.en: The family runs trench, entrench, entrenchment, trenchant, trench coat.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 trench、entrench、entrenchment、trenchant、trench coat。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the military sense: trench warfare, trench coat, trench foot.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出军事义：堑壕战、风衣、战壕足。

normal.en: Geology says trench for the deep cut and trench for its two walls.
normal.cn: 地质学用 trench 指深切口，也指切口的两壁。

normal.en: The verb takes field or line as its object: trench a field, trench a line.
normal.cn: 这个动词常以 field 或 line 作宾语：在田里开沟、沿线开沟。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut once and left open, its layers exposed on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋糕被切了一刀后摊开，两边的层次都露出来。

abstract.en: Picture two gardens separated by a line no one is allowed to cross.
abstract.cn: 想象两座花园之间隔着一条谁也不许越过的线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that cuts cleanly through an argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话干净利落地切开一场争论。

examples.en: The workers filled the trench after laying the pipe.
examples.cn: 铺好管道后，工人把沟填了回去。

examples.en: Soldiers shared a narrow trench for three weeks.
examples.cn: 士兵们在一条窄战壕里共处了三周。

examples.en: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known ocean trench.
examples.cn: 马里亚纳海沟是已知最深的洋底海沟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trench（切）」——在地上切出一道窄口 → 沟、战壕、海沟

root: 古法语 trenche「切口、沟」来自 trenchier「切」；与拉丁 truncare「切掉」的联系常被提出但未确证，更深来源不确定，相关中间形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cut: a dug ditch, a military line, an ocean deep, a fault trough, three kinds of digging, and an archaic encroachment that survives in old prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条切口展开：挖出的沟、军事防线、海底深凹、断层沟、三种开挖动作，以及仅存于古旧文字的侵占义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single straight cut opening the ground into two walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道笔直的切口把地面分成两壁。

branches.en: CUT IN GROUND: a dug ditch and a natural fault trough share the shape.
branches.cn: 地面切口：人工沟与天然断层沟共享同一形状。

branches.en: DEFENSIVE LINE: the ditch becomes a place to fight from.
branches.cn: 防御线：沟变成据以作战的地方。

branches.en: OCEANIC CUT: the same narrow deep shape lies under the sea.
branches.cn: 海底切口：同样的狭长深形出现在海面之下。

branches.en: DIGGING ACTS: engineering, crossing land, archaeology.
branches.cn: 开挖动作：工程、穿越土地、考古。

branches.en: OLD INFRINGEMENT: cutting into another's ground became legal encroachment.
branches.cn: 旧日侵占：切入他人土地变成法律上的侵占。

intro.en: Trench is a borrowed French noun of cutting; its family includes the verb entrench, the adjective trenchant and two modern compounds.
intro.cn: trench 是借自法语的「切」名词；其词族包括动词 entrench、形容词 trenchant 与两个现代复合词。

latinIntro.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; a link to Latin truncare 'to cut off' is often proposed but not proven, so the Latin entries are given only as possible sources.
latinIntro.cn: 更深来源不确定；与拉丁 truncare「切掉」的联系常被提出却未证实，因此所给拉丁条目只能视为可能的来源。

items.example: The verb named the act of cutting into the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指切入地面的动作。

items.example: The trench was two metres deep.
items.exampleCN: 这条沟有两米深。

items.example: They trenched the whole field.
items.exampleCN: 他们给整块田开了沟。

items.meaning: to fix firmly; to fortify with trenches
items.meaningCN: 使牢固扎根；用壕沟防护
items.example: The habit was entrenched by years of use.
items.exampleCN: 这个习惯因多年使用而根深蒂固。

items.meaning: a fortified ditch; a fixed state
items.meaningCN: 壕沟工事；根深蒂固的状态
items.example: The entrenchment slowed the advance.
items.exampleCN: 壕沟工事拖慢了推进。

items.meaningCN: 切割的；引申为犀利有力的
items.example: Her trenchant criticism silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 她犀利的批评让全场安静。

items.meaning: a belted raincoat in military style
items.example: He wore a trench coat in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他雨天穿着一件风衣。

items.meaning: war fought from opposing trench systems
items.meaningCN: 以对峙壕沟体系进行的战争
items.example: Trench warfare defined the western front.
items.exampleCN: 堑壕战定义了西线战场。
