definition_zh: 哺乳动物（有毛发、用乳汁哺育幼崽的温血脊椎动物）
definition_en: a warm-blooded vertebrate with hair that feeds its young with milk
core_image: 洞穴深处，母兽侧躺，幼崽紧贴腹部吸奶，毛上还带着夜里的凉气
scene: 洞穴口，母兽侧躺，幼崽紧贴腹部吸奶，毛上还带着夜里的凉气。 The mammal nursed her young in the dark, her body warm against the cold ground.
sceneCN: 这里 mammal 指「哺乳动物」（第 1 个义项：有毛发、以乳汁哺育幼崽的温血脊椎动物）；句意为这只哺乳动物在黑暗中给幼崽喂奶，身体贴着冷地面仍保持温暖。

pos.zh: 哺乳动物

forms.label: 复合形容词（似哺乳类的）

senses.title: A member of the class Mammalia
senses.definition: a vertebrate that is warm-blooded, has hair or fur, and feeds its young with milk from mammary glands
senses.definitionCN: 温血、有毛发、用乳腺分泌的乳汁哺育幼崽的脊椎动物
senses.example: The mammal nursed her young in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 这只哺乳动物在黑暗中给幼崽喂奶。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin mamma 'breast', so the defining feature is the gland that makes milk.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁 mamma「乳房」之上，因此定义特征是产乳的腺体。

senses.title: The class as a whole
senses.definition: the mammals collectively, one class of vertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 所有哺乳动物的集合，是脊椎动物的一个纲
senses.example: Mammals appeared only after the dinosaurs had declined.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物直到恐龙衰落之后才兴盛起来。
senses.why: As a formal class, the plural often names a category in evolution rather than a group of individuals.
senses.whyCN: 作为一个正式纲，复数常指演化中的一个范畴，而不是一群个体。

senses.title: A marine mammal
senses.definition: a mammal that lives in the sea, such as a whale, seal or dolphin
senses.definitionCN: 生活在海中的哺乳动物，如鲸、海豹或海豚
senses.example: The bay is a nursery for marine mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个海湾是海洋哺乳动物的育幼场。
senses.why: The category crosses habitats, so 'marine' is added to keep the milk-and-hair definition while changing the setting.
senses.whyCN: 这一范畴跨越生境，因此加 marine 来保留「哺乳与毛发」的定义，同时改变场景。

senses.title: A conservation target
senses.definition: a mammal species or population managed to prevent decline or extinction
senses.definitionCN: 为防止数量下降或灭绝而加以管理的哺乳动物物种或种群
senses.example: Mammal conservation focuses on corridors between reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物保护的重点是保护区之间的走廊。
senses.why: Large, visible animals attract funding and legislation, so the class name became a policy unit.
senses.whyCN: 大型、可见的动物容易获得资金与立法关注，因此纲名成了政策单元。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: a mammal used in medical research, especially the mouse
senses.definitionCN: 用于医学研究的哺乳动物，尤指小鼠
senses.example: The mouse is the standard mammal in genetics labs.
senses.exampleCN: 小鼠是遗传学实验室里的标准哺乳动物。
senses.why: Because humans are mammals, a mammalian model lets researchers study diseases in a closely related body.
senses.whyCN: 因为人类也是哺乳动物，哺乳动物模型让研究者能在亲缘很近的身体中研究疾病。

senses.title: A fossil mammal
senses.definition: ancient mammal remains, especially teeth and jawbones used to trace diets
senses.definitionCN: 古代哺乳动物遗骸，尤指用于推断食性的牙齿与颌骨
senses.example: The fossil mammal had teeth for both plants and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 这只哺乳动物化石的牙齿既能吃植物也能吃肉。
senses.why: Mammal teeth preserve well and carry dietary information, which is why palaeontology relies on them.
senses.whyCN: 哺乳动物的牙齿易保存且携带食性信息，因此古生物学高度依赖它们。

senses.title: A vertebrate pest
senses.definition: a mammal that damages crops, stores or property, such as a rat
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物、仓储或财产的哺乳动物，如鼠
senses.example: The grain store was sealed against mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 粮仓被封住以防哺乳动物进入。
senses.why: Pest control separates mammal problems from insect problems, and the class name does that work.
senses.whyCN: 有害生物防治把哺乳动物问题与昆虫问题分开，纲名正好承担这一区分。

senses.title: A hunted game animal
senses.definition: a mammal hunted for meat, trophies or population control
senses.definitionCN: 为肉、战利品或控制数量而猎杀的哺乳动物
senses.example: The forest is managed for large game mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林按大型狩猎哺乳动物来管理。
senses.why: Hunting law uses the class name because quotas are set for deer, boar and other mammals together.
senses.whyCN: 狩猎法使用纲名，因为配额是给鹿、野猪等哺乳动物统一设定的。

intro.en: Mammal is built on Latin mamma 'breast' through Late Latin mammalis; Linnaeus fixed Mammalia as the class name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mammal 经晚期拉丁 mammalis 建立在拉丁 mamma「乳房」之上；林奈把 Mammalia 固定为纲名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mamma meant 'breast'. It is probably an expressive or nursery word, and its deeper origin is not established; any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mamma 意为「乳房」。它很可能是拟声或儿语词，更深来源未有定论；凡为它提出的印欧形式都属重构。

items.en: Mammalis meant 'of the breast', an adjective formed from mamma and used in anatomical writing.
items.cn: mammalis 意为「乳房的」，由 mamma 构成的形容词，用于解剖学文字。

items.en: Linnaeus used Mammalia as the class name for animals that suckle their young, placing the milk glands at the centre of the definition.
items.cn: 林奈用 Mammalia 作为哺育幼崽的动物纲名，把乳腺放在定义的核心。

items.en: English mammal appears in the 1820s through French mammifère, shortening the Latin plural Mammalia into a singular English noun.
items.cn: 英语 mammal 在 1820 年代经法语 mammifère 出现，把拉丁复数 Mammalia 缩成一个英语单数名词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science added mammalian for the adjective and mammalogy for the field, completing the English family.
items.cn: 19 世纪科学补上形容词 mammalian 与学科名 mammalogy，完成了英语词族。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): mamma's origin is probably expressive rather than derivable, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：mamma 的来源很可能是拟声性的，无法再往上推导，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same mamma stem; group two holds vertebrate categories that sit above, below or beside mammals.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 mamma 词干的词；第二组是位于哺乳动物之上、之下或旁边的脊椎动物范畴。

entries.definition: The breast or milk gland itself; the animal name was built on it, but the noun is not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 乳房或乳腺本身；动物名由它构成，但名词本身不是动物。

entries.definition: Relating to the milk glands, as in mammary gland; it describes a body part, not a class of animals.
entries.definitionCN: 与乳腺有关，如 mammary gland；它描述身体部位，而非动物纲。

entries.definition: The formal Latin class; Mammalia is the whole class, a mammal is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 正式拉丁纲名；Mammalia 是整个纲，mammal 是一个成员。

entries.definition: The study of mammals, built with -logy; it names a discipline rather than an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 研究哺乳动物的学科，由 -logy 构成；它指学科，不指动物。

entries.definition: Any animal with a backbone; mammals are one class within the vertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有脊柱的动物；哺乳动物是脊椎动物中的一个纲。

entries.definition: A mammal that carries its young in a pouch, such as a kangaroo; it is a subgroup of mammals.
entries.definitionCN: 把幼崽放在育儿袋里的哺乳动物，如袋鼠；它是哺乳动物的一个亚群。

entries.definition: A mammal whose young develop inside the womb attached to a placenta; another subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 幼崽在子宫内通过胎盘发育的哺乳动物；另一个亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Able to maintain a steady body temperature internally; mammals generally are, but so are birds.
entries.definitionCN: 能靠自身维持稳定体温；哺乳动物大多如此，但鸟类也如此。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mamma 'breast' + -al: the animal defined by its milk glands.
normal.cn: mamma「乳房」+ -al：以乳腺定义的那类动物。

normal.en: Mammal is singular; Mammalia is the class; mammalian is the adjective.
normal.cn: mammal 是单数个体；Mammalia 是纲；mammalian 是形容词。

normal.en: Whales and dolphins are marine mammals, not fish, because they breathe air and nurse their young.
normal.cn: 鲸与海豚是海洋哺乳动物，不是鱼，因为它们呼吸空气并哺育幼崽。

normal.en: Mammal-like is the phrase for extinct relatives that had some but not all mammal traits.
normal.cn: mammal-like 用来指已灭绝、只具备部分哺乳动物特征的近亲。

normal.en: Mammalogy is the field; mammalogist is the person.
normal.cn: mammalogy 是学科；mammalogist 是从业者。

abstract.en: Picture warmth passed from a mother's body to a blind newborn.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖从母体传给一只还看不见东西的幼崽。

abstract.en: Picture a whale that left the land but kept the milk.
abstract.cn: 想象一头离开了陆地却保留了哺乳方式的鲸。

abstract.en: Picture a fossil jaw whose teeth still tell what the animal ate.
abstract.cn: 想象一块化石颌骨，牙齿仍在说明那只动物吃什么。

examples.en: Mammals are the only animals that produce milk for their young.
examples.cn: 哺乳动物是唯一为幼崽产奶的动物。

examples.en: The survey found twelve mammal species in the valley.
examples.cn: 调查在山谷中发现十二种哺乳动物。

examples.en: Marine mammals surface to breathe every few minutes.
examples.cn: 海洋哺乳动物每隔几分钟浮出水面呼吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: mamma（妈妈）+ al——由妈妈喂奶养大的动物，就是哺乳动物；记「吃奶长大的」

root: 拉丁 mamma「乳房」→ 晚期拉丁 mammalis「乳房的」→ 林奈 Mammalia；mamma 的更深来源很可能是拟声词，无法再上推。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one milk-feeding animal through classification, evolution, oceans, conservation, laboratories, fossils, pest control and hunting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种喂奶的动物穿过分类、演化、海洋、保护、实验室、化石、有害生物防治与狩猎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mother's warm body against a newborn in a dark den.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗洞穴里，母兽温暖的身体贴着新生幼崽。

branches.en: DEFINITION: hair and milk define one animal and the whole class.
branches.cn: 定义：毛发与乳汁既定义一个动物，也定义整个纲。

branches.en: HABITAT: the same class enters the sea without ceasing to be mammals.
branches.cn: 生境：同一个纲进入海洋，却不因此不再是哺乳动物。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: protect it, control it, or hunt it under quota.
branches.cn: 管理：保护它、防治它，或在配额下猎取它。

branches.en: RESEARCH: because humans are mammals, a mouse can stand in for us.
branches.cn: 研究：因为人类也是哺乳动物，小鼠可以代替我们。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: fossil teeth record what ancient mammals ate.
branches.cn: 深时：化石牙齿记录着古代哺乳动物吃什么。

intro.en: Mammal is a Latin-derived noun built on mamma plus the adjective ending -al, shortened from the class name Mammalia.
intro.cn: mammal 是由拉丁 mamma 加形容词词尾 -al 构成的名词，从纲名 Mammalia 缩短而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin mamma 'breast' gives mammalis 'of the breast'; Linnaeus formed Mammalia from it, and English shortened that to mammal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mamma「乳房」衍生 mammalis「乳房的」；林奈据此造出 Mammalia，英语再缩短为 mammal。

items.example: The root supplies the milk-feeding image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「哺乳」的形象。

items.example: Mammalis means pertaining to the breast.
items.exampleCN: mammalis 意为与乳房有关的。

items.example: The mammal fed her cub.
items.exampleCN: 这只哺乳动物给幼崽喂奶。

items.example: Mammals colonised every continent.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物占据了每个大陆。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词。

items.example: The mammalian heart has four chambers.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的心脏有四个腔。

items.example: Mammalia is a class of vertebrates.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳纲是脊椎动物的一纲。

items.example: Mammalogy grew out of natural history.
items.exampleCN: 哺乳动物学从博物学中发展出来。

definition_zh: 青铜：以铜为主、加入锡等元素熔成的合金；也指它的颜色、青铜器物、铜牌以及染色与晒黑等引申义
definition_en: an alloy of copper with tin or another metal, and by extension its colour, objects made from it and a third-place medal
core_image: 铸范打开，一件青铜斧还带着余温，表面从亮金渐渐转为青灰
scene: 铸范打开，一件斧头还带着余温，表面由亮金渐渐转成青灰。 The bronze in the workshop was melted from copper and tin.
sceneCN: 这里指青铜这种合金（第 1 个义项：铜与锡等元素合成的金属材料）；句意为作坊里的青铜是由铜和锡熔炼而成的。

pos.zh: 青铜；青铜合金（不可数）
青铜色；古铜色（颜色）
青铜制品（总称，或可数指一件）
青铜制的；青铜色的
使呈青铜色；（皮肤）晒成古铜色

derivatives.zh: bronze + -ed（过去分词形容词）→ 呈青铜色的，语义偏移为「皮肤被晒成古铜色的」
bronze + -ing（动名词）→ 上青铜色；表面处理中的着色工序
bronze + -er（物）→ 修容粉，语义偏移为「让皮肤显古铜色的化妆品」
bronze + -y（形容词后缀）→ 青铜般的，语义偏移为「颜色或光泽近似青铜的」
bronze + colour + -ed → 青铜色的复合形容词

senses.title: The alloy
senses.titleCN: 青铜：铜与锡熔成的合金
senses.definition: a metal made mainly of copper with tin or another element added
senses.definitionCN: 以铜为主，掺入锡或其他元素制成的金属
senses.example: The bronze in the workshop was melted from copper and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊里的青铜是由铜和锡熔炼而成的。
senses.why: Copper alone is soft; adding tin makes it harder and easier to cast, and the resulting alloy takes a name of its own rather than staying a kind of copper.
senses.whyCN: 纯铜偏软；加入锡使它更硬也更好铸，于是这种合金得到了自己的名称，而不再只被当作铜的一种。

senses.title: The colour
senses.titleCN: 青铜色：从金黄到青灰的那一层颜色
senses.definition: the brownish or greenish-gold colour of bronze
senses.definitionCN: 青铜那种偏褐或偏青的金色
senses.example: The sky turned a deep bronze before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前，天空变成深青铜色。
senses.why: A metal's colour is one of its most memorable properties, so the material word serves directly as a colour name without any added suffix.
senses.whyCN: 金属的颜色是它最容易记住的性质之一，因此材料名可以直接充当颜色名，不必另加词尾。

senses.title: Bronzes as a class
senses.titleCN: 青铜器物：作为一类的青铜制品
senses.definition: objects made of bronze taken together as a group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类来看的青铜制品
senses.example: The museum's bronzes date from the late period.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的青铜器属于晚期。
senses.why: A material name often stands for what is made from it; a whole collection can be called by the metal, with the objects understood.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常常代替用它做成的东西；整整一批藏品可以用这种金属来称呼，器物本身则被默认。

senses.title: One cast piece
senses.titleCN: 一件青铜制品：可数用法
senses.definition: a single object, usually cast, made of bronze
senses.definitionCN: 单件青铜器物，通常为铸造而成
senses.example: A small bronze stood at the corner of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌角立着一件小型青铜器。
senses.why: Once the class sense exists, the same noun can count individual pieces, especially in gallery and auction language.
senses.whyCN: 类别义一旦成立，同一个名词就能数单件，在画廊与拍卖语言中尤其如此。

senses.title: Third place
senses.definition: a medal awarded for third place in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中授予第三名的奖牌
senses.example: She took bronze in the 400 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她在四百米比赛中获得铜牌。
senses.why: Medals are ranked by metal, and the third rank was assigned the cheapest of the three customary metals, so the material's name became the rank's name.
senses.whyCN: 奖牌按金属排等级，第三等被分给三种常用金属中最便宜的一种，于是材料名就成了名次名。

senses.title: Made of bronze
senses.definition: made of or relating to bronze
senses.definitionCN: 用青铜制成的，或与青铜有关的
senses.example: A bronze plate marked the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 入口处挂着一块青铜铭牌。
senses.why: English lets a material noun modify another noun without change of form, so the same word works as an adjective of substance.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许材料名词不加形态变化就修饰另一名词，因此同一个词可以直接充当表示材质的形容词。

senses.title: To bronze the skin
senses.definition: to give something, especially skin, a bronze colour
senses.definitionCN: 使某物（尤指皮肤）呈现青铜色
senses.example: They bronzed themselves on the roof all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在屋顶上把皮肤晒成古铜色。
senses.why: The colour sense turns into a verb: applying the metal's hue to a surface, whether by sun, lotion or plating, is expressed by the material's name.
senses.whyCN: 颜色义转为动词：把这种金属的色调加到某个表面上，不论靠太阳、乳液还是电镀，都用这种材料名来表达。

senses.title: Shorthand for the age
senses.definition: a short way of referring to the Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 对青铜时代的简称
senses.example: The site spans the late bronze into the early iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这处遗址从青铜时代晚期延续到铁器时代早期。
senses.why: Because the age is named after the metal, the metal alone can carry the period in running text, especially in archaeology.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个时代以这种金属命名，金属名本身就能在行文中代替那个时期，在考古文献中尤其如此。

intro.en: Bronze reached English through Italian and French. The medieval Latin word behind it has no settled origin, so the usual reference works offer competing suggestions rather than a proven source.
intro.cn: bronze 经意大利语与法语进入英语。它背后的中世纪拉丁词没有定论来源，因此常见词源资料给出的是并列的猜测，而非已证实的源头。

items.en: Italian bronzo named the alloy from the fourteenth century, and its form is the earliest well-attested link in the chain that leads to English.
items.cn: 意大利语 bronzo 自十四世纪起指这种合金，它的形态是通往英语这条链上最早的有力书证。

items.en: Medieval Latin bronzium is usually cited as the form behind the Italian word. Its own origin is uncertain: one suggestion ties it to the port of Brindisi, another to a Byzantine Greek term, and neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bronzium 常被引作意大利词背后的形式。它自身的来源不确定：一种猜测把它联系到布林迪西港，另一种联系到某个拜占庭希腊词，两种都未获证实。

items.en: French bronze appears in the sixteenth century and English borrowed it in the eighteenth. The same French form also gave English its spelling with the final silent e.
items.cn: 法语 bronze 出现于十六世纪，英语在十八世纪借入。同一个法语形式也让英语保留了词尾不发音的 e。

items.en: The colour sense follows the material directly. The medal sense grows with ranked competitions in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when third place was regularly marked in bronze.
items.cn: 颜色义直接跟随材料义。奖牌义随十九与二十世纪的名次赛制成长，第三名通常用青铜标记。

items.en: Source uncertain: no origin for bronzium is accepted, the earliest written dates are approximate, and the material itself was known in Europe long before any of these words were recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定：bronzium 没有任何公认来源，最早书证年代只是大致，而这种合金在欧洲被人使用的时间，远早于这些词被记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that are easily swapped for bronze; group two holds the metals and objects it is usually compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 bronze 互换的词；第二组是常与它比较的金属与物件。

entries.definition: Made of brass, and by extension shameless. It belongs to the brass family, not to bronze, and also means 'bold'.
entries.definitionCN: 黄铜制的，引申为厚颜无耻的。它属于黄铜一族而非青铜，另有「大胆的」之义。

entries.definition: Given a bronze colour, usually of skin. It is a form of the same word, not a different metal.
entries.definitionCN: 被染成青铜色的，通常指皮肤。它是同一个词的形式，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: A copper alloy with zinc, yellower and easier to machine; bronze is copper with tin, and the two are routinely confused.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与锌的合金，更黄也更好切削；青铜是铜与锡的合金，两者常被混淆。

entries.definition: The archaeological period named after the metal; the metal alone is a material, while the phrase names a stretch of time.
entries.definitionCN: 以这种金属命名的考古时期；单独的材料名指物质，而这个短语指一段时间。

entries.definition: The reddish metal that forms the main part of bronze; copper is an element, bronze is a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 构成青铜主体的红色金属；铜是元素，青铜是混合物。

entries.definition: Any metal deliberately mixed with another; bronze is one alloy among many.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有意把一种金属与另一种混合所得的金属；青铜只是众多合金中的一种。

entries.definition: The green or brown film that age gives a bronze surface; it is the metal's skin, not the metal.
entries.definitionCN: 岁月在青铜表面留下的绿或褐色薄膜；它是金属的表皮，而不是金属本身。

entries.definition: The object awarded for a place in a competition; bronze is only the grade of one such medal.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中按名次授予的物件；bronze 只是其中某一等级的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real metals involved, the real colour shift and the real medal ranking.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实涉及的金属、真实的颜色变化，以及真实的名次排列。

normal.en: Bronze is copper plus tin: the base metal gives the body, the added metal gives the hardness.
normal.cn: 青铜是铜加锡：基底金属提供主体，加入的金属提供硬度。

normal.en: The colour runs from gold to green as the surface oxidises, which is why old bronze looks nothing like new bronze.
normal.cn: 随着表面氧化，颜色从金黄走向青绿，所以旧青铜看起来与新青铜完全不同。

normal.en: The medal ladder is gold, silver, bronze; third place is the bronze rung.
normal.cn: 奖牌阶梯是金、银、铜；第三名就是青铜这一级。

normal.en: The family is regular: bronzed for the colour, bronzing for the process, bronzer for the cosmetic.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：bronzed 表颜色，bronzing 表工序，bronzer 表化妆品。

normal.en: The fixed phrases mark the uses: cast in bronze, bronze statue, bronze medal, bronzed skin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：青铜铸造、青铜像、铜牌、古铜色皮肤。

abstract.en: Picture a metal that changes colour as it ages, so time is visible on its skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一种会随年龄变色的金属，于是时间就写在它的表皮上。

abstract.en: Picture three metals stacked as a staircase, with the cheapest one holding up the third step.
abstract.cn: 想象三种金属叠成一道楼梯，最便宜的那一种托着第三级。

abstract.en: Picture a mould opening: the same metal is first liquid fire and then a cold grey tool.
abstract.cn: 想象铸范打开的一刻：同一种金属先是流动的火，随后成了冷灰的工具。

examples.en: The bell is cast in bronze and has rung for four centuries.
examples.cn: 这口钟以青铜铸成，已经敲了四百年。

examples.en: Collectors distinguish early bronzes by the shape of their handles.
examples.cn: 收藏者靠把手形状来区分早期青铜器。

examples.en: He finished third and brought home a bronze.
examples.cn: 他得了第三名，带回来一枚铜牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: bronze＝铜加锡的合金；记「金黄入范、青灰出范、第三名挂铜牌」。

root: 经意大利语 bronzo、法语 bronze 进入英语；其背后的中世纪拉丁 bronzium 来源不确定，常见猜测或联系布林迪西港，或联系某个拜占庭希腊词，均未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one metal: the alloy, its colour, its objects as a class, one such object, a third-place medal, the material as an adjective, the act of bronzing, and the age named after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一种金属向外辐射：合金本身、它的颜色、作为一类的器物、单件器物、铜牌、作定语的材质、晒成古铜色的动作，以及以它命名的时代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: copper and tin melt together, take a mould's shape, and slowly turn from gold to green-grey.
core.cn: 核心意象：铜与锡熔在一起，取得铸范的形状，再慢慢从金黄转为青灰。

branches.en: THE MIXTURE ITSELF: copper needs tin to become harder and castable.
branches.cn: 混合物本身：铜需要锡才能变得更硬、更好铸。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: the metal's hue becomes a colour word, then a verb for giving that hue.
branches.cn: 颜色：金属的色调成为颜色词，再成为赋予这种色调的动词。

branches.en: THE OBJECTS: a whole class of bronzes, and one countable piece in a gallery.
branches.cn: 器物：作为一整类的青铜器，以及画廊里可数的一件。

branches.en: THE RANK: third place wears the cheapest of the three medal metals.
branches.cn: 名次：第三名佩戴三种奖牌金属中最便宜的一种。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER AND THE PERIOD: material as adjective, skin bronzed by sun, and the age called by the metal's name.
branches.cn: 修饰与时期：作定语的材质、被太阳晒成古铜色的皮肤，以及用金属名命名的时代。

intro.en: Bronze is a borrowed noun that became a verb and an adjective without adding a prefix; its endings are all ordinary English ones.
intro.cn: bronze 是借来的名词，不加前缀就变成了动词与形容词；它接的词尾都是普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form behind the word, bronzium, is medieval and its origin is uncertain; Latin also had aes for copper or bronze, but that is a different word with a different history.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁形式 bronzium 属中世纪，来源不确定；拉丁语另有 aes 指铜或青铜，但那是另一个词，历史也不同。

items.structure: bronze (n., adj., v.; from Italian bronzo via French)
items.meaning: the alloy, its colour, and the act of giving that colour
items.meaningCN: 这种合金、它的颜色，以及赋予该颜色的动作
items.example: They bronze the fittings before assembly.
items.exampleCN: 他们在装配前给配件上青铜色。

items.example: Her arms were bronzed by the summer.
items.exampleCN: 她的手臂被夏天晒成了古铜色。

items.meaning: the process of colouring or plating
items.example: Bronzing is the last step before packing.

items.meaning: a cosmetic that gives a bronzed look
